# Bend Vulkan: checked native handles, explicit dispatch and allocation

## Usage (caller's view)

Import `src/vulkan.bend as Vk`; import pinned `Giulio2002/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W` for every Vulkan size and offset. These IO sketches abbreviate namespace qualification and show successful `Done`/`Some` branches. Every `Fail`/`None` branch instead runs root cleanup and reports the original error. `R<A>` means `Result<&1, &1, Error, A>`.

```text
# Discovery: retain each returned owner even when the result is Fail.
e <- IO.try(Entry, Entry.load())
(e, Done{i}) <- Entry.create_instance(e, InstanceCreateInfo.default("headless"))
(i, Done{physicals}) <- Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(i)
physical = application_selects_device(physicals)
(i, Done{families}) <- Instance.queue_family_properties(i, physical)
(i, Done{mem_props}) <- Instance.memory_properties(i, physical)
# Explicit configuration; family is application-selected from families.
(i, Done{d}) <- Instance.create_device(i, physical, DeviceCreateInfo.single_queue(family))
(d, Done{buffer}) <- Device.create_buffer(d, BufferCreateInfo.transfer(U64{4096, 0}))
(d, Done{requirements}) <- Device.buffer_memory_requirements(d, buffer)
Some{memory_type} = MemoryProperties.find_type(mem_props, requirements.memory_type_bits, HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT)
(d, Done{memory}) <- Device.allocate_memory(d, MemoryAllocateInfo{requirements.size, memory_type})
(d, Done{bound}) <- Device.bind_buffer_memory(d, buffer, memory, U64{0, 0})
# Actual Vulkan memory; assert readback == [0, 255, 17, 42].
(d, Done{mapping}) <- Device.map_memory(d, memory)
(d, Done{written}) <- Device.write_mapped(d, mapping, U64{0, 0}, [0, 255, 17, 42])
(d, Done{readback}) <- Device.read_mapped(d, mapping, U64{0, 0}, 4)
(d, Done{unmapped}) <- Device.unmap_memory(d, mapping)
(d, Done{destroyed}) <- Device.destroy_buffer(d, buffer)
(d, Done{freed}) <- Device.free_memory(d, memory)
cleanup_result <- Entry.close_tree(e)  # Also called after any intermediate failure.
```

Executable examples expand these patterns into small continuation functions, as Bend requires matching computed results through parameters. Keep the first application error while reporting cleanup failures separately. Do not use `IO.try` after acquiring resources: it exits before cleanup. A successful `close_tree` invalidates descendant tokens; drop their Bend values.

## Problem

Build an ash-shaped Linux native Vulkan 1.0 subset on Bend 2.0.37: distinct Entry/Instance/Device dispatch, ordinary configuration records, exact result codes, discovery and explicit buffer/memory operations. Bend has no extensible opaque foreign-handle ABI, and affine constructors can still be forged or dropped. Native lifetime and pointer validity therefore require checked registry records, rather than a fictitious foreign type or integer-to-pointer conversion.

## Shape

```text
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
type Entry is Type:          Entry{id: W.U64}
type Instance is Type:       Instance{id: W.U64}
type Device is Type:         Device{id: W.U64}
# Each following type is Data with one id:W.U64 field and its own constructor:
PhysicalDevice; Buffer; DeviceMemory; Mapping
type Error is Data:
  Vulkan{command: String, code_bits: U32}  # Exact int32_t VkResult bit pattern, including unknown codes.
  Host{operation: String, code: U32, message: String}
  InvalidHandle{kind: String}; InvalidArgument{field: String}; Unsupported{feature: String}
  ChildrenLive{kind: String}; EnumerationUnstable{command: String}
# Configuration/query records are Data; no C pointers or sType/pNext fields escape.
ApplicationInfo{application_name:String, application_version:U32, engine_name:String, engine_version:U32, api_version:U32}
InstanceCreateInfo{application:ApplicationInfo, layers:List<String>, extensions:List<String>}
QueueCreateInfo{family:U32, priorities:List<F32>}
DeviceCreateInfo{queues:List<QueueCreateInfo>, extensions:List<String>}
BufferCreateInfo{size:W.U64, usage:U32}  # Initially exclusive sharing, flags=0.
MemoryRequirements{size:W.U64, alignment:W.U64, memory_type_bits:U32}
MemoryAllocateInfo{allocation_size:W.U64, memory_type_index:U32}
PhysicalDeviceProperties; QueueFamilyProperties; MemoryProperties; MemoryType; MemoryHeap
MemoryProperties.find_type(props:MemoryProperties, type_bits:U32, required_flags:U32) -> Maybe<&2, U32>
def Entry.load() -> IO(Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Entry>):
  import "./native.c"
  import "./native.js"
Entry.create_instance(e:Entry, cfg:InstanceCreateInfo) -> IO(Entry & R<Instance>)
Entry.instance_layers/instance_extensions(e:Entry) -> IO(Entry & R<List<respective properties>>)
Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(i:Instance) -> IO(Instance & R<List<PhysicalDevice>>)
Instance.physical_device_properties/queue_family_properties/memory_properties(i:Instance, p:PhysicalDevice) -> IO(Instance & R<respective snapshot>)
Instance.create_device(i:Instance, p:PhysicalDevice, cfg:DeviceCreateInfo) -> IO(Instance & R<Device>)
Device.create_buffer/allocate_memory(d:Device, cfg:respective config) -> IO(Device & R<respective handle>)
Device.buffer_memory_requirements(d:Device, b:Buffer) -> IO(Device & R<MemoryRequirements>)
Device.bind_buffer_memory(d:Device, b:Buffer, m:DeviceMemory, offset:W.U64) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
Device.map_memory(d:Device, m:DeviceMemory) -> IO(Device & R<Mapping>)  # Whole allocation initially.
Device.write_mapped(d:Device, view:Mapping, offset:W.U64, bytes:List<U32>) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
Device.read_mapped(d:Device, view:Mapping, offset:W.U64, count:U32) -> IO(Device & R<List<U32>>)
Device.flush_mapped/invalidate_mapped/unmap_memory(d:Device, view:Mapping) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
Device.destroy_buffer/free_memory(d:Device, handle:respective handle) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
Device.wait_idle(d:Device) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
Device.destroy(d:Device) -> IO(Result<&1, &1, Error & Device, Unit>)
Instance.destroy/Entry.unload/Entry.close_tree(owner) -> IO(Result<&1, &1, Error & owner_type, Unit>)
```

The type block abbreviates separate declarations/signatures; it introduces no new Bend syntax. Device creation enables no optional feature bits initially. Query snapshots expose names, IDs, API version, queue flags/counts, memory flags/types/heaps and relevant limits with their correct widths. Caller code chooses devices, queue families and memory types; the wrapper hides loader dispatch, ABI layout and temporary storage. This is a small, deep interface per boundary-discipline, with explicit Vulkan allocation policy rather than a renderer framework.

Native records contain the real `Vk*` values and `PFN_vk*` tables. Entry loads `libvulkan.so.1` with `dlopen`, obtains `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, then global commands; Instance loads its commands through that function; Device loads its commands through `vkGetDeviceProcAddr`. Required missing symbols produce errors before publishing an owner. Native parent links keep the loader alive; ordinary parent destruction refuses live owned children. Physical-device records are borrowed and invalidated with their instance. [Dispatch reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetInstanceProcAddr.html).

Each constructor contains a registry ID `U64{slot,generation}`, never a pointer or raw Vulkan handle. Resolve slot bounds, generation, object kind, liveness and parent ownership before every native call; retire slots when generation would wrap. Registry records track buffer bindings and mappings, so wrong-device use, stale copies, freeing bound/mapped memory and double destruction return errors without reaching Vulkan. Affine dispatch owners reduce accidental misuse; they are not a security boundary or a destructor guarantee. This puts the invariant in one boundary, per encode-lessons-in-structure.

Marshal constructors using the runtime constructor ABI (`io_node(e,CID(K),a,b)`, `io_tup`, `io_done/io_fail`, `io_cstr`); register effects using the supplied `io_eff(CID(Entry.load),fn,0)` ABI, verified against emitted C. C imports are spliced into the program, so shared native code is included once and registrations are emitted only for reachable effects. Build typed C structs against `<vulkan/vulkan.h>`; initialize `sType`, `pNext=NULL`, counts and pointers there. Validate embedded NULs, queue bounds/priorities, list lengths, bind alignment/range/type compatibility, repeated binding, and allocation failures; free temporary strings/arrays on every branch. JS effects return a clear native-only error with the same result/state shape.

Use precisely upstream `W.U64{lo:U32,hi:U32}` for sizes, offsets, alignments and heap sizes. Reconstruct C values with `((uint64_t)hi << 32) | lo`; split both limbs on return. Implement unsigned lexicographic comparison where needed; upstream `le_signed` is unsuitable. Check ranges with subtraction after validating the start, and check `SIZE_MAX` before pointer arithmetic. Byte values must be 0..255. `count:U32` limits each copied chunk, not allocations or offsets; there is no fake 32-bit `VkDeviceSize`.

Mapping stores the returned pointer in its native registry record and exposes only checked byte copies relative to the mapping. Initially map the complete allocation; flush/invalidate the complete mapping with offset zero and `VK_WHOLE_SIZE`, avoiding partial noncoherent atom alignment policy. Copies are bounds checked and serialized; map/unmap state and HOST_VISIBLE are validated. The example selects coherent memory; noncoherent callers explicitly flush after host writes and invalidate only after the necessary synchronization. [Mapping reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory.html), [invalidation reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges.html).

Enumerations use count/query/retry on `VK_INCOMPLETE`, accepting only a complete snapshot, with bounded retries and overflow-checked native allocation. Failed creates roll back unpublished Vulkan objects and registry reservations. Explicit destroy checks dependencies; `close_tree` walks live records in dependency order: establish device idle, unmap, destroy buffers, free memory, destroy devices/instances, unload. If idle cannot be established and the error does not permit teardown, return the surviving Entry for retry. Partial cleanup updates records immediately, making retries safe; preserve the original operation error separately. Dropping a Bend value alone releases no native object.

Only the IO event loop mutates native records; no Vulkan calls enter Bend parallel evaluation or GPU `!` calls. Distinct Entry trees have separate owned state behind a small ID router. Collect discovery snapshots sequentially, then use balanced parallel calls for independent pure device scoring and payload generation. This satisfies parallelism without racing dispatch, mappings or cleanup.

## Modules and generated path

`src/vulkan.bend` exports the public surface; `src/vk/types.bend` holds records/errors/handle constructors; `src/vk/memory.bend` holds pure selection and checked-size helpers; `src/vk/native.c` owns loader, registry, marshalling and effects; `src/vk/native.js` implements explicit unsupported results. Calls cross at most public API → native bridge → Vulkan. Keep generated declarations in `src/vk/generated.bend` and dispatch metadata in `src/vk/generated.h`.

`tools/generate.py` reads pinned Khronos `vk.xml` plus `bindings.json` listing supported commands and ownership/marshalling annotations. Generate constants/result names, typed dispatch tables and Bend effect declarations; handwrite registry and supported struct marshalling. Reject an allowlisted command with an unsupported field shape rather than emitting placeholder wrappers. Check in generated output with registry revision/hash; `--check` detects drift. Header layouts remain C's responsibility. Add commands in verified vertical slices; this scales beyond a manually maintained command list without promising all Vulkan.

## Proofs and practical acceptance

`LAWS.bend` records pure invariants: both U64 limbs survive size conversions; unsigned ordering honors the high limb; selected memory types satisfy the bitmask/required-flags predicate; checked ranges reject overflow. `PROOF.bend` imports LAWS and supplies actual proofs. Keep this import graph free of native effects; state explicitly that proofs do not verify drivers, C marshalling or cleanup. Run `bend PROOF.bend` before committing, and never silence a failed law with `@unsafe`.

Native integration builds and runs a Bend executable that enumerates devices/families/memory, creates a logical device, creates and binds a buffer, writes/reads exact bytes, and explicitly cleans up. This proves real Vulkan host-memory integration, not GPU command execution. Use an available hardware ICD or Lavapipe; no loader/device is a clearly reported unavailable test, never a pass. Exercise unknown/stale/wrong-parent IDs, failed-create rollback, live-child refusal, bound/mapped free refusal, and callback U64 roundtrips above 2^32 without huge allocations. Run with validation layers when present and compare registry live counts before/after both successful and induced-failure paths.

## Tradeoffs accepted and alternatives considered

We accept checked Data resource IDs and copy-based mapped IO for a supported Bend ABI and controlled pointer lifetimes. We accept explicit destruction and native dependency checks because Bend affine values may be dropped. We accept a Vulkan 1.0 headless subset, whole-allocation maps and disabled optional features before adding shaders, command submission, synchronization, WSI, extension pNext chains or callbacks. glslangValidator becomes useful in a subsequent independently verified compute-submission slice.

Rejected: raw U64 Vulkan handles cast back to pointers exposes lifetime/forgery hazards and platform handle representation. Rejected: one `run_compute` facade hides so much configuration that it cannot support independent resource management or later ash-like growth. Rejected: fully linear parent/child typestate trees make every query and failed allocation rebuild an expanding ownership tuple; checked native relationships provide better interface depth within Bend's actual ABI. Ash's explicit dispatch and destruction remain the inspiration, not its Rust borrowing machinery. [Ash Entry reference](https://docs.rs/ash/latest/ash/struct.Entry.html).

## Open questions and next implementation step

Which optional core features and submission commands should the next vertical slice expose? Can installed runtime helper sources differ from the ABI emitted by Bend 2.0.37? Resolve the latter first with a tiny compiled constructor-return probe carrying a nonzero U64 high limb and the actual IO callback registration; inspect emitted C, then implement the registry-backed Entry/Instance discovery slice. Synthesis is reserved for the managing orchestrator; this candidate makes no repository edits.

Rejected: raw U64 Vulkan handles cast back to pointers exposes lifetime/forgery hazards and platform handle representation. Rejected: one `run_compute` facade hides so much configuration that it cannot support independent resource management or later ash-like growth. Rejected: fully linear parent/child typestate trees make every query and failed allocation rebuild an expanding ownership tuple; checked native relationships provide better interface depth within Bend's actual ABI. Ash's explicit dispatch and destruction remain the inspiration, not its Rust borrowing machinery. [Ash Entry reference](https://docs.rs/ash/latest/ash/struct.Entry.html).

## Open questions and next implementation step

Which optional core features and submission commands should the next vertical slice expose? Can installed runtime helper sources differ from the ABI emitted by Bend 2.0.37? Resolve the latter first with a tiny compiled constructor-return probe carrying a nonzero U64 high limb and the actual IO callback registration; inspect emitted C, then implement the registry-backed Entry/Instance discovery slice. Synthesis is reserved for the managing orchestrator; this candidate makes no repository edits.

Rubric 1 real Bend ABI compatibility 2 ash-like reusable explicit operations 3 lifetime/forgery/error cleanup rigor 4 small extensible API 5 verifiability and native integration, each 1..5. Parent prefers Data token handles with native validated registry, copy-based read/write (no exported mapped pointers), Entry.with cleanup. Discovery+buffers+one-shot GPU fill subset.  def VkResult(-A: Type) -> Type:
   Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>
+
+# A Result-returning IO monad: Fail skips the remaining actions, then Entry.with cleans up.
+def Action(-A: Type) -> Type:
+  IO(VkResult(A))
+
+def Action.pure(-A: Type, value: A) -> Action(A):
+  IO.pure(VkResult(A), Done{value})
+
+def Action.next(-A: Type, -B: Type, next: A -> Action(B), result: VkResult(A)) -> Action(B):
+  match result:
+    case Done{value}:
+      next(value)
+    case Fail{error}:

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > tests/native.bend <<'EOF'
import Base
import ../Vulkan.bend as V
import ../src/core.bend as Core
import ../src/constants.bend as vk
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo

def check_error(-A: Type, expected: U32, result: V.VkResult(A)) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match result:
    case Fail{(code, message)}:
      Demo.require(U32.is_eq(code, expected), "Wrong error code: " ++ U32.show(code) ++ " / " ++ message)
    case Done{value}:
      IO.pure(V.VkResult(Unit), Fail{(1, "Expected an error; operation succeeded")})

def expect_error(-A: Type, expected: U32, action: V.Action(A)) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do IO<V.VkResult(Unit)>:
    result : V.VkResult(A) <- action
    check_error(A, expected, result)

def check_words(words: U32 & U32, lo: U32, hi: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  (actual_lo, actual_hi) = words
  Demo.require(Bool.and(U32.is_eq(actual_lo, lo), U32.is_eq(actual_hi, hi)), "C U64 boundary lost a limb")

def check_u64() -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    zero : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(W.zero())
    check_words(zero, 0, 0)
    high : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(W.U64{0, 1})
    check_words(high, 0, 1)
    mixed : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(W.U64{2309737967, 19088743})
    check_words(mixed, 2309737967, 19088743)
    max : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(Core.whole_size())
    check_words(max, 4294967295, 4294967295)

def buffer_checks(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +buffer: V.Buffer, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(Unit):
  V.MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, bits} = requirements
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)
    index : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_memory_type(types, bits, 2), "No host-visible memory")
    +memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device, size, index)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.U64{0, 1}))
    V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.zero())
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.zero()))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.free_memory(device, memory))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy(device))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Instance.destroy(instance))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.Device.write_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), [256]))
    expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612739, V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.U64{0, 1}, 1))
    expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612739, V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, Core.whole_size(), 2))
    expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612741, V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 16777217))
    V.Device.write_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), [9, 8, 7, 6])
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 4)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes, [9, 8, 7, 6]), "Rejected writes altered memory")
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.CommandBuffer.end(command))
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.CommandBuffer.begin(command))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, W.of_u32(1), W.of_u32(4), 0))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, W.zero(), W.U64{0, 1}, 0))
    V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, W.zero(), Core.whole_size(), 707406378)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer))
    V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
    V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command))
    gpu : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 16)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(gpu, [42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42]), "GPU fill mismatch")
    V.Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.CommandBuffer.begin(command))
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer))
    V.Device.free_memory(device, memory)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.free_memory(device, memory))
    V.Device.destroy(device)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.wait_idle(device))
    V.Instance.destroy(instance)
    expect_error(V.PhysicalDeviceProperties, 1610612738, V.Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical))

def run_checks(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.wait_idle(V.Device{4294967295}))
    expect_error(V.Instance, 4294967289, V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo{"test", 4194304, [], ["VK_BEND_missing_extension"]}))
    expect_error(V.Instance, 1610612739, V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo{SCon{Chr{0}, SNil{}}, 4194304, [], []}))
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    before : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    again : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    after : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(before, after), "Repeated enumeration allocated duplicate handles")
    +other_instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    expect_error(V.PhysicalDeviceProperties, 1610612738, V.Instance.get_physical_device_properties(other_instance, physical))
    V.Instance.destroy(other_instance)
    expect_error(V.Device, 1610612739, V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{4294967295, []}))
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)
    +family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families, 1), "No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{family, []})
    +other : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{family, []})
    +foreign_buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(other, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(16), 2})
    expect_error(V.MemoryRequirements, 1610612738, V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, foreign_buffer))
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(other, foreign_buffer)
    V.Device.destroy(other)
    expect_error(V.Buffer, 1610612739, V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.zero(), 2}))
    +buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(16), vk.VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT()})
    requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)
    buffer_checks(instance, physical, device, buffer, requirements)

# Return a failure with an entire device tree still live: Entry.with must release it.
def abandon_buffer(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families, 1), "No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{family, []})
    buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(16), 2})
    pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)
    IO.pure(V.VkResult(Unit), Fail{(73, "intentional callback failure")})

def all_checks() -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    check_u64()
    V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => run_checks(entry))
    live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live, 0), "Success cleanup leaked native objects")
    expect_error(Unit, 73, V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => abandon_buffer(entry)))
    remaining : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(remaining, 0), "Failure cleanup leaked native objects")
    V.Action.lift(Unit, IO.print("Native Vulkan checks passed"))

def report(result: V.VkResult(Unit)) -> IO(Unit):
  match result:
    case Done{unit}:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case Fail{(code, message)}:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "Vulkan test failed (" ++ U32.show(code) ++ "): " ++ message)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- all_checks()
    report(result)
EOF

import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo

def check_error(-A: Type, expected: U32, result: V.VkResult(A)) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match result:
    case Fail{(code, message)}:
      Demo.require(U32.is_eq(code, expected), "Wrong error code: " ++ U32.show(code) ++ " / " ++ message)
    case Done{value}:
      IO.pure(V.VkResult(Unit), Fail{(1, "Expected an error; operation succeeded")})

def expect_error(-A: Type, expected: U32, action: V.Action(A)) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do IO<V.VkResult(Unit)>:
    result : V.VkResult(A) <- action
    check_error(A, expected, result)

def check_words(words: U32 & U32, lo: U32, hi: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  (actual_lo, actual_hi) = words
  Demo.require(Bool.and(U32.is_eq(actual_lo, lo), U32.is_eq(actual_hi, hi)), "C U64 boundary lost a limb")

def check_u64() -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    zero : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(W.zero())
    check_words(zero, 0, 0)
    high : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(W.U64{0, 1})
    check_words(high, 0, 1)
    mixed : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(W.U64{2309737967, 19088743})
    check_words(mixed, 2309737967, 19088743)
    max : U32 & U32 <- V.debug_u64_roundtrip(Core.whole_size())
    check_words(max, 4294967295, 4294967295)

def buffer_checks(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +buffer: V.Buffer, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(Unit):
  V.MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, bits} = requirements
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)
    index : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_memory_type(types, bits, 2), "No host-visible memory")
    +memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device, size, index)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.U64{0, 1}))
    V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.zero())
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.zero()))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.free_memory(device, memory))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy(device))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Instance.destroy(instance))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.Device.write_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), [256]))
    expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612739, V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.U64{0, 1}, 1))
    expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612739, V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, Core.whole_size(), 2))
    expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612741, V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 16777217))
    V.Device.write_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), [9, 8, 7, 6])
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 4)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes, [9, 8, 7, 6]), "Rejected writes altered memory")
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.CommandBuffer.end(command))
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.CommandBuffer.begin(command))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, W.of_u32(1), W.of_u32(4), 0))
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612739, V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, W.zero(), W.U64{0, 1}, 0))
    V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, W.zero(), Core.whole_size(), 707406378)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer))
    V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
    V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command))
    gpu : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 16)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(gpu, [42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42]), "GPU fill mismatch")
    V.Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.CommandBuffer.begin(command))
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer))
    V.Device.free_memory(device, memory)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.free_memory(device, memory))
    V.Device.destroy(device)
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.wait_idle(device))
    V.Instance.destroy(instance)
    expect_error(V.PhysicalDeviceProperties, 1610612738, V.Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical))

def run_checks(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    expect_error(Unit, 1610612738, V.Device.wait_idle(V.Device{4294967295}))
    expect_error(V.Instance, 4294967289, V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo{"test", 4194304, [], ["VK_BEND_missing_extension"]}))
    expect_error(V.Instance, 1610612739, V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo{SCon{Chr{0}, SNil{}}, 4194304, [], []}))
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    before : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    again : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    after : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(before, after), "Repeated enumeration allocated duplicate handles")
    +other_instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    expect_error(V.PhysicalDeviceProperties, 1610612738, V.Instance.get_physical_device_properties(other_instance, physical))
    V.Instance.destroy(other_instance)
    expect_error(V.Device, 1610612739, V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{4294967295, []}))
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)
    +family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families, 1), "No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{family, []})
    +other : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{family, []})
    +foreign_buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(other, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(16), 2})
    expect_error(V.MemoryRequirements, 1610612738, V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, foreign_buffer))
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(other, foreign_buffer)
    V.Device.destroy(other)
    expect_error(V.Buffer, 1610612739, V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.zero(), 2}))
    +buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(16), vk.VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT()})
    requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)
    buffer_checks(instance, physical, device, buffer, requirements)

# Return a failure with an entire device tree still live: Entry.with must release it.
def abandon_buffer(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry, V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families, 1), "No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance, physical, V.DeviceCreateInfo{family, []})
    buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(16), 2})
    pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)
    IO.pure(V.VkResult(Unit), Fail{(73, "intentional callback failure")})

def all_checks() -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    check_u64()
    V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => run_checks(entry))
    live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live, 0), "Success cleanup leaked native objects")
    expect_error(Unit, 73, V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => abandon_buffer(entry)))
    remaining : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(remaining, 0), "Failure cleanup leaked native objects")
    V.Action.lift(Unit, IO.print("Native Vulkan checks passed"))

def report(result: V.VkResult(Unit)) -> IO(Unit):
  match result:
    case Done{unit}:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case Fail{(code, message)}:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "Vulkan test failed (" ++ U32.show(code) ++ "): " ++ message)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- all_checks()
    report(result)
EOF
bend tests/native.bend -o /tmp/bend-vulkan-tests

---
name: technical-writing
description: "Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Technical writing

The goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.

Three rules sit above the layers:

- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.

The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.

Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.

## Vary the rhythm

The layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.

- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".

## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)

One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?

- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
- Action + work: **how-to**.
- Understanding + work: **reference**.
- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.

Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.

**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as "we", in commands: "First, do x. Now, do y."

**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: "If you want x, do y." Name the guide by the task: "How to calibrate the radar array", not "Radar array calibration".

**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.

**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.

Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.

## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)

- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete." The reader skips what does not apply.
- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.
- Don't pre-announce ("we will soon support...") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.
- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never "click here". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.
- Headings carry the point, not just the topic ("Pick the mode first", not "Modes"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase ("Create an instance"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.
- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.
- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop "etc." and say up front that a list is partial.

## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)

- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.
- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.
- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: "If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur."
- Keep "the" and "a": "Remove backup file" reads two ways. "Remove the backup file" reads one.
- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If "check" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.
- Pick one word per action and stick to it: "start", not "start" here and "initiate" there.
- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: "Install the component", not "the component must be installed".
- Avoid "-ing" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.

## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)

- Keep words like "only" and "not" next to the word they change: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth" say different things.
- Break up long noun strings: "the proto import budget check script" becomes "the script that checks the proto-import budget".
- Make every "it", "they", and "this" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use "this" or "which" to point at a whole clause.
- Don't drop verbs: "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.
- Keep the small words that show structure. "Ensure that the switch is off" keeps "that" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.
- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: "the client and the host", not "the client and host", when they are two things.
- Say which parts "and" or "or" joins when a sentence can group two ways. "Both...and", "either...or", and "if...then" are free disambiguators.
- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.
- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with "(s)".
- No slashes: write "a, b, or both" instead of "a/b" or "and/or".
- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says "the gate", "the ratchet", and "the budget check" for one thing teaches three things. Rewording an unchanged sentence between edits costs the same way. Don't churn what didn't change.
- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.

## Voice and repo specifics

- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.
- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.
- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.
- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.

## Worked example

Before:

> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.

After:

> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.

# Unslop

Edit text to remove AI patterns. Scan for the patterns below, then rewrite. Preserve meaning and match the intended tone.

## Patterns to detect and fix

Rule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.

### Content

3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.

### Language

7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Say "is" or "has".
9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
10. **Rule of three.** Don't force ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

### Style

13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example, not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
19. **Curly quotes.** Use straight quotes.

### Communication artifacts

20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

### Filler

23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". Delete "It is important to note that".
24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

### Jargon

26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate (base), wedge, wedge in (add), vector (way, method), locus, vantage, nexus, primitive as a noun, harness as a metaphor, surface as in "API surface", bedrock, scaffolding as a metaphor, modality, paradigm, gold-plating (more than the job needs), ratchet as a metaphor (the mechanism's real name, or a limit that only tightens), evacuate for moving code (move out), endgame (the last phase), north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. Pick the concrete word.

### Plain speech

27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.
30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number, and "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.
31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" and "leverage" become "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.
32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms ("wire it or delete it"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code ("the plan holds it"), figurative verbs ("rides along", "stands on"), stock framing phrases. "A dial worth turning" becomes "a parameter worth varying". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.
33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. "Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write" becomes "The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing." Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check generation and proofs, then build and run the public Vulkan examples."""
import argparse
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BUILD = ROOT / "build"


def run(*args, **kwargs):
    print("+", " ".join(map(str, args)), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=ROOT, check=True, **kwargs)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--sanitize", action="store_true", help="also run native checks under ASan and UBSan")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not (ROOT / "deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend").is_file():
        raise SystemExit("Initialize the pinned dependency: git submodule update --init --recursive")
    if not shutil.which("bend"):
        raise SystemExit("Bend 2.0.37 is required on PATH")
    run(sys.executable, "tools/generate.py", "--check")
    run("bend", "PROOF.bend")
    BUILD.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    # The interpreted backend must fail explicitly, with a well-formed Result.
    unsupported = subprocess.run(["bend", "examples/discover.bend"], cwd=ROOT,
                                 text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
    output = unsupported.stdout + unsupported.stderr
    if unsupported.returncode == 0 or "Vulkan error 1610612737: Vulkan requires a native build" not in output:
        raise SystemExit("JavaScript backend did not report the expected native-only error:\n" + output)
    for source, name, expected in (
        ("examples/discover.bend", "discover", "Loader API version bits:"),
        ("examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend", "buffer-roundtrip", "Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified"),
        ("tests/native.bend", "native-tests", "Native Vulkan checks passed"),
    ):
        binary = BUILD / name
        run("bend", source, "-o", str(binary))
        completed = run(str(binary), text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        print(completed.stdout, end="", flush=True)
        if completed.stderr:
            print(completed.stderr, end="", file=sys.stderr)
        if expected not in completed.stdout:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} omitted its success marker")
    if args.sanitize:
        generated = BUILD / "native-tests.c"
        binary = BUILD / "native-tests-sanitized"
        run("bend", "tests/native.bend", "-o", str(generated))
        run("clang", "-std=c11", "-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined",
            "-fno-omit-frame-pointer", str(generated), "-lpthread", "-lm", "-ldl", "-o", str(binary))
        env = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0", UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1")
        # Vulkan drivers may retain process-global allocations. The tests check our registry count.
        run(str(binary), env=env, timeout=60)
    print("Generation, proofs, and native Vulkan integration passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# bend-vulkan

A native Vulkan wrapper for Bend, inspired by [ash](https://github.com/ash-rs/ash).
The initial implementation provides explicit instance, device, buffer, memory, and command-buffer operations.
All Vulkan byte sizes, offsets, and alignments use the actual two-limb `U64` from [bend-collections](https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend-collections).

This is a Linux, headless Vulkan 1.0 subset. It can discover devices, allocate and bind buffers, copy host bytes, and submit a GPU buffer fill.
Graphics pipelines, compute shaders, images, descriptors, surfaces, swapchains, callbacks, and general `pNext` chains are not implemented.

## Run the buffer example

Install Bend **2.0.37**, Clang, Python 3, Vulkan development headers, `libvulkan.so.1`, and a Vulkan driver.
A hardware driver or a software ICD such as Lavapipe can provide the device.

# API reference

The public module is `Vulkan.bend`. Vulkan constants are zero-argument definitions in `src/constants.bend`, with their original `VK_` names.
`src/core.bend` provides API-version encoding, flag predicates, queue-family selection, memory-type selection, and U64 limb conversion.

Every native operation returns `IO(VkResult(A))`. `VkResult(A)` is `Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>`.
The `U32` in an error is the exact two's-complement bit pattern of a Vulkan `VkResult`, or a wrapper error from the table below.
The string names the failed operation or invalid input.

| Wrapper code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x60000001` | Loader unavailable or JavaScript backend unsupported |
| `0x60000002` | Unknown, stale, wrong-kind, or wrong-owner handle |
| `0x60000003` | Invalid argument or unsupported memory access range |
| `0x60000004` | Resource still referenced or invalid command state |
| `0x60000005` | Registry, allocation, enumeration, or copy limit |

`Entry.with` preserves the callback's failure code. If cleanup also fails, its diagnostic is appended to the message.
If cleanup alone fails, the scope returns that failure.

## Entry and instance operations

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Entry.load()` | A loader entry |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_version(entry)` | Loader API version, with a Vulkan 1.0 fallback |
| `Entry.create_instance(entry, info)` | An instance |
| `Entry.close(entry)` | Cascading resource teardown and library unload |
| `Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)` | A list of physical devices |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical)` | Name, API version, driver version, vendor ID, device ID, and type |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `(flags, queue_count)` pairs indexed by family |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `Core.MemoryType{property_flags, heap_index}` indexed by memory type |
| `Instance.create_device(instance, physical, info)` | A device with one queue at priority 1.0 |
| `Instance.destroy(instance)` | Instance teardown, rejecting live devices |

`InstanceCreateInfo{application_name, api_version, layers, extensions}` accepts explicit layer and extension names.
`InstanceCreateInfo.default()` requests Vulkan 1.0, with no layers or extensions.
`DeviceCreateInfo{queue_family_index, extensions}` selects one queue and enables no optional device features.
Strings containing NUL are rejected. Allocation callbacks are null.

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_buffer(device, BufferCreateInfo{size, usage})` | An exclusive, non-sparse buffer |
| `Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.allocate_memory(device, size, memory_type_index)` | An allocation |
| `Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, offset)` | A binding after size, alignment, type, and owner checks |
| `Device.write_memory(device, memory, offset, bytes)` | Checked host write, including flush for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.read_memory(device, memory, offset, count)` | Byte list, including invalidation for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)` | Buffer teardown |

| `Device.wait_idle(device)` | Device completion |

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |

| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | Record a transfer-write-to-host-read barrier, then end recording |

# Bend Vulkan dispatch and ownership

Bend 2.0.37 accepts custom IO effects but cannot extend its opaque host-handle types.
Ordinary constructors can cross the FFI, and callers can construct those values themselves.
The wrapper therefore keeps Vulkan pointers and dispatch tables in C and exposes checked identifiers in distinct Bend handle types.

## Caller's view

The allocation sequence remains explicit: create a buffer, query its requirements, select a compatible memory type, allocate memory, and bind it.
The public API also exposes command pools, command buffers, and submission.
`examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend` is the executable usage specification.
The `Action` monad propagates returned failures to `Entry.with`, which performs dependency-ordered cleanup.

## Native ownership

Each registry row has a kind, parent, and process-wide monotonic U32 key.
Keys never repeat, even after destruction or an unsuccessful operation. Exhausting the key space fails allocation.
These keys are registry identifiers, separate from Vulkan's native handle representation.
All Vulkan byte sizes and offsets use upstream `bend-collections` U64.

An Entry owns `dlopen` and global functions obtained through `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`.
An Instance owns instance functions obtained with its `VkInstance`.
A Device owns device functions obtained through `vkGetDeviceProcAddr`.
Parent rows outlive children. Buffer bindings and recorded command references add the dependencies required for destruction checks.
Physical-device rows are borrowed from their instance and interned across repeated enumeration.

All registry mutations and Vulkan effects run on Bend's IO event loop.
The initial submission API waits before returning. It introduces no shared writer across Bend parallel evaluation or helper threads.
Pure preparation can use Bend parallel calls. Dependent Vulkan state transitions remain sequenced through IO.

## FFI representation

The installed compiler emits packed constructors for single U32 handles and flattens the two limbs inside `BufferCreateInfo`.
The native boundary follows those emitted layouts rather than treating every constructor as a boxed object.
Imported constructor aliases cannot appear in this compiler's `CID` macros.
Native outputs that contain U64 values therefore cross as limb tuples, and pure Bend adapters reconstruct the dependency's actual U64.
No second U64 arithmetic implementation is present.

The effect ABI is internal to Bend. The native registrations use the two-argument `io_eff` emitted by Bend 2.0.37.
The integration tests exercise packed handles, the flattened buffer config, all U64 limbs, strings, lists, nested tuples, and result values.
Changing compiler versions requires rebuilding and rerunning those checks.

## Synthesis decision

Three independent designs compared affine owners, Data references, explicit mapped views, and temporary copy-based mapping.
All proposed native ownership checks. The selected base was candidate 3's Data references, entry scope, and copy-based mapping.
Candidate 2 contributed physical-device interning and strict stale-key errors. Candidate 1 contributed dependency-aware cleanup and completion checks.
An independent cross-judge also selected candidate 3 and approved monotonic U32 registry keys and the U64 limb adapter.

The implementation adds reusable command recording and synchronous GPU fill submission to the initial discovery and allocation subset.
The GPU example verifies driver execution, while `tests/native.bend` checks invalid inputs and successful and failed scope cleanup.

Raw pointer-valued handles would allow fabricated constructors to reach driver pointers.
Affine wrappers alone would still allow drops without native destruction and would require threading owners through every result.
Explicit mapped views would add pointer and cache lifetime states to the first API.
The chosen copy operations hide those states while preserving explicit Vulkan allocation choices.

The costs are registry lookup overhead, copied host byte lists, a synchronous queue, and a limited initial API.
Native handle adoption, full Vulkan registry generation, graphics, compute pipelines, and platform integration remain outside this implementation.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check generation and proofs, then build and run the public Vulkan examples."""
import argparse
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BUILD = ROOT / "build"


def run(*args, **kwargs):
    print("+", " ".join(map(str, args)), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=ROOT, check=True, **kwargs)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--sanitize", action="store_true", help="also run native checks under ASan and UBSan")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not (ROOT / "deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend").is_file():
        raise SystemExit("Initialize the pinned dependency: git submodule update --init --recursive")
    if not shutil.which("bend"):
        raise SystemExit("Bend 2.0.37 is required on PATH")
    run(sys.executable, "tools/generate.py", "--check")
    run("bend", "PROOF.bend")
    BUILD.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    # The interpreted backend must fail explicitly, with a well-formed Result.
    unsupported = subprocess.run(["bend", "examples/discover.bend"], cwd=ROOT,
                                 text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
    output = unsupported.stdout + unsupported.stderr
    if unsupported.returncode == 0 or "Vulkan error 1610612737: Vulkan requires a native build" not in output:
        raise SystemExit("JavaScript backend did not report the expected native-only error:\n" + output)
    for source, name, expected in (
        ("examples/discover.bend", "discover", "Loader API version bits:"),
        ("examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend", "buffer-roundtrip", "Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified"),
        ("tests/native.bend", "native-tests", "Native Vulkan checks passed"),
    ):
        binary = BUILD / name
        run("bend", source, "-o", str(binary))
        completed = run(str(binary), text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        print(completed.stdout, end="", flush=True)
        if completed.stderr:
            print(completed.stderr, end="", file=sys.stderr)
        if expected not in completed.stdout:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} omitted its success marker")
    if args.sanitize:
        generated = BUILD / "native-tests.c"
        binary = BUILD / "native-tests-sanitized"
        run("bend", "tests/native.bend", "-o", str(generated))
        run("clang", "-std=c11", "-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined",
            "-fno-omit-frame-pointer", str(generated), "-lpthread", "-lm", "-ldl", "-o", str(binary))
        env = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0", UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1")
        # Vulkan drivers may retain process-global allocations. The tests check our registry count.
        run(str(binary), env=env, timeout=60)
    print("Generation, proofs, and native Vulkan integration passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check generation and proofs, then build and run the public Vulkan examples."""
import argparse
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BUILD = ROOT / "build"


def run(*args, **kwargs):
    print("+", " ".join(map(str, args)), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=ROOT, check=True, **kwargs)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--sanitize", action="store_true", help="also run native checks under ASan and UBSan")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not (ROOT / "deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend").is_file():
        raise SystemExit("Initialize the pinned dependency: git submodule update --init --recursive")
    if not shutil.which("bend"):
        raise SystemExit("Bend 2.0.37 is required on PATH")
    run(sys.executable, "tools/generate.py", "--check")
    run("bend", "PROOF.bend")
    BUILD.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    # The interpreted backend must fail explicitly, with a well-formed Result.
    unsupported = subprocess.run(["bend", "examples/discover.bend"], cwd=ROOT,
                                 text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
    output = unsupported.stdout + unsupported.stderr
    if unsupported.returncode == 0 or "Vulkan error 1610612737: Vulkan requires a native build" not in output:
        raise SystemExit("JavaScript backend did not report the expected native-only error:\n" + output)
    for source, name, expected in (
        ("examples/discover.bend", "discover", "Loader API version bits:"),
        ("examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend", "buffer-roundtrip", "Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified"),
        ("tests/native.bend", "native-tests", "Native Vulkan checks passed"),
    ):
        binary = BUILD / name
        run("bend", source, "-o", str(binary))
        completed = run(str(binary), text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        print(completed.stdout, end="", flush=True)
        if completed.stderr:
            print(completed.stderr, end="", file=sys.stderr)
        if expected not in completed.stdout:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} omitted its success marker")
    if args.sanitize:
        generated = BUILD / "native-tests.c"
        binary = BUILD / "native-tests-sanitized"
        run("bend", "tests/native.bend", "-o", str(generated))
        run("clang", "-std=c11", "-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined",
            "-fno-omit-frame-pointer", str(generated), "-lpthread", "-lm", "-ldl", "-o", str(binary))
        env = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0", UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1")
        # Vulkan drivers may retain process-global allocations. The tests check our registry count.
        run(str(binary), env=env, timeout=60)
    print("Generation, proofs, and native Vulkan integration passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# bend-vulkan

A native Vulkan wrapper for Bend, inspired by [ash](https://github.com/ash-rs/ash).
The initial implementation provides explicit instance, device, buffer, memory, and command-buffer operations.
All Vulkan byte sizes, offsets, and alignments use the actual two-limb `U64` from [bend-collections](https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend-collections).

This is a Linux, headless Vulkan 1.0 subset. It can discover devices, allocate and bind buffers, copy host bytes, and submit a GPU buffer fill.
Graphics pipelines, compute shaders, images, descriptors, surfaces, swapchains, callbacks, and general `pNext` chains are not implemented.

## Run the buffer example

Install Bend **2.0.37**, Clang, Python 3, Vulkan development headers, `libvulkan.so.1`, and a Vulkan driver.
A hardware driver or a software ICD such as Lavapipe can provide the device.
The examples select a graphics queue for transfer commands.

Initialize the pinned dependency:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Build and run the native example:

```sh
mkdir -p build
bend examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend -o build/buffer-roundtrip
./build/buffer-roundtrip
```

Expected output:

```text
Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified
```

The example writes four bytes to Vulkan memory and checks their readback.
It then records `vkCmdFillBuffer`, submits the command buffer, waits for completion, and checks sixteen bytes against the value `42`.
To list devices, build and run `examples/discover.bend` the same way.

`bend example.bend` uses Bend's JavaScript backend. Vulkan effects report a native-build-required error in that backend.

## Use the API

Import `Vulkan.bend`, `src/core.bend`, `src/constants.bend`, and the dependency's `src/math/u64.bend` with paths relative to your program.
The executable [buffer example](examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend) shows the complete allocation and submission sequence.

`V.Action(A)` is `IO(V.VkResult(A))`. A `do V.Action<Unit>:` block propagates returned failures.
`V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => run(entry))` loads the Vulkan library, runs your callback, and closes its resource tree after either `Done` or `Fail`.
Use `V.or_exit(Unit, result)` at the application boundary to report the final result.
Calling `IO.die`, `IO.exit`, or `IO.try` inside a resource scope bypasses that cleanup callback.

Handle values are copyable with Bend's `+` annotations. Each handle kind has a distinct type.
Native code validates registry keys, object kinds, ownership, and liveness before it calls Vulkan.
Explicit destroy operations reject live dependents. `Entry.close` releases descendants in dependency order.
Dropping a Bend handle value does not destroy its Vulkan object.

See [the API reference](docs/api.md) for supported operations and [the design](docs/design.md) for the FFI and ownership decisions.

## Verify changes

Run the generator check, proof gate, native examples, and negative integration checks:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py
```

To include address and undefined-behavior sanitizers:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize
```

The native checks cover U64 high limbs, exact GPU readback, stale and wrong-owner keys, invalid byte values and ranges, destruction order, and cleanup after a failed callback.
A missing driver or device fails native verification. It is not a passing skip.
Bend's pure laws live in `LAWS.bend`; their proofs live in `PROOF.bend`.
Before committing, run `bend PROOF.bend`. For the additional proof-kernel check, run `bend PROOF.bend --verdict`.
The laws cover pure functions. They do not verify C code, Vulkan drivers, or GPU execution.

`tools/bindings.json` defines the supported effects. `tools/generate.py` generates their Bend declarations, native registrations, JavaScript errors, and selected core constants from the checked-in Khronos registry extract.
Run `python3 tools/generate.py` after changing the manifest. The generator does not implement new native commands or translate arbitrary Vulkan structs.
EOF
cat > docs/api.md <<'EOF'
# API reference

The public module is `Vulkan.bend`. Vulkan constants are zero-argument definitions in `src/constants.bend`, with their original `VK_` names.
`src/core.bend` provides API-version encoding, flag predicates, queue-family selection, memory-type selection, and U64 limb conversion.

Every native operation returns `IO(VkResult(A))`. `VkResult(A)` is `Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>`.
The `U32` in an error is the exact two's-complement bit pattern of a Vulkan `VkResult`, or a wrapper error from the table below.
The string names the failed operation or invalid input.

| Wrapper code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x60000001` | Loader unavailable or JavaScript backend unsupported |
| `0x60000002` | Unknown, stale, wrong-kind, or wrong-owner handle |
| `0x60000003` | Invalid argument or unsupported memory access range |
| `0x60000004` | Resource still referenced or invalid command state |
| `0x60000005` | Registry, allocation, enumeration, or copy limit |

`Entry.with` preserves the callback's failure code. If cleanup also fails, its diagnostic is appended to the message.
If cleanup alone fails, the scope returns that failure.

## Entry and instance operations

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Entry.load()` | A loader entry |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_version(entry)` | Loader API version, with a Vulkan 1.0 fallback |
| `Entry.create_instance(entry, info)` | An instance |
| `Entry.close(entry)` | Cascading resource teardown and library unload |
| `Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)` | A list of physical devices |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical)` | Name, API version, driver version, vendor ID, device ID, and type |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `(flags, queue_count)` pairs indexed by family |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `Core.MemoryType{property_flags, heap_index}` indexed by memory type |
| `Instance.create_device(instance, physical, info)` | A device with one queue at priority 1.0 |
| `Instance.destroy(instance)` | Instance teardown, rejecting live devices |

`InstanceCreateInfo{application_name, api_version, layers, extensions}` accepts explicit layer and extension names.
`InstanceCreateInfo.default()` requests Vulkan 1.0, with no layers or extensions.
`DeviceCreateInfo{queue_family_index, extensions}` selects one queue and enables no optional device features.
Strings containing NUL are rejected. Allocation callbacks are null.
Physical devices are interned within an instance and invalidated when the instance is destroyed.
The memory query currently exposes memory types, without heap sizes or device limits.

## Buffers and memory

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_buffer(device, BufferCreateInfo{size, usage})` | An exclusive, non-sparse buffer |
| `Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.allocate_memory(device, size, memory_type_index)` | An allocation |
| `Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, offset)` | A binding after size, alignment, type, and owner checks |
| `Device.write_memory(device, memory, offset, bytes)` | Checked host write, including flush for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.read_memory(device, memory, offset, count)` | Byte list, including invalidation for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)` | Buffer teardown |
| `Device.free_memory(device, memory)` | Allocation teardown, rejecting bound buffers |
| `Device.wait_idle(device)` | Device completion |
| `Device.destroy(device)` | Device teardown, rejecting live resources |

Sizes, offsets, and alignments are `bend-collections` `W.U64` values.
`Core.whole_size()` returns Vulkan's all-ones `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` value.
`Core.find_memory_type(types, memory_type_bits, required_flags)` returns the first eligible index or `None`.
`Core.find_queue_family(families, required_flags)` skips empty queues and returns the first matching family.

A byte list contains U32 values from 0 through 255. Copies require host-visible memory.
Each read or write maps the whole allocation temporarily and copies a checked subrange.
`read_memory` takes a U32 byte count. Both copy operations are limited to 16 MiB per call.
Memory allocation sizes and copy offsets retain all 64 bits.

The wrapper checks common lifetime and memory-access errors. Callers remain responsible for Vulkan validity requirements for chosen flags, extensions, and resource use.
Handle keys are checked process-local identifiers. They provide no raw Vulkan handle interoperation or access-control guarantee.

## Command submission

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |
| `Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)` | One primary command buffer |
| `CommandBuffer.begin(command)` | Begin one-time recording |
| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | Record a transfer-write-to-host-read barrier, then end recording |
| `Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)` | Queue submission followed by `vkQueueWaitIdle` |
| `Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)` | Pool teardown and invalidation of its command buffers |

Command buffers are one-shot. They progress through initial, recording, executable, and submitted states.
A fill requires bound memory, `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, four-byte alignment, and a nonempty valid range.
Recorded buffer references remain live until their command pool is destroyed.
The selected queue family must support transfer commands. The examples use a graphics queue.
The API has no asynchronous submission, command reset, individual command-buffer free, or semaphore operations.

`Entry.close` waits for devices, destroys pools and buffers, frees allocations, destroys devices and instances, and unloads the library.
If waiting returns an error other than device loss, cleanup leaves the remaining entry tree live for an explicit retry.
Repeated explicit destruction returns an invalid-handle error.

## Development operations

`debug_live_objects()` returns the live native-registry row count.
`debug_u64_roundtrip(value)` returns two limbs after conversion through a native `uint64_t`.
`Device.buffer_requirements_raw` and `Instance.memory_types_raw` are FFI adapters used by the public query operations.
EOF
