  Resources{device: V.Device, pool: V.CommandPool, command: V.CommandBuffer, spare: V.CommandBuffer, fence: V.Fence, spare_fence: V.Fence, staging: V.Buffer, staging_memory: V.DeviceMemory, gpu: V.Buffer, readback: V.Buffer, readback_memory: V.DeviceMemory, guard: V.Buffer, unrelated: V.DeviceMemory}

def payload(alternate: Bool) -> Array<U32>:
  match alternate:
    case False{}:
      A.words()
    case True{}:
      a = [0 : U32*4n]
      a[0] <- 286397204
      a[1] <- 404166165
      a[2] <- 471538201
      a[3] <- 538910237
      a

def expected(alternate: Bool) -> List<U32>:
  match alternate:
    case False{}:
      [4,3,2,1,5,6,7]
    case True{}:
      [20,19,18,17,21,22,23]

def upload_result(owned: Array<U32> & V.VkResult(Unit), alternate: Bool) -> V.Action(Unit):
  (words, result) = owned
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(Array.to_list(~U32, words), Array.to_list(~U32, payload(alternate))), "Repeated upload changed words")
    A.result_code(0, result)

def upload(+device: V.Device, memory: V.DeviceMemory, +alternate: Bool) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do IO<V.VkResult(Unit)>:
    owned : Array<U32> & V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Device.write_memory_words(device, memory, W.of_u32(3), W.of_u32(7), payload(alternate))
    upload_result(owned, alternate)

def poll(fuel: Nat, +fence: V.Fence, status: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match fuel:
    case 0n:
      Demo.require(U32.is_eq(status,0), "Bounded status polling did not complete")
    case 1n+p:
      match status:
        case 0:
          V.Action.pure(Unit, Unit{})
        case _:
          do V.Action<Unit>:
            next : U32 <- V.Fence.status(fence)
            poll(p, fence, next)

def complete(mode: U32, +device: V.Device, +fence: V.Fence) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match mode:
    case 0:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        status : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence, W.of_u32(1000000000))
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(status,0), "Finite GPU completion wait timed out")
    case 1:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        status : U32 <- V.Fence.status(fence)
        poll(100000n, fence, status)
    case _:
      V.Device.wait_idle(device)

def pending_checks(resources: Resources) -> V.Action(Unit):
  Resources{+device,+pool,+command,+spare,+fence,+spare_fence,+staging,+staging_memory,gpu,+readback,+readback_memory,guard,+unrelated} = resources
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit(device, spare, spare_fence))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, spare))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.CommandBuffer.reset(command))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Fence.reset(fence))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_fence(device, fence))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, staging))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, readback))
    T.expect_error(List<U32>, 1610612740, V.Device.read_memory(device, staging_memory, W.zero(), 1))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.write_memory(device, readback_memory, W.zero(), [0]))
    Transfer.upload(device, staging_memory, W.zero(), W.of_u32(1), 1610612740)
    V.Device.write_memory(device, unrelated, W.zero(), [91])
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, unrelated, W.zero(), 1)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,[91]), "Unrelated memory was blocked")

def cycle(+resources: Resources, +alternate: Bool, mode: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  Resources{+device,pool,+command,spare,+fence,spare_fence,+staging,+staging_memory,+gpu,+readback,+readback_memory,+guard,unrelated} = resources
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    upload(device, staging_memory, alternate)
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, staging, gpu, [V.BufferCopy{W.of_u32(3), W.of_u32(5), W.of_u32(7)}])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, 4096, 4096, [], [V.BufferMemoryBarrier{gpu,W.of_u32(5),W.of_u32(7),4096,2048},V.BufferMemoryBarrier{guard,W.zero(),Core.whole_size(),0,0}])
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, gpu, readback, [V.BufferCopy{W.of_u32(5),W.of_u32(9),W.of_u32(7)}])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, 4096, 16384, [V.MemoryBarrier{4096,8192}], [])
    V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
    V.Device.submit(device, command, fence)
    pending_checks(resources)
    complete(mode, device, fence)
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, readback_memory, W.of_u32(9), 7)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,expected(alternate)), "Repeated GPU literal readback mismatch")
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.submit(device, command, fence))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, staging))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, readback))
    T.expect_error(Unit, 1610612740, V.Device.destroy_buffer(device, guard))

def cycles(fuel: Nat, +resources: Resources, +alternate: Bool, +mode: U32, +rows: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match fuel:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        cycle(resources, alternate, mode)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,rows), "Registry grew during reused transfers")
        cycles(p, resources, Bool.not(alternate), U32.mod(U32.inc(mode),3), rows)

def convenience_cycles(fuel: Nat, +device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +rows: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match fuel:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
        V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
        V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
        V.Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,rows), "Private convenience fence was reallocated")
        convenience_cycles(p,device,command,rows)

def exercise(+device: V.Device, source: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory, middle: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory, destination: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory, barrier: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory, +unrelated: V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  (+src,+sm) = source
  (+gpu,gm) = middle
  (+dst,+rm) = destination
  (+guard,guard_memory) = barrier
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +spare : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    +spare_fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,True{})
    ready : U32 <- V.Fence.status(spare_fence)
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(ready,0), "Initially signaled fence")
    high : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(spare_fence,W.U64{0,1})
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(high,0), "High timeout limb")
    maximum : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(spare_fence,Core.whole_size())
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(maximum,0), "Maximum timeout")
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(spare)
    V.CommandBuffer.end(spare)
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612740,V.Device.submit(device,spare,spare_fence))
    V.Fence.reset(spare_fence)
    not_ready : U32 <- V.Fence.status(fence)
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(not_ready,1), "Never-submitted fence NOT_READY")
    zero : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence,W.zero())
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(zero,2), "Never-submitted zero TIMEOUT")
    finite : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence,W.of_u32(1000))
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(finite,2), "Never-submitted finite TIMEOUT")
    +resources : Resources = Resources{device,pool,command,spare,fence,spare_fence,src,sm,gpu,dst,rm,guard,unrelated}
    rows : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    cycles(32n,resources,False{},0,rows)
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
    V.Device.submit_and_wait(device,command)
    stable : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    convenience_cycles(32n,device,command,stable)
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device,src)
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device,dst)
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device,guard)
    V.Device.destroy_fence(device,fence)
    T.expect_error(U32,1610612738,V.Fence.status(fence))
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612738,V.Fence.reset(fence))
    V.Device.destroy_command_pool(device,pool)

def with_guard(+instance: V.Instance,+physical: V.PhysicalDevice,+device: V.Device,source: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory,middle: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory,destination: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    guard : V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory <- Transfer.buffer(instance,physical,device,3,2)
    +probe : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device,V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(64),3})
    req : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device,probe)
    unrelated : V.DeviceMemory <- Transfer.allocate(instance,physical,device,req,2)
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device,probe)
    exercise(device,source,middle,destination,guard,unrelated)

def with_destination(+instance: V.Instance,+physical: V.PhysicalDevice,+device: V.Device,source: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory,middle: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    destination : V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory <- Transfer.buffer(instance,physical,device,3,2)
    with_guard(instance,physical,device,source,middle,destination)

def with_middle(+instance: V.Instance,+physical: V.PhysicalDevice,+device: V.Device,source: V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    middle : V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory <- Transfer.buffer(instance,physical,device,3,1)
    with_destination(instance,physical,device,source,middle)

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    source : V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory <- Transfer.buffer(instance,physical,device,3,2)
    with_middle(instance,physical,device,source)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    check : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Repeated scope leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,check)
    IO.print("32 repeated GPU transfers and 32 private-fence reuses passed")

def Entry.finish(-A: Type, result: VkResult(A), cleanup: VkResult(Unit)) -> VkResult(A):
  match result cleanup:
    case Fail{(code, message)} Fail{(cleanup_code, cleanup_message)}:
      Fail{(code, message ++ "; cleanup error " ++ U32.show(cleanup_code) ++ ": " ++ cleanup_message)}
    case Fail{error} Done{unit}:
      Fail{error}
    case Done{value} Done{unit}:
      Done{value}
    case Done{value} Fail{error}:
      Fail{error}

def Entry.run_loaded(-A: Type, body: Entry -> IO(VkResult(A)), loaded: VkResult(Entry)) -> IO(VkResult(A)):
  match loaded:
    case Fail{error}:
      IO.pure(VkResult(A), Fail{error})
    case Done{+entry}:
      do IO<VkResult(A)>:
        result : VkResult(A) <- body(entry)
        cleanup : VkResult(Unit) <- Entry.close(entry)
        return Entry.finish(A, result, cleanup)

def Entry.with(-A: Type, body: Entry -> IO(VkResult(A))) -> IO(VkResult(A)):
  do IO<VkResult(A)>:
    loaded : VkResult(Entry) <- Entry.load()
    Entry.run_loaded(A, body, loaded)

def upload(+device: V.Device, +memory: V.DeviceMemory, offset: W.U64, length: W.U64, expected: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do IO<V.VkResult(Unit)>:
    owned : Array<U32> & V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Device.write_memory_words(device, memory, offset, length, A.words())
    A.check_owned(owned, expected)

def allocate(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements, required: U32) -> V.Action(V.DeviceMemory):
  V.MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, bits} = requirements
  do V.Action<V.DeviceMemory>:
    types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)
    index : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_memory_type(types, bits, required), "No compatible memory type")

def buffer(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, usage: U32, required: U32) -> V.Action(V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory):
  do V.Action<V.Buffer & V.DeviceMemory>:
    +buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device, V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(64), usage})
    requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)
    +memory : V.DeviceMemory <- allocate(instance, physical, device, requirements, required)
    V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.zero())

# API reference

The public module is `Vulkan.bend`. Vulkan constants are zero-argument definitions in `src/constants.bend`, with their original `VK_` names.
`src/core.bend` provides API-version encoding, flag predicates, queue-family selection, memory-type selection, and U64 limb conversion.

Operations return `IO(VkResult(A))`, except `write_memory_words`, which returns its array beside the result. `VkResult(A)` is `Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>`.
The `U32` in an error is the exact two's-complement bit pattern of a Vulkan `VkResult`, or a wrapper error from the table below.
The string names the failed operation or invalid input.

| Wrapper code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x60000001` | Loader unavailable or JavaScript backend unsupported |
| `0x60000002` | Unknown, stale, wrong-kind, or wrong-owner handle |
| `0x60000003` | Invalid argument or unsupported memory access range |
| `0x60000004` | Resource still referenced or invalid command state |
| `0x60000005` | Registry, allocation, enumeration, or copy limit |

`Entry.with` preserves the callback's failure code. If cleanup also fails, its diagnostic is appended to the message.
If cleanup alone fails, the scope returns that failure.

## Entry and instance operations

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Entry.load()` | A loader entry |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_version(entry)` | Loader API version, with a Vulkan 1.0 fallback |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_layers(entry)` | Layer names, specification/implementation versions, and descriptions |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_extensions(entry, layer)` | Extension names and specification versions |
| `Entry.create_instance(entry, info)` | An instance |
| `Entry.close(entry)` | Cascading resource teardown and library unload |
| `Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)` | A list of physical devices |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical)` | Name, API version, driver version, vendor ID, device ID, and type |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `(flags, queue_count)` pairs indexed by family |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `Core.MemoryType{property_flags, heap_index}` indexed by memory type |
| `Instance.enumerate_device_extensions(instance, physical, layer)` | Device extension names and specification versions |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_heaps(instance, physical)` | `MemoryHeap{size, flags}` values |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_format_properties(instance, physical, format)` | Linear/optimal tiling and buffer feature masks |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_limits(instance, physical)` | The selected `PhysicalDeviceLimits` fields |
| `Instance.create_device(instance, physical, info)` | A device with one queue at priority 1.0 |
| `Instance.destroy(instance)` | Instance teardown, rejecting live devices |

`InstanceCreateInfo{application_name, api_version, layers, extensions}` accepts explicit layer and extension names.
`InstanceCreateInfo.default()` requests Vulkan 1.0, with no layers or extensions.
`DeviceCreateInfo{queue_family_index, extensions}` selects one queue and enables no optional device features.
Strings containing NUL are rejected. Allocation callbacks are null.
Physical devices are interned within an instance and invalidated when the instance is destroyed.
Layer arguments are `Maybe<String>`. `None` queries global extensions. `Some{name}` forwards that explicit layer name.
Names containing NUL reject. Empty enumerations are valid. Counts are bounded to 4096 and VK_INCOMPLETE retries to eight attempts.
A final Vulkan error, including VK_INCOMPLETE, retains its exact bits. Extension queries preserve the loader's result for the requested layer.
Format queries accept core Vulkan 1.0 enum values 0 through 184 and return raw feature masks.
Discovery does not enable extensions, features, or layers.

`PhysicalDeviceLimits` has these ten U32 fields in order:

- `max_image_dimension_2d`, `max_framebuffer_width`, and `max_framebuffer_height`.
- `max_color_attachments` and `max_push_constants_size`.
- `max_vertex_input_attributes`, `max_vertex_input_bindings`, `max_vertex_input_attribute_offset`, and `max_vertex_input_binding_stride`.
- `max_memory_allocation_count`.

Its final three fields are upstream W.U64 values, `non_coherent_atom_size`, `optimal_buffer_copy_offset_alignment`, and `optimal_buffer_copy_row_pitch_alignment`.
Copy-alignment limits do not impose an alignment restriction on buffer-to-buffer byte copies.

## Buffers and memory

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_buffer(device, BufferCreateInfo{size, usage})` | An exclusive, non-sparse buffer |
| `Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.allocate_memory(device, size, memory_type_index)` | An allocation |
| `Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, offset)` | A binding after size, alignment, type, and owner checks |
| `Device.write_memory(device, memory, offset, bytes)` | Checked host write, including flush for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.write_memory_words(device, memory, offset, byte_length, words)` | Original `Array<U32>` beside `VkResult(Unit)` |
| `Device.read_memory(device, memory, offset, count)` | Byte list, including invalidation for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)` | Buffer teardown |
| `Device.free_memory(device, memory)` | Allocation teardown, rejecting bound buffers |
| `Device.wait_idle(device)` | Device completion |
| `Device.destroy(device)` | Device teardown, rejecting live resources |

Sizes, offsets, and alignments are `bend-collections` `W.U64` values.
`Core.whole_size()` returns Vulkan's all-ones `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` value.
`Core.find_memory_type(types, memory_type_bits, required_flags)` returns the first eligible index or `None`.
`Core.find_queue_family(families, required_flags)` skips empty queues and returns the first matching family.

A byte list contains U32 values from 0 through 255. Host reads and writes require host-visible memory.
Each host operation maps the whole allocation temporarily and copies a checked subrange.
`read_memory` takes a U32 byte count. Host reads and both upload paths are limited to 16 MiB per call.
Memory allocation sizes and copy offsets retain all 64 bits.
Packed uploads emit each word's low-order byte first and truncate the final partial word.
The explicit U64 byte length must fit the array capacity, allocation range, and 16 MiB chunk limit.
Zero bytes at an in-bounds offset is valid. Every outcome returns the unchanged array, including the interpreted backend's native-only error.
A flush failure can leave mapped destination bytes changed.
No Bend heap pointer survives the operation.

The wrapper checks common lifetime and memory-access errors. Callers remain responsible for Vulkan validity requirements for chosen flags, extensions, and resource use.
Handle keys are checked process-local identifiers. They provide no raw Vulkan handle interoperation or access-control guarantee.

## Command submission

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |
| `Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)` | One primary command buffer |
| `CommandBuffer.begin(command)` | Begin one-time recording |
| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, src, dst, regions)` | Record nonempty byte ranges from `List<BufferCopy>` |
| `CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, src_stage, dst_stage, memory, buffers)` | Record explicit memory and buffer barriers |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | End recording |
| `Device.create_fence(device, signaled)` | A caller-owned fence |
| `Device.submit(device, command, fence)` | Submit one executable command with an unsignaled same-device fence |
| `Fence.status(fence)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_NOT_READY` |
| `Fence.wait(fence, timeout_ns)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_TIMEOUT`, with a full U64 nanosecond timeout |
| `Fence.reset(fence)` | Reset an unassociated fence |
| `Device.destroy_fence(device, fence)` | Destroy an unassociated caller-owned fence |
| `CommandBuffer.reset(command)` | Reset a nonpending command and release recorded references after success |
| `Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)` | The same submission/completion core with a persistent private fence and infinite wait |
| `Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)` | Pool teardown and invalidation of its command buffers |

`begin` records with `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. Commands have Initial, Recording, Executable, Pending, Uncertain, Completed, and Invalid states.
Only Initial commands can begin. Successful individual reset returns a command to Initial, including during recording.
Observed completion makes a one-time command Completed. Reset and re-record before submitting it again.
A failed driver reset makes the command Invalid and retains its references.
Pools enable `RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER`. Whole-pool reset and individual command free are absent.

A fill requires bound memory, `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, four-byte alignment, and a nonempty valid range.
Copies require bound buffers, source/destination transfer usages, and positive in-bounds ranges.
They reject overlapping destinations and physical source/destination overlap across every region, including distinct buffers sharing an allocation.
Byte copies impose no four-byte alignment rule.
Recorded references are deduplicated and survive completion and recording/reset failures.
Successful command reset or pool destruction releases them. Referenced buffers cannot be destroyed before that release.

Barrier arguments and every new reference node are validated and allocated before recording.
Buffer barriers use `VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED` for both family indices. Ownership transfers are absent.
Stage/access validation accepts supported core Vulkan 1.0 bits. Optional geometry and tessellation features remain disabled.
`ALL_COMMANDS` excludes HOST. The fill caller records its transfer-to-host barrier explicitly.
The selected queue must support transfers. There is one selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command per device.

Pending/Uncertain commands reject command reset, affected pool destruction, associated fence reset/destruction, and further submission.
Protection remains deterministic until a caller observes completion, even if the GPU has already finished.
Host access rejects entire allocations reached through active references and buffer bindings, including aliases.
Unrelated allocations remain usable. No destructor or mapping operation polls for completion.

Fence SUCCESS and successful device idle complete Pending work. TIMEOUT, NOT_READY, and ordinary wait errors preserve protection.
Known submission OOM leaves command and fence unchanged. Other submit errors enter Uncertain.
Uncertain fence status/wait rejects with `BV_LIFETIME`. Successful idle recovery makes that command Invalid without claiming execution succeeded.
Device loss is sticky, returns exact `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` bits, invalidates commands, detaches associations, and permits ordered destruction.
The convenience fence is private, lazily allocated once per device, and destroyed at device teardown.
Fabricated public fence keys cannot reset, destroy, or submit that private fence.

`Entry.close` waits for devices, destroys pools, fences, and buffers, frees allocations, destroys devices and instances, and unloads the library.
If waiting returns an error other than device loss, cleanup leaves the remaining entry tree live for an explicit retry.
Repeated explicit destruction returns an invalid-handle error.

## Development operations

`debug_live_objects()` returns the live native-registry row count.
`debug_u64_roundtrip(value)` returns two limbs after conversion through a native `uint64_t`.
`Device.buffer_requirements_raw`, `Instance.memory_types_raw`, `Instance.memory_heaps_raw`, and `Instance.limits_raw` are FFI adapters used by the public queries.
`LimitsWords()` names the nested raw limb tuple. Applications use `PhysicalDeviceLimits`.
# Bend Vulkan dispatch and ownership

Bend 2.0.37 cannot extend its opaque host-handle types. Ordinary Data constructors are copyable and forgeable.
The wrapper keeps native handles and dispatch in C and exposes distinct checked U32 registry keys.
`Entry.with` closes the resource tree after a callback returns either success or failure.
Allocation, binding, stage/access masks, timeouts, and reset remain explicit caller choices.

## Registry and dependencies

An Entry owns the loader library and global dispatch. An Instance owns instance dispatch and interned physical-device rows.
A Device owns device dispatch, one selected queue, and its resources. Pools own command buffers.
Buffers retain their bound allocations. Commands retain generic, deduplicated references to recorded resources.
Keys are monotonic and never reused, including after failed creation. Native pointers never come from public keys.
Every effect and registry mutation runs on Bend's IO event loop. Pure preparation can run in parallel.
Dependent Vulkan effects remain sequenced because they mutate the same queue and resource tree.

Recording validates every argument and reserves all reference nodes and marshaling arrays before any void `vkCmd*` dispatch.
Fill retains its buffer. Copy retains both buffers. Buffer barriers retain each mentioned buffer.
References survive completion and failed recording/reset. Successful individual reset or pool destruction releases them.
This keeps buffer destruction independent of whether hardware has finished but completion remains unobserved.
Copy overlap checks use allocation identity plus buffer binding offsets across all source/destination regions.

## Command-owned completion

The command has one tagged state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Initial | Can begin recording |
| Recording | Can record and end |
| Executable | Can submit |
| Pending with a fence | Vulkan accepted the submission; completion is unobserved |
| Uncertain with a fence | An unexpected submit error requires idle recovery |
| Completed | Completion was observed for this one-time recording |
| Invalid | Reset is required before another recording |

`begin` preserves `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. A Completed command cannot resubmit.
Successful reset returns any nonactive command to Initial and clears references. Failed reset invalidates the command and retains references.
Pools enable individual command reset. There is no public whole-pool reset or usage mode.

The command union is the sole submission association. Registry scans find a device's active command or a fence's association.
The device has Healthy/Lost health and a private convenience-fence cache. A fence has a native handle and caller/private lifetime.
There is no device pending flag, fence backpointer, cached signal bit, or second submission registry.
One selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command keep these linear scans bounded by the live registry.

Fence SUCCESS and successful device idle use the same completion transition.
Timeouts, NOT_READY, and ordinary errors retain Pending protection. Submit OOM leaves command and fence unchanged.

# API reference

The public module is `Vulkan.bend`. Vulkan constants are zero-argument definitions in `src/constants.bend`, with their original `VK_` names.
`src/core.bend` provides API-version encoding, flag predicates, queue-family selection, memory-type selection, and U64 limb conversion.

Operations return `IO(VkResult(A))`, except `write_memory_words`, which returns its array beside the result. `VkResult(A)` is `Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>`.
The `U32` in an error is the exact two's-complement bit pattern of a Vulkan `VkResult`, or a wrapper error from the table below.
The string names the failed operation or invalid input.

| Wrapper code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x60000001` | Loader unavailable or JavaScript backend unsupported |
| `0x60000002` | Unknown, stale, wrong-kind, or wrong-owner handle |
| `0x60000003` | Invalid argument or unsupported memory access range |
| `0x60000004` | Resource still referenced or invalid command state |
| `0x60000005` | Registry, allocation, enumeration, or copy limit |

# API reference

The public module is `Vulkan.bend`. Vulkan constants are zero-argument definitions in `src/constants.bend`, with their original `VK_` names.
`src/core.bend` provides API-version encoding, flag predicates, queue-family selection, memory-type selection, and U64 limb conversion.

Operations return `IO(VkResult(A))`, except `write_memory_words`, which returns its array beside the result. `VkResult(A)` is `Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>`.
The `U32` in an error is the exact two's-complement bit pattern of a Vulkan `VkResult`, or a wrapper error from the table below.
The string names the failed operation or invalid input.

| Wrapper code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x60000001` | Loader unavailable or JavaScript backend unsupported |
| `0x60000002` | Unknown, stale, wrong-kind, or wrong-owner handle |
| `0x60000003` | Invalid argument or unsupported memory access range |
| `0x60000004` | Resource still referenced or invalid command state |
| `0x60000005` | Registry, allocation, enumeration, or copy limit |

`Entry.with` preserves the callback's failure code. If cleanup also fails, its diagnostic is appended to the message.
If cleanup alone fails, the scope returns that failure.

## Entry and instance operations

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Entry.load()` | A loader entry |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_version(entry)` | Loader API version, with a Vulkan 1.0 fallback |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_layers(entry)` | Layer names, specification/implementation versions, and descriptions |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_extensions(entry, layer)` | Extension names and specification versions |
| `Entry.create_instance(entry, info)` | An instance |
| `Entry.close(entry)` | Cascading resource teardown and library unload |
| `Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)` | A list of physical devices |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical)` | Name, API version, driver version, vendor ID, device ID, and type |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `(flags, queue_count)` pairs indexed by family |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `Core.MemoryType{property_flags, heap_index}` indexed by memory type |
| `Instance.enumerate_device_extensions(instance, physical, layer)` | Device extension names and specification versions |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_heaps(instance, physical)` | `MemoryHeap{size, flags}` values |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_format_properties(instance, physical, format)` | Linear/optimal tiling and buffer feature masks |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_limits(instance, physical)` | The selected `PhysicalDeviceLimits` fields |
| `Instance.create_device(instance, physical, info)` | A device with one queue at priority 1.0 |
| `Instance.destroy(instance)` | Instance teardown, rejecting live devices |

`InstanceCreateInfo{application_name, api_version, layers, extensions}` accepts explicit layer and extension names.
`InstanceCreateInfo.default()` requests Vulkan 1.0, with no layers or extensions.
`DeviceCreateInfo{queue_family_index, extensions}` selects one queue and enables no optional device features.
Strings containing NUL are rejected. Allocation callbacks are null.
Physical devices are interned within an instance and invalidated when the instance is destroyed.
Layer arguments are `Maybe<String>`. `None` queries global extensions. `Some{name}` forwards that explicit layer name.
Names containing NUL reject. Empty enumerations are valid. Counts are bounded to 4096 and VK_INCOMPLETE retries to eight attempts.
A final Vulkan error, including VK_INCOMPLETE, retains its exact bits. Extension queries preserve the loader's result for the requested layer.
Format queries accept core Vulkan 1.0 enum values 0 through 184 and return raw feature masks.
Discovery does not enable extensions, features, or layers.

`PhysicalDeviceLimits` has these ten U32 fields in order:

- `max_image_dimension_2d`, `max_framebuffer_width`, and `max_framebuffer_height`.
- `max_color_attachments` and `max_push_constants_size`.
- `max_vertex_input_attributes`, `max_vertex_input_bindings`, `max_vertex_input_attribute_offset`, and `max_vertex_input_binding_stride`.
- `max_memory_allocation_count`.

Its final three fields are upstream W.U64 values, `non_coherent_atom_size`, `optimal_buffer_copy_offset_alignment`, and `optimal_buffer_copy_row_pitch_alignment`.
Copy-alignment limits do not impose an alignment restriction on buffer-to-buffer byte copies.

## Buffers and memory

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_buffer(device, BufferCreateInfo{size, usage})` | An exclusive, non-sparse buffer |
| `Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.allocate_memory(device, size, memory_type_index)` | An allocation |
| `Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, offset)` | A binding after size, alignment, type, and owner checks |
| `Device.write_memory(device, memory, offset, bytes)` | Checked host write, including flush for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.write_memory_words(device, memory, offset, byte_length, words)` | Original `Array<U32>` beside `VkResult(Unit)` |
| `Device.read_memory(device, memory, offset, count)` | Byte list, including invalidation for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)` | Buffer teardown |
| `Device.free_memory(device, memory)` | Allocation teardown, rejecting bound buffers |
| `Device.wait_idle(device)` | Device completion |
| `Device.destroy(device)` | Device teardown, rejecting live resources |

Sizes, offsets, and alignments are `bend-collections` `W.U64` values.
`Core.whole_size()` returns Vulkan's all-ones `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` value.
`Core.find_memory_type(types, memory_type_bits, required_flags)` returns the first eligible index or `None`.
`Core.find_queue_family(families, required_flags)` skips empty queues and returns the first matching family.

A byte list contains U32 values from 0 through 255. Host reads and writes require host-visible memory.
Each host operation maps the whole allocation temporarily and copies a checked subrange.
`read_memory` takes a U32 byte count. Host reads and both upload paths are limited to 16 MiB per call.
Memory allocation sizes and copy offsets retain all 64 bits.
Packed uploads emit each word's low-order byte first and truncate the final partial word.
The explicit U64 byte length must fit the array capacity, allocation range, and 16 MiB chunk limit.
Zero bytes at an in-bounds offset is valid. Every outcome returns the unchanged array, including the interpreted backend's native-only error.
A flush failure can leave mapped destination bytes changed.
No Bend heap pointer survives the operation.

The wrapper checks common lifetime and memory-access errors. Callers remain responsible for Vulkan validity requirements for chosen flags, extensions, and resource use.
Handle keys are checked process-local identifiers. They provide no raw Vulkan handle interoperation or access-control guarantee.

## Command submission

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |
| `Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)` | One primary command buffer |
| `CommandBuffer.begin(command)` | Begin one-time recording |
| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, src, dst, regions)` | Record nonempty byte ranges from `List<BufferCopy>` |
| `CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, src_stage, dst_stage, memory, buffers)` | Record explicit memory and buffer barriers |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | End recording |
| `Device.create_fence(device, signaled)` | A caller-owned fence |
| `Device.submit(device, command, fence)` | Submit one executable command with an unsignaled same-device fence |
| `Fence.status(fence)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_NOT_READY` |
| `Fence.wait(fence, timeout_ns)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_TIMEOUT`, with a full U64 nanosecond timeout |
| `Fence.reset(fence)` | Reset an unassociated fence |
| `Device.destroy_fence(device, fence)` | Destroy an unassociated caller-owned fence |
| `CommandBuffer.reset(command)` | Reset a nonpending command and release recorded references after success |
| `Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)` | The same submission/completion core with a persistent private fence and infinite wait |
| `Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)` | Pool teardown and invalidation of its command buffers |

`begin` records with `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. Commands have Initial, Recording, Executable, Pending, Uncertain, Completed, and Invalid states.
Only Initial commands can begin. Successful individual reset returns a command to Initial, including during recording.
Observed completion makes a one-time command Completed. Reset and re-record before submitting it again.
A failed driver reset makes the command Invalid and retains its references.
Pools enable `RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER`. Whole-pool reset and individual command free are absent.

A fill requires bound memory, `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, four-byte alignment, and a nonempty valid range.
Copies require bound buffers, source/destination transfer usages, and positive in-bounds ranges.
They reject overlapping destinations and physical source/destination overlap across every region, including distinct buffers sharing an allocation.
Byte copies impose no four-byte alignment rule.
Recorded references are deduplicated and survive completion and recording/reset failures.
Successful command reset or pool destruction releases them. Referenced buffers cannot be destroyed before that release.

Barrier arguments and every new reference node are validated and allocated before recording.
Buffer barriers use `VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED` for both family indices. Ownership transfers are absent.
Stage/access validation accepts supported core Vulkan 1.0 bits. Optional geometry and tessellation features remain disabled.
`ALL_COMMANDS` excludes HOST. The fill caller records its transfer-to-host barrier explicitly.
The selected queue must support transfers. There is one selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command per device.

Pending/Uncertain commands reject command reset, affected pool destruction, associated fence reset/destruction, and further submission.
Protection remains deterministic until a caller observes completion, even if the GPU has already finished.
Host access rejects entire allocations reached through active references and buffer bindings, including aliases.
Unrelated allocations remain usable. No destructor or mapping operation polls for completion.

Fence SUCCESS and successful device idle complete Pending work. TIMEOUT, NOT_READY, and ordinary wait errors preserve protection.
Known submission OOM leaves command and fence unchanged. Other submit errors enter Uncertain.
Uncertain fence status/wait rejects with `BV_LIFETIME`. Successful idle recovery makes that command Invalid without claiming execution succeeded.
Device loss is sticky, returns exact `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` bits, invalidates commands, detaches associations, and permits ordered destruction.
The convenience fence is private, lazily allocated once per device, and destroyed at device teardown.
Fabricated public fence keys cannot reset, destroy, or submit that private fence.

`Entry.close` waits for devices, destroys pools, fences, and buffers, frees allocations, destroys devices and instances, and unloads the library.
If waiting returns an error other than device loss, cleanup leaves the remaining entry tree live for an explicit retry.
Repeated explicit destruction returns an invalid-handle error.

## Development operations

`debug_live_objects()` returns the live native-registry row count.
`debug_u64_roundtrip(value)` returns two limbs after conversion through a native `uint64_t`.
`Device.buffer_requirements_raw`, `Instance.memory_types_raw`, `Instance.memory_heaps_raw`, and `Instance.limits_raw` are FFI adapters used by the public queries.
`LimitsWords()` names the nested raw limb tuple. Applications use `PhysicalDeviceLimits`.
# Bend Vulkan dispatch and ownership

Bend 2.0.37 cannot extend its opaque host-handle types. Ordinary Data constructors are copyable and forgeable.
The wrapper keeps native handles and dispatch in C and exposes distinct checked U32 registry keys.
`Entry.with` closes the resource tree after a callback returns either success or failure.
Allocation, binding, stage/access masks, timeouts, and reset remain explicit caller choices.

## Registry and dependencies

An Entry owns the loader library and global dispatch. An Instance owns instance dispatch and interned physical-device rows.
A Device owns device dispatch, one selected queue, and its resources. Pools own command buffers.
Buffers retain their bound allocations. Commands retain generic, deduplicated references to recorded resources.
Keys are monotonic and never reused, including after failed creation. Native pointers never come from public keys.
Every effect and registry mutation runs on Bend's IO event loop. Pure preparation can run in parallel.
Dependent Vulkan effects remain sequenced because they mutate the same queue and resource tree.

Recording validates every argument and reserves all reference nodes and marshaling arrays before any void `vkCmd*` dispatch.
Fill retains its buffer. Copy retains both buffers. Buffer barriers retain each mentioned buffer.
References survive completion and failed recording/reset. Successful individual reset or pool destruction releases them.
This keeps buffer destruction independent of whether hardware has finished but completion remains unobserved.
Copy overlap checks use allocation identity plus buffer binding offsets across all source/destination regions.

## Command-owned completion

The command has one tagged state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Initial | Can begin recording |
| Recording | Can record and end |
| Executable | Can submit |
| Pending with a fence | Vulkan accepted the submission; completion is unobserved |
| Uncertain with a fence | An unexpected submit error requires idle recovery |
| Completed | Completion was observed for this one-time recording |
| Invalid | Reset is required before another recording |

`begin` preserves `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. A Completed command cannot resubmit.
Successful reset returns any nonactive command to Initial and clears references. Failed reset invalidates the command and retains references.
Pools enable individual command reset. There is no public whole-pool reset or usage mode.

The command union is the sole submission association. Registry scans find a device's active command or a fence's association.
The device has Healthy/Lost health and a private convenience-fence cache. A fence has a native handle and caller/private lifetime.
There is no device pending flag, fence backpointer, cached signal bit, or second submission registry.
One selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command keep these linear scans bounded by the live registry.

Fence SUCCESS and successful device idle use the same completion transition.
Timeouts, NOT_READY, and ordinary errors retain Pending protection. Submit OOM leaves command and fence unchanged.
Unexpected submit errors enter Uncertain. Fence status/wait rejects that state because submission may never have occurred.
Successful idle recovery makes Uncertain work Invalid without claiming execution or readback succeeded.
Device loss is sticky. It invalidates every command, detaches associations, and permits dependency-ordered teardown with exact loss bits.

Host mapping follows active command references through buffer bindings and rejects the entire reached allocation, including aliases.
Unrelated allocations remain usable. Reset, destruction, mapping, and further submit never poll for completion implicitly.
`submit_and_wait` uses the same submit/observe functions with U64_MAX and one lazily allocated persistent private fence per device.
Public fence lookup rejects private rows, including fabricated keys. Only device teardown destroys the cached fence.

## Cleanup and errors

Entry cleanup observes idle first, then destroys pools, fences, buffers, allocations, devices, physical rows, instances, and the loader.
An ordinary idle error leaves unsafe resources and the entry live for explicit retry. Known loss permits teardown and returns exact loss.
A callback failure keeps its original code and appends a cleanup failure's diagnostic.
Explicit device destruction requires public children gone and also destroys its private convenience fence.

Vulkan results retain their exact two's-complement U32 bits. Fence status/wait return ordinary SUCCESS, NOT_READY, or TIMEOUT inside Done.
Wrapper failures have distinct invalid-handle, argument, lifetime, and allocation-limit codes.
Checks cover this subset's native boundary. The application still owns Vulkan synchronization correctness and capability negotiation.

## Compiler ABI and packed uploads

The compiler packs single-U32 handles and flattens nested Data fields in buffer configs, copies, and buffer barriers.
C follows emitted layouts. Imported U64 constructors cannot appear in native CID macros.
Heap sizes and selected limits cross as nested U32 limb tuples. Pure adapters reconstruct the pinned bend-collections U64.
All sizes, offsets, alignments, and nanosecond timeouts use that upstream type. Existing byte-list read counts remain U32.

Packed uploads return `Array<U32> & VkResult(Unit)` on every path. The generator records the owner argument explicitly in its manifest.
Native code reads packed TAG_BUF slots or Term-backed TAG_ARR slots with emitted block helpers and resolves shared blocks.
Capacity is the block's logical word count, rather than its heap span. No Bend heap pointer survives the immediate operation.
Words emit low-order bytes first. An explicit byte length truncates a partial final word and must fit capacity, allocation range, SIZE_MAX, and 16 MiB.
Each operation maps the whole allocation, maintains whole-allocation noncoherent cache ranges when needed, and unmaps every mapped path.
A flush error may leave destination bytes modified while returning the original words unchanged.

## Discovery and scope

Entry dispatch enumerates layers and instance extensions. Instance dispatch queries device extensions, heaps, core-1.0 formats, and thirteen selected limits.
Enumeration accepts empty results, bounds count allocations, and retries VK_INCOMPLETE at most eight times.
Optional layer names pass to Vulkan explicitly. Queries return capabilities without enabling them.
The registry extract retains its original source SHA256 and adds core format, format-feature, and memory-heap constants from that same source.

The fixed compiler version is part of this ABI contract. Real effect-return tests cover native and interpreted array ownership.
Test-only C probes substitute dispatch and metadata allocation in an emitted translation unit. Production code exposes no injection hooks.
Those probes distinguish controlled errors and loss from driver execution.
Separate native runs verify literal GPU readback, 32 changing staging/copy/readback cycles, command/fence reuse, and stable registry rows.
Pure laws cover packing and limb conversion, not driver behavior.

Linear registry scans, allocation-wide host exclusion, and one-time recordings keep one ownership model for this milestone.
Multiple queues, multiple active submissions, images, shaders, graphics, descriptors, and presentation remain outside this subset.

# API reference

The public module is `Vulkan.bend`. Vulkan constants are zero-argument definitions in `src/constants.bend`, with their original `VK_` names.
`src/core.bend` provides API-version encoding, flag predicates, queue-family selection, memory-type selection, and U64 limb conversion.

Operations return `IO(VkResult(A))`, except `write_memory_words`, which returns its array beside the result. `VkResult(A)` is `Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), A>`.
The `U32` in an error is the exact two's-complement bit pattern of a Vulkan `VkResult`, or a wrapper error from the table below.
The string names the failed operation or invalid input.

| Wrapper code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x60000001` | Loader unavailable or JavaScript backend unsupported |
| `0x60000002` | Unknown, stale, wrong-kind, or wrong-owner handle |
| `0x60000003` | Invalid argument or unsupported memory access range |
| `0x60000004` | Resource still referenced or invalid command state |
| `0x60000005` | Registry, allocation, enumeration, or copy limit |

`Entry.with` preserves the callback's failure code. If cleanup also fails, its diagnostic is appended to the message.
If cleanup alone fails, the scope returns that failure.

## Entry and instance operations

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Entry.load()` | A loader entry |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_version(entry)` | Loader API version, with a Vulkan 1.0 fallback |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_layers(entry)` | Layer names, specification/implementation versions, and descriptions |
| `Entry.enumerate_instance_extensions(entry, layer)` | Extension names and specification versions |
| `Entry.create_instance(entry, info)` | An instance |
| `Entry.close(entry)` | Cascading resource teardown and library unload |
| `Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)` | A list of physical devices |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_properties(instance, physical)` | Name, API version, driver version, vendor ID, device ID, and type |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `(flags, queue_count)` pairs indexed by family |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)` | A list of `Core.MemoryType{property_flags, heap_index}` indexed by memory type |
| `Instance.enumerate_device_extensions(instance, physical, layer)` | Device extension names and specification versions |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_memory_heaps(instance, physical)` | `MemoryHeap{size, flags}` values |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_format_properties(instance, physical, format)` | Linear/optimal tiling and buffer feature masks |
| `Instance.get_physical_device_limits(instance, physical)` | The selected `PhysicalDeviceLimits` fields |
| `Instance.create_device(instance, physical, info)` | A device with one queue at priority 1.0 |
| `Instance.destroy(instance)` | Instance teardown, rejecting live devices |

`InstanceCreateInfo{application_name, api_version, layers, extensions}` accepts explicit layer and extension names.
`InstanceCreateInfo.default()` requests Vulkan 1.0, with no layers or extensions.
`DeviceCreateInfo{queue_family_index, extensions}` selects one queue and enables no optional device features.
Strings containing NUL are rejected. Allocation callbacks are null.
Physical devices are interned within an instance and invalidated when the instance is destroyed.
Layer arguments are `Maybe<String>`. `None` queries global extensions. `Some{name}` forwards that explicit layer name.
Names containing NUL reject. Empty enumerations are valid. Counts are bounded to 4096 and VK_INCOMPLETE retries to eight attempts.
A final Vulkan error, including VK_INCOMPLETE, retains its exact bits. Extension queries preserve the loader's result for the requested layer.
Format queries accept core Vulkan 1.0 enum values 0 through 184 and return raw feature masks.
Discovery does not enable extensions, features, or layers.

`PhysicalDeviceLimits` has these ten U32 fields in order:

- `max_image_dimension_2d`, `max_framebuffer_width`, and `max_framebuffer_height`.
- `max_color_attachments` and `max_push_constants_size`.
- `max_vertex_input_attributes`, `max_vertex_input_bindings`, `max_vertex_input_attribute_offset`, and `max_vertex_input_binding_stride`.
- `max_memory_allocation_count`.

Its final three fields are upstream W.U64 values, `non_coherent_atom_size`, `optimal_buffer_copy_offset_alignment`, and `optimal_buffer_copy_row_pitch_alignment`.
Copy-alignment limits do not impose an alignment restriction on buffer-to-buffer byte copies.

## Buffers and memory

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_buffer(device, BufferCreateInfo{size, usage})` | An exclusive, non-sparse buffer |
| `Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.allocate_memory(device, size, memory_type_index)` | An allocation |
| `Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, offset)` | A binding after size, alignment, type, and owner checks |
| `Device.write_memory(device, memory, offset, bytes)` | Checked host write, including flush for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.write_memory_words(device, memory, offset, byte_length, words)` | Original `Array<U32>` beside `VkResult(Unit)` |
| `Device.read_memory(device, memory, offset, count)` | Byte list, including invalidation for noncoherent memory |
| `Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)` | Buffer teardown |
| `Device.free_memory(device, memory)` | Allocation teardown, rejecting bound buffers |
| `Device.wait_idle(device)` | Device completion |
| `Device.destroy(device)` | Device teardown, rejecting live resources |

Sizes, offsets, and alignments are `bend-collections` `W.U64` values.
`Core.whole_size()` returns Vulkan's all-ones `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` value.
`Core.find_memory_type(types, memory_type_bits, required_flags)` returns the first eligible index or `None`.
`Core.find_queue_family(families, required_flags)` skips empty queues and returns the first matching family.

A byte list contains U32 values from 0 through 255. Host reads and writes require host-visible memory.
Each host operation maps the whole allocation temporarily and copies a checked subrange.
`read_memory` takes a U32 byte count. Host reads and both upload paths are limited to 16 MiB per call.
Memory allocation sizes and copy offsets retain all 64 bits.
Packed uploads emit each word's low-order byte first and truncate the final partial word.
The explicit U64 byte length must fit the array capacity, allocation range, and 16 MiB chunk limit.
Zero bytes at an in-bounds offset is valid. Every outcome returns the unchanged array, including the interpreted backend's native-only error.
A flush failure can leave mapped destination bytes changed.
No Bend heap pointer survives the operation.

The wrapper checks common lifetime and memory-access errors. Callers remain responsible for Vulkan validity requirements for chosen flags, extensions, and resource use.
Handle keys are checked process-local identifiers. They provide no raw Vulkan handle interoperation or access-control guarantee.

## Command submission

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |
| `Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)` | One primary command buffer |
| `CommandBuffer.begin(command)` | Begin one-time recording |
| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, src, dst, regions)` | Record nonempty byte ranges from `List<BufferCopy>` |
| `CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, src_stage, dst_stage, memory, buffers)` | Record explicit memory and buffer barriers |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | End recording |
| `Device.create_fence(device, signaled)` | A caller-owned fence |
| `Device.submit(device, command, fence)` | Submit one executable command with an unsignaled same-device fence |
| `Fence.status(fence)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_NOT_READY` |
| `Fence.wait(fence, timeout_ns)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_TIMEOUT`, with a full U64 nanosecond timeout |
| `Fence.reset(fence)` | Reset an unassociated fence |
| `Device.destroy_fence(device, fence)` | Destroy an unassociated caller-owned fence |
| `CommandBuffer.reset(command)` | Reset a nonpending command and release recorded references after success |
| `Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)` | The same submission/completion core with a persistent private fence and infinite wait |
| `Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)` | Pool teardown and invalidation of its command buffers |

`begin` records with `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. Commands have Initial, Recording, Executable, Pending, Uncertain, Completed, and Invalid states.
Only Initial commands can begin. Successful individual reset returns a command to Initial, including during recording.
Observed completion makes a one-time command Completed. Reset and re-record before submitting it again.
A failed driver reset makes the command Invalid and retains its references.
Pools enable `RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER`. Whole-pool reset and individual command free are absent.

A fill requires bound memory, `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, four-byte alignment, and a nonempty valid range.
Copies require bound buffers, source/destination transfer usages, and positive in-bounds ranges.
They reject overlapping destinations and physical source/destination overlap across every region, including distinct buffers sharing an allocation.
Byte copies impose no four-byte alignment rule.
Recorded references are deduplicated and survive completion and recording/reset failures.
Successful command reset or pool destruction releases them. Referenced buffers cannot be destroyed before that release.

Barrier arguments and every new reference node are validated and allocated before recording.
Buffer barriers use `VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED` for both family indices. Ownership transfers are absent.
Stage/access validation accepts supported core Vulkan 1.0 bits. Optional geometry and tessellation features remain disabled.
`ALL_COMMANDS` excludes HOST. The fill caller records its transfer-to-host barrier explicitly.
The selected queue must support transfers. There is one selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command per device.

Pending/Uncertain commands reject command reset, affected pool destruction, associated fence reset/destruction, and further submission.
Protection remains deterministic until a caller observes completion, even if the GPU has already finished.
Host access rejects entire allocations reached through active references and buffer bindings, including aliases.
Unrelated allocations remain usable. No destructor or mapping operation polls for completion.

Fence SUCCESS and successful device idle complete Pending work. TIMEOUT, NOT_READY, and ordinary wait errors preserve protection.
Known submission OOM leaves command and fence unchanged. Other submit errors enter Uncertain.
Uncertain fence status/wait rejects with `BV_LIFETIME`. Successful idle recovery makes that command Invalid without claiming execution succeeded.
Device loss is sticky, returns exact `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` bits, invalidates commands, detaches associations, and permits ordered destruction.
The convenience fence is private, lazily allocated once per device, and destroyed at device teardown.
Fabricated public fence keys cannot reset, destroy, or submit that private fence.

`Entry.close` waits for devices, destroys pools, fences, and buffers, frees allocations, destroys devices and instances, and unloads the library.
If waiting returns an error other than device loss, cleanup leaves the remaining entry tree live for an explicit retry.
Repeated explicit destruction returns an invalid-handle error.

## Development operations

`debug_live_objects()` returns the live native-registry row count.
`debug_u64_roundtrip(value)` returns two limbs after conversion through a native `uint64_t`.
`Device.buffer_requirements_raw`, `Instance.memory_types_raw`, `Instance.memory_heaps_raw`, and `Instance.limits_raw` are FFI adapters used by the public queries.
`LimitsWords()` names the nested raw limb tuple. Applications use `PhysicalDeviceLimits`.
# Bend Vulkan dispatch and ownership

Bend 2.0.37 cannot extend its opaque host-handle types. Ordinary Data constructors are copyable and forgeable.
The wrapper keeps native handles and dispatch in C and exposes distinct checked U32 registry keys.
`Entry.with` closes the resource tree after a callback returns either success or failure.
Allocation, binding, stage/access masks, timeouts, and reset remain explicit caller choices.

## Registry and dependencies

An Entry owns the loader library and global dispatch. An Instance owns instance dispatch and interned physical-device rows.
A Device owns device dispatch, one selected queue, and its resources. Pools own command buffers.
Buffers retain their bound allocations. Commands retain generic, deduplicated references to recorded resources.
Keys are monotonic and never reused, including after failed creation. Native pointers never come from public keys.
Every effect and registry mutation runs on Bend's IO event loop. Pure preparation can run in parallel.
Dependent Vulkan effects remain sequenced because they mutate the same queue and resource tree.

Recording validates every argument and reserves all reference nodes and marshaling arrays before any void `vkCmd*` dispatch.
Fill retains its buffer. Copy retains both buffers. Buffer barriers retain each mentioned buffer.
References survive completion and failed recording/reset. Successful individual reset or pool destruction releases them.

## Discovery and scope

Entry dispatch enumerates layers and instance extensions. Instance dispatch queries device extensions, heaps, core-1.0 formats, and thirteen selected limits.
Enumeration accepts empty results, bounds count allocations, and retries VK_INCOMPLETE at most eight times.
Optional layer names pass to Vulkan explicitly. Queries return capabilities without enabling them.
The registry extract retains its original source SHA256 and adds core format, format-feature, and memory-heap constants from that same source.

The fixed compiler version is part of this ABI contract. Real effect-return tests cover native and interpreted array ownership.
Test-only C probes substitute dispatch and metadata allocation in an emitted translation unit. Production code exposes no injection hooks.
Those probes distinguish controlled errors and loss from driver execution.
Separate native runs verify literal GPU readback, 32 changing staging/copy/readback cycles, command/fence reuse, and stable registry rows.
Pure laws cover packing and limb conversion, not driver behavior.

Linear registry scans, allocation-wide host exclusion, and one-time recordings keep one ownership model for this milestone.

`begin` preserves `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. A Completed command cannot resubmit.
Successful reset returns any nonactive command to Initial and clears references. Failed reset invalidates the command and retains references.
Pools enable individual command reset. There is no public whole-pool reset or usage mode.

The command union is the sole submission association. Registry scans find a device's active command or a fence's association.
The device has Healthy/Lost health and a private convenience-fence cache. A fence has a native handle and caller/private lifetime.
There is no device pending flag, fence backpointer, cached signal bit, or second submission registry.
One selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command keep these linear scans bounded by the live registry.

Fence SUCCESS and successful device idle use the same completion transition.
Timeouts, NOT_READY, and ordinary errors retain Pending protection. Submit OOM leaves command and fence unchanged.
Unexpected submit errors enter Uncertain. Fence status/wait rejects that state because submission may never have occurred.
Successful idle recovery makes Uncertain work Invalid without claiming execution or readback succeeded.
Device loss is sticky. It invalidates every command, detaches associations, and permits dependency-ordered teardown with exact loss bits.

Host mapping follows active command references through buffer bindings and rejects the entire reached allocation, including aliases.
Unrelated allocations remain usable. Reset, destruction, mapping, and further submit never poll for completion implicitly.
`submit_and_wait` uses the same submit/observe functions with U64_MAX and one lazily allocated persistent private fence per device.
Public fence lookup rejects private rows, including fabricated keys. Only device teardown destroys the cached fence.

## Cleanup and errors

Entry cleanup observes idle first, then destroys pools, fences, buffers, allocations, devices, physical rows, instances, and the loader.
An ordinary idle error leaves unsafe resources and the entry live for explicit retry. Known loss permits teardown and returns exact loss.
A callback failure keeps its original code and appends a cleanup failure's diagnostic.
Explicit device destruction requires public children gone and also destroys its private convenience fence.

Vulkan results retain their exact two's-complement U32 bits. Fence status/wait return ordinary SUCCESS, NOT_READY, or TIMEOUT inside Done.
Wrapper failures have distinct invalid-handle, argument, lifetime, and allocation-limit codes.
Checks cover this subset's native boundary. The application still owns Vulkan synchronization correctness and capability negotiation.

## Compiler ABI and packed uploads

The compiler packs single-U32 handles and flattens nested Data fields in buffer configs, copies, and buffer barriers.
C follows emitted layouts. Imported U64 constructors cannot appear in native CID macros.
Heap sizes and selected limits cross as nested U32 limb tuples. Pure adapters reconstruct the pinned bend-collections U64.
All sizes, offsets, alignments, and nanosecond timeouts use that upstream type. Existing byte-list read counts remain U32.

Packed uploads return `Array<U32> & VkResult(Unit)` on every path. The generator records the owner argument explicitly in its manifest.
Native code reads packed TAG_BUF slots or Term-backed TAG_ARR slots with emitted block helpers and resolves shared blocks.
Capacity is the block's logical word count, rather than its heap span. No Bend heap pointer survives the immediate operation.
Words emit low-order bytes first. An explicit byte length truncates a partial final word and must fit capacity, allocation range, SIZE_MAX, and 16 MiB.
Each operation maps the whole allocation, maintains whole-allocation noncoherent cache ranges when needed, and unmaps every mapped path.
A flush error may leave destination bytes modified while returning the original words unchanged.

## Discovery and scope

Entry dispatch enumerates layers and instance extensions. Instance dispatch queries device extensions, heaps, core-1.0 formats, and thirteen selected limits.
Enumeration accepts empty results, bounds count allocations, and retries VK_INCOMPLETE at most eight times.
# Vulkan wrapper roadmap

The target is an ash-inspired Bend wrapper that can run bend-voxel as a mesh renderer.
Bend owns the world, edits, meshing, and application state. GLSL vertex and fragment shaders run through Vulkan graphics pipelines.
The first renderer milestone is a headless, indexed mesh draw with color and depth readback. Window presentation follows that working path.

Milestones are ordered by dependency and observable results. They are not release dates.
Only milestone 0 is implemented. Proposed API names below describe capabilities, not existing declarations.

## Delivery order

| Milestone | Status | Wrapper capability | Acceptance result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0. Native foundation | Implemented | Loader, checked handles, buffers, memory, synchronous fill | Exact host and GPU buffer readback |
| 1. General transfers and completion | Next | Bulk uploads, explicit barriers, buffer copies, fences, command reuse | Repeated upload, copy, and readback with bounded live resources |
| 2. Offscreen images | Planned | Images, memory binding, views, layouts, render targets, readback | Clear and read back a known color image |
| 3. Indexed graphics | Planned | SPIR-V modules, graphics pipelines, vertex/index binding, depth, push constants | Indexed geometry renders with verified occlusion |
| 4. Voxel mesh consumer | Planned | Complete the minimal mesh-drawing API through a real consumer | Intact and carved 8³ cube exported at 512×512 |
| 5. Interactive presentation | Planned | Native surfaces, swapchains, acquire/submit/present, frame lifecycle | Editable cube runs in a Vulkan window |
| 6. Full scene and appearance | Planned | Descriptors, uniforms, sampled images, samplers, shadow passes | Atelier scene, materials, ground, shadows, and brush preview |
| 7. Repeated edits and throughput | Planned | Reusable upload storage, resource retirement, measured batching | Camera flight and repeated carving stay correct with stable resource use |
| 8. Library breadth and portability | Planned | Broader generated bindings, negotiated extensions, additional platforms | Documented support verified on additional drivers and applications |

The first public renderer checkpoint is milestone 4. The first interactive renderer checkpoint is milestone 5.

## 0. Native foundation

The current implementation provides these capabilities:

- [x] Entry, instance, and device dispatch with distinct checked handle types.
- [x] Device, queue-family, and memory-type discovery.
- [x] Explicit buffer creation, memory requirements, allocation, binding, and destruction.
- [x] Bounds-checked host byte copies, including noncoherent cache handling.

ALL PROOFS CHECK

Implement milestone 1 as a sequence of verifiable changes: explicit barriers, buffer copy with bulk upload, then fence-backed submission and command reuse.
Migrate the existing fill example during those changes. Keep its exact GPU readback as the baseline while adding general recording behavior.
# bend-vulkan

A native Vulkan wrapper for Bend, inspired by [ash](https://github.com/ash-rs/ash).
The implementation provides explicit instance, device, buffer, memory, command-buffer, and fence operations.
All Vulkan byte sizes, offsets, and alignments use the actual two-limb `U64` from [bend-collections](https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend-collections).

This is a 64-bit Linux, headless Vulkan 1.0 subset. It supports capability discovery, explicit barriers, packed array uploads, alias-safe GPU buffer copies, and fence-backed command reuse.
Graphics pipelines, compute shaders, images, descriptors, surfaces, swapchains, callbacks, and general `pNext` chains are not implemented.

## Run the buffer example

Use Linux with glibc 2.34 or newer. Install Bend **2.0.37**, Clang, Python 3, Vulkan development headers, `libvulkan.so.1`, and a Vulkan driver.
A hardware driver or a software ICD such as Lavapipe can provide the device.
The examples select a graphics queue for transfer commands.

Initialize the pinned dependency:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Build and run the native example:

```sh
mkdir -p build
bend examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend -o build/buffer-roundtrip
./build/buffer-roundtrip
```

Expected output:

```text
Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified
```

The example writes four bytes to Vulkan memory and checks their readback.
It then records `vkCmdFillBuffer`, submits the command buffer, waits for completion, and checks sixteen bytes against the value `42`.
Build and run `examples/discover.bend` the same way to list layers, extensions, devices, heaps, format masks, and selected limits.
It prints U64 values as low/high limbs.

`bend example.bend` uses Bend's JavaScript backend. Vulkan effects report a native-build-required error in that backend.

## Use the API

Import `Vulkan.bend`, `src/core.bend`, `src/constants.bend`, and the dependency's `src/math/u64.bend` with paths relative to your program.
The executable [buffer example](examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend) shows allocation and fill submission.
The [repeated transfer check](tests/repeated.bend) shows packed upload, explicit barriers, general submission, finite completion, and reset/re-recording.

`V.Action(A)` is `IO(V.VkResult(A))`. A `do V.Action<Unit>:` block propagates returned failures.
`V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => run(entry))` loads the Vulkan library, runs your callback, and closes its resource tree after either `Done` or `Fail`.
Use `V.or_exit(Unit, result)` at the application boundary to report the final result.
Calling `IO.die`, `IO.exit`, or `IO.try` inside a resource scope bypasses that cleanup callback.

Handle values are copyable with Bend's `+` annotations. Each handle kind has a distinct type.
Native code validates registry keys, object kinds, ownership, and liveness before it calls Vulkan.
Explicit destroy operations reject live dependents. `Entry.close` releases descendants in dependency order.
Dropping a Bend handle value does not destroy its Vulkan object.

See [the API reference](docs/api.md) for supported operations and [the design](docs/design.md) for the FFI and ownership decisions.
The [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) orders the remaining wrapper work around an indexed voxel mesh renderer, after completed general transfers and fence-backed submission.

## Verify changes

Run the generator check, proof gate, native examples, and negative integration checks:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py
```

To include address and undefined-behavior sanitizers:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize
```

The native checks include 32 alternating packed uploads copied through a device-local intermediate GPU buffer to literal readback bytes.
They reuse command/pool/fence objects, check stable row counts, and reject pending reset, destruction, mapping, and further submission before observing completion.
Separate checks cover fence status/wait/idle completion, retained references, stale/wrong-owner keys, and zero remaining objects after successful and accepted-pending failure scopes.
Native and interpreted probes read the returned upload array after success and rejection.

`tools/check_native.py` adds controlled dispatch/allocation probes only to emitted test C.
These exercise submit OOM/uncertainty, wait/idle/reset errors, map/flush failure ownership, metadata allocation failures, enumeration retries, composite ABI, private-fence isolation, and sticky device loss.
Injected results are distinct from real GPU execution. The tests never provoke hardware loss.
The sanitizer run includes those probes and the real repeated transfer test.
The verifier records queried device/layer output in `build/discovery.txt` and validation availability in `build/validation.txt`.
When Khronos validation is installed, it also runs the real GPU checks with synchronization validation enabled.
A missing driver or device fails native verification. It is not a passing skip.
Bend's pure laws live in `LAWS.bend`; their proofs live in `PROOF.bend`.
Before committing, run `bend PROOF.bend`. For the additional proof-kernel check, run `bend PROOF.bend --verdict`.
The laws cover pure functions. They do not verify C code, Vulkan drivers, or GPU execution.

`tools/bindings.json` defines the supported effects. `tools/generate.py` generates their Bend declarations, native registrations, JavaScript errors, and selected core constants from the checked-in Khronos registry extract.
Run `python3 tools/generate.py` after changing the manifest. The generator does not implement new native commands or translate arbitrary Vulkan structs.

The milestone-1 run on NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 passed `python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize`.
Khronos validation and synchronization validation were unavailable in that run.
Noncoherent cache paths have controlled flush-failure coverage. Their driver coverage depends on the selected memory type.
