Vulkan receives `bufferRowLength = row / B`, `bufferImageHeight = layer / row`, `imageOffset.z = 0`, and `imageExtent.depth = 1`. [Khronos buffer-image copy fields](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html).

The final span excludes trailing padding after the last written row/layer. A one-pixel region in a long row therefore does not require an unused entire row at the buffer's end. Bounds must use the checked final address, not `offset + row * height * layers`. Zero strides normalize before division, and positive extents prevent zero-divisor cases.

Buffer-to-image rejects overlapping destination image boxes in intersecting mip/layer selections. Image-to-buffer rejects overlapping destination buffer bounding intervals. Bounding intervals include interior padding, so a safe interleaving of two regions in padding may conservatively reject. Repeated source reads are allowed. Reject physical source/destination overlap using canonical binding identity and requirement intervals, including across regions. The no-image-alias binding rule makes that check conclusive despite opaque optimal tiling.

Clear ranges use the same aspect/mip/layer normalization and positive-count checks. Reject overlapping ranges within a clear call. Layout continuity is per entire cell. A subrectangle upload initializes only its rectangle, even though the cell's layout covers the complete subresource.

### Pixel and clear semantics

`ColorClear` represents floating-point RGBA values. UNORM conversion and sRGB encoding follow Vulkan format semantics. There is no UI packed-color convention. Color values can be finite values outside `[0,1]`; format conversion applies. Depth clear is finite and within `[0,1]`. Endpoint colors and binary-representable depth values make exact acceptance expectations possible.

Staging copies preserve numerical image coordinates. Rows advance in increasing image y, and layers advance by the explicit layer stride. The example defines row zero as its top row. Native code never flips rows or swizzles components. R8G8B8A8 bytes are R,G,B,A and B8G8R8A8 bytes are B,G,R,A. SRGB copies preserve stored encoded bytes. UNORM clear inputs are normalized values, and sRGB color conversion must be documented separately from byte storage. D32_SFLOAT readback is four-byte IEEE binary32 depth data. D16_UNORM readback is two-byte normalized unsigned depth data. The current platform remains 64-bit little-endian Linux.

It loses automatic stale-recording rejection and unknown-state enforcement. |

An explicit-layout-only wrapper cannot detect those cases without taking on the same responsibility. The shared old/new arguments preserve reviewable Vulkan intent and let the wrapper check it.

Bounds must use the checked final address, not `offset + row * height * layers`. Zero strides normalize before division, and positive extents prevent zero-divisor cases.

Buffer-to-image rejects overlapping destination image boxes in intersecting mip/layer selections. Image-to-buffer rejects overlapping destination buffer bounding intervals. Bounding intervals include interior padding, so a safe interleaving of two regions in padding may conservatively reject. Repeated source reads are allowed. Reject physical source/destination overlap using canonical binding identity and requirement intervals, including across regions. The no-image-alias binding rule makes that check conclusive despite opaque optimal tiling.

Clear ranges use the same aspect/mip/layer normalization and positive-count checks. Reject overlapping ranges within a clear call. Layout continuity is per entire cell. A subrectangle upload initializes only its rectangle, even though the cell's layout covers the complete subresource.

### Pixel and clear semantics

`ColorClear` represents floating-point RGBA values. UNORM conversion and sRGB encoding follow Vulkan format semantics. There is no UI packed-color convention. Color values can be finite values outside `[0,1]`; format conversion applies. Depth clear is finite and within `[0,1]`. Endpoint colors and binary-representable depth values make exact acceptance expectations possible.

Staging copies preserve numerical image coordinates. Rows advance in increasing image y, and layers advance by the explicit layer stride. The example defines row zero as its top row. Native code never flips rows or swizzles components. R8G8B8A8 bytes are R,G,B,A and B8G8R8A8 bytes are B,G,R,A. SRGB copies preserve stored encoded bytes. UNORM clear inputs are normalized values, and sRGB color conversion must be documented separately from byte storage. D32_SFLOAT readback is four-byte IEEE binary32 depth data. D16_UNORM readback is two-byte normalized unsigned depth data. The current platform remains 64-bit little-endian Linux.

Expected readback comparisons use independently specified bytes. They must not call the conversion helper that prepared upload values. Uniform clears alone do not prove orientation or row addressing.

### Installed Bend ABI gate

The new public data shapes do not prescribe a C field layout. Existing emitted C confirms that handles can be packed and nested single-constructor Data values flatten. It does not prove the new floats, unions, or nested regions. [Existing ABI explanation](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md).

Before implementing marshalling, emit a small dedicated Bend 2.0.37 probe that keeps every constructor live through real effects. Inspect and check the emitted argument and constructor layouts for ImageCreateInfo, ImageFormatInfo, view and barrier ranges, BufferImageCopy with three U64 fields, Rect2D, attachment descriptions, `Maybe` depth, and both AttachmentClear tags. Include separate ColorClear and DepthClear effects. Exercise packed and nonpacked/shared values where the compiler emits both. Check the actual argument positions in public effect dispatch as well as constructor storage.

Use color lanes `0.0`, `0.25`, `0.5`, and `1.0` in one value, then distinct values including negative zero in a second. Depth `0.5` must reach C as bits `0x3f000000`. Prove the runtime's float extraction with emitted evidence. Do not numerically cast a tagged Term to float. Native conversion into `VkClearColorValue` and `VkClearDepthStencilValue` is explicit. Compare native Vulkan struct sizes/offsets against installed headers where handwritten bridge data is involved. General C union size equality alone does not prove lane interpretation.

Preferred public semantics remain F32. If the installed compiler prevents reliable direct F32 handling, the smallest fallback is a pure public F32-to-IEEE-bits adapter feeding a private raw clear effect. Use a compiler-supported bit reinterpretation confirmed by the probe, not numeric `F32.to_u32`. Keep callers on the same F32 declarations. If neither route is available, publish an explicit `Float32Bits{bits:U32}` alternative only after documenting that experimentally established limitation. Do not replace general clear values with 0xRRGGBBAA or divide UI channels by 255.

Requirements and format-property U64 outputs use exact raw limb tuples and pure adapters. Every driver failure preserves `(uint32_t)(int32_t)VkResult`. The existing owned-array upload remains `Array<U32> & VkResult(Unit)` on every path, including JavaScript rejection, new image-alias rejection, and active-memory rejection. New command inputs use lists and retain no Bend heap pointer after the effect. Every early reject consumes or returns each input according to its existing ownership contract.

### Cleanup and migration

Scoped cleanup keeps the existing idle-first rule. Ordinary idle failures leave the unsafe remainder and Entry live for retry. Known loss allows ordered teardown and preserves exact loss bits. After an acceptable idle outcome, destroy pools/commands, fences, framebuffers, views, render passes, images and buffers, allocations, devices, physical rows, instances, and the loader. Views and passes can exchange order after framebuffers are gone. Each row removal frees its dependency edges and owned metadata. Completed plans never replay during destruction.

There is one public pipeline barrier operation. Add `images` as the last argument, update the manifest, regenerate declarations/registrations/JavaScript, and migrate every caller in the same unit. Add `[]` to the buffer-only calls in `examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend`, `tests/native.bend`, `tests/transfers.bend`, and `tests/repeated.bend`. Update `tests/probes.c` raw effect argument vectors and any injected function signatures. Update the API table and examples. Search all non-generated source for `pipeline_barrier` and `bv_cmd_pipeline_barrier` before committing. Do not retain the five-argument wrapper or add a separate legacy image barrier effect.

The graph migration also replaces every `bound`, binding `offset`, `uses`, `bv_memory_busy`, and direct reference helper access in production and emitted-C probes. Binding helpers retrieve the canonical edge. Existing M1 buffer alias and pending tests are retained and adapted. `tools/check_native.py` currently anchors injection on `bv_prepare_refs` and exact allocation text, so change that script and its probes together with the allocator migration. Count expected injection replacements and fail if an anchor silently disappears.

## Module and file changes

| File | Owned change |
| --- | --- |
| `Vulkan.bend` | New handles/configuration/value types and raw-result adapters. Generated effects reflect the manifest. |
| `src/native.c` | Canonical typed dependencies, image/pass/view/framebuffer contexts, plan transactions, completion/uncertainty/loss hooks, dispatch, and handwritten marshalling. Keep lifecycle decisions together instead of splitting them into forwarding modules. |
| `src/core.bend` | Pure checked copy-address calculations and a small pure observation/plan transition model for important laws. No registry or second mutable state. |
| `tools/bindings.json` | Approximately eighteen new effects plus the unified barrier signature change. Preserve the owned-array policy on the existing upload effect. |
| `tools/generate.py`, `registry/vk.xml`, `registry/README.md`, generated constants | Add core image type, tiling, usage, aspect, layout, view type, sample count, attachment load/store, and needed render-pass constants from the same pinned registry provenance. No hand-edited generated effect blocks. |
| `tests/image_abi.bend`, `tests/image_probes.c` | Emitted ABI checks and controlled allocation/dispatch/layout-state failures. New names are proposed. |
| `tests/images.bend`, `tests/render_targets.bend`, `examples/image_roundtrip.bend` | Real GPU transfer and color/depth attachment evidence, plus negative lifecycle/range/scope cases. |
| Existing tests and `tools/check_native.py` | Graph and barrier migration, fault-injection anchors, array ownership, old-suite regression coverage. |
| `tools/verify.py` | Run new real programs and controlled probes, extend ASan/UBSan execution to new paths, preserve generator freshness and old suites. |
| `LAWS.bend`, `PROOF.bend` | State and prove pure important invariants. Native dispatch still requires runtime evidence. |
| `docs/roadmap.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/api.md`, `README.md` | Move actual render-pass begin/end and attachment clears into M2, retain viewport/draw work in M3, describe the profile, observations, uncertainty, copy strides, byte order, and evidence limits. |

No shader, pipeline, vertex/index binding, draw, mesher, swapchain, surface, or presentation implementation belongs in these changes.

## Alternatives considered

| Whole design | Caller complexity | Hidden complexity | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit caller-owned layouts, canonical dependency graph | Caller must maintain image state across reset, execution, uncertainty, and recovery. Old/new layouts are accepted as assertions once structurally valid. | Graph lifetimes and checked marshalling remain native. No layout consistency state. | Viable and smaller. It loses automatic stale-recording rejection and unknown-state enforcement. |
| Command-local versioned ledger and canonical dependency graph | Caller provides explicit barriers and pass initial/final layouts, resets stale commands, and explicitly discards unknown contents. | Native code plans layouts, checks epochs, publishes only at completion, and handles uncertainty. | Selected. The existing one-active-submission rule makes the commit boundary precise. |
| Retained command stream compiled at submit, with flattened resource closure | Caller records abstract operations and can submit pre-recorded work against newer observations. | A second command representation, delayed validation, replay/compiler allocation, native command emission, and closure maintenance. | Rejected. It changes the immediate-effect contract, delays recoverable recording errors, and creates another representation of resources and commands. |

The selected ledger genuinely changes who owns cross-command layout knowledge. The wrapper rejects a stale preserving command, rejects reads from Unknown, and owns recovery knowledge. An explicit-layout-only wrapper cannot detect those cases without taking on the same responsibility. The shared old/new arguments preserve reviewable Vulkan intent and let the wrapper check it.

A completion-only ledger without observed cells cannot validate the next recording. An eagerly updated global layout cannot survive reset or failed submission. Both incomplete variants fail the contract. The smallest viable revision is the selected split between observed cells and proposed command entries, with epochs and no-allocation publication.

## Tradeoffs accepted

item.stdout:
# Milestone 2 with typed dependencies and flat command retention

This candidate gives library callers explicit Vulkan 1.0 image operations and preserves the milestone 1 submission guarantees. Maintainers get typed persistent dependencies and a command-owned set of every retained resource. Host-access checks never walk a resource graph.

This is a proposed design, not an implementation or a test result. The only executed Bend command in this design task was informational `bend guide`. No repository files or git state were changed. No builds, tests, or other agents were run. All new source signatures below are proposed. The snippets use the existing `V.Action` result monad and `W` from upstream bend-collections.

## Usage first

### Create an offscreen image and its view

The caller has selected a physical device, a graphics queue, and its logical device. `choose` is the example-local fallible memory-type selector already used in `examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend`. The caller runs this inside `Entry.with` so intermediate failures receive scoped cleanup.

```python
def target(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice,
	+device: V.Device) -> V.Action(V.Image & (V.DeviceMemory & V.ImageView)):
	+usage = U32.or(vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT(),
		U32.or(vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT(),
			vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT()))
	+format = vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM()
	do V.Action<V.Image & (V.DeviceMemory & V.ImageView)>:
		properties : V.ImageFormatProperties <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_image_format_properties(
			instance, physical, V.ImageFormatQuery{format,
				vk.VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D(), vk.VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL(), usage, 0})
		+image : V.Image <- V.Device.create_image(device,
			V.ImageCreateInfo{format, V.Extent2D{4, 3}, 1, 1, usage})
		req : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device, image)
		V.MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, bits} = req
		types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)
		index : U32 <- choose(Core.find_memory_type(types, bits,
			vk.VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT()), "No image memory type")
		+memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device, size, index)
		V.Device.bind_image_memory(device, image, memory, W.zero())
		view : V.ImageView <- V.Device.create_image_view(device,
			V.ImageViewCreateInfo{image, vk.VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D(),
				V.ImageSubresourceRange{vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT(), 0, 1, 0, 1}})
		return (image, (memory, view))
```

The properties query exposes configuration support and limits. Creation independently checks its exact configuration, extent, mip count, and layer count. No caller-created support token can bypass the checked native boundary.

### Clear, transfer, observe completion, and read raw bytes

Here `command` is Initial, `fence` is unsignaled, the image is the 4 by 3 RGBA target above, and the bound readback buffer has at least 48 bytes. Its allocation is host-visible. UNDEFINED is legitimate because this call discards the target's previous contents.

```python
def clear_read(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer,
	+image: V.Image, +buffer: V.Buffer, +memory: V.DeviceMemory,
	+fence: V.Fence) -> V.Action(List<U32>):
	+top = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT()
	+transfer = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT()
	+host = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT()
	+transfer_write = vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT()
	+transfer_read = vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()
	+host_read = vk.VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT()
	+undefined = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED()
	+transfer_dst = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL()
	+transfer_src = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL()
	+color = vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT()
	+color_range = V.ImageSubresourceRange{color, 0, 1, 0, 1}
	do V.Action<List<U32>>:
		V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, top, transfer, [], [],
			[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, undefined, transfer_dst,
				color_range, 0, transfer_write}])
		V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, transfer_dst,
			V.ClearColor{1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0}, [color_range])
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, transfer, transfer, [], [],
			[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, transfer_dst, transfer_src,
				color_range, transfer_write, transfer_read}])
		V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, image, transfer_src, buffer,
			[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(), 0, 0,
				V.ImageSubresourceLayers{color, 0, 0, 1},
				V.Offset2D{0, 0}, V.Extent2D{4, 3}}])
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, transfer, host,
			[V.MemoryBarrier{transfer_write, host_read}], [], [])
		V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
		V.Device.submit(device, command, fence)
		status : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence, Core.whole_size())
		require(U32.is_eq(status, vk.VK_SUCCESS()), "Fence did not complete")
		bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 48)
		V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
		V.Fence.reset(fence)
		return bytes
```

`require` is example-local, as in the current buffer example. Every group of four returned bytes must equal `[255,0,0,255]`. Reading follows a successful completion observation and the existing noncoherent invalidation path. A timeout never licenses host access. Successful reset releases retention but does not alter an image layout.

### Clear color and depth through a real render pass

`color_view` and `depth_view` select one mip and one layer of bound RGBA8 and D32_SFLOAT images. The caller first checks D32 configuration support. It uses D16 if D32 is unavailable. ```python

	+device: V.Device) -> V.Action(V.Image & (V.DeviceMemory & V.ImageView)):
	+usage = U32.or(vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT(),
		U32.or(vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT(),
			vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT()))
	+format = vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM()
	do V.Action<V.Image & (V.DeviceMemory & V.ImageView)>:
		properties : V.ImageFormatProperties <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_image_format_properties(
			instance, physical, V.ImageFormatQuery{format,
				vk.VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D(), vk.VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL(), usage, 0})

		types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)
		index : U32 <- choose(Core.find_memory_type(types, bits,
			vk.VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT()), "No image memory type")
		+memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device, size, index)

Here `command` is Initial, `fence` is unsignaled, the image is the 4 by 3 RGBA target above, and the bound readback buffer has at least 48 bytes. Its allocation is host-visible. UNDEFINED is legitimate because this call discards the target's previous contents.

```python

	+image: V.Image, +buffer: V.Buffer, +memory: V.DeviceMemory,
	+fence: V.Fence) -> V.Action(List<U32>):
	+top = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT()
	+transfer = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT()
	+host = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT()
	+transfer_write = vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT()
	+transfer_read = vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()
	+host_read = vk.VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT()
	+undefined = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED()
	+transfer_dst = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL()
	+transfer_src = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL()
	+color = vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT()
	+color_range = V.ImageSubresourceRange{color, 0, 1, 0, 1}
	do V.Action<List<U32>>:
		V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, top, transfer, [], [],
			[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, undefined, transfer_dst,
				color_range, 0, transfer_write}])
		V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, transfer_dst,
			V.ClearColor{1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0}, [color_range])
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, transfer, transfer, [], [],
			[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, transfer_dst, transfer_src,
				color_range, transfer_write, transfer_read}])
		V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, image, transfer_src, buffer,
			[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(), 0, 0,
				V.ImageSubresourceLayers{color, 0, 0, 1},
				V.Offset2D{0, 0}, V.Extent2D{4, 3}}])
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, transfer, host,
			[V.MemoryBarrier{transfer_write, host_read}], [], [])
		V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
		V.Device.submit(device, command, fence)
		status : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence, Core.whole_size())
		require(U32.is_eq(status, vk.VK_SUCCESS()), "Fence did not complete")
		bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 48)
		V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
		V.Fence.reset(fence)
		return bytes

# Milestone 2 with typed dependencies and flat command retention

This candidate gives library callers explicit Vulkan 1.0 image operations and preserves the milestone 1 submission guarantees. Maintainers get typed persistent dependencies and a command-owned set of every retained resource. Host-access checks never walk a resource graph.

This is a proposed design, not an implementation or a test result. The only executed Bend command in this design task was informational `bend guide`. No repository files or git state were changed. No builds, tests, or other agents were run. All new source signatures below are proposed. The snippets use the existing `V.Action` result monad and `W` from upstream bend-collections.

## Usage first

### Create an offscreen image and its view

The caller has selected a physical device, a graphics queue, and its logical device. `choose` is the example-local fallible memory-type selector already used in `examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend`. The caller runs this inside `Entry.with` so intermediate failures receive scoped cleanup.

```python
def target(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice,
	+device: V.Device) -> V.Action(V.Image & (V.DeviceMemory & V.ImageView)):
	+usage = U32.or(vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT(),
		U32.or(vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT(),
			vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT()))
	+format = vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM()
	do V.Action<V.Image & (V.DeviceMemory & V.ImageView)>:
		properties : V.ImageFormatProperties <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_image_format_properties(
			instance, physical, V.ImageFormatQuery{format,
				vk.VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D(), vk.VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL(), usage, 0})
		+image : V.Image <- V.Device.create_image(device,
			V.ImageCreateInfo{format, V.Extent2D{4, 3}, 1, 1, usage})
		req : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device, image)
		V.MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, bits} = req
		types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance, physical)
		index : U32 <- choose(Core.find_memory_type(types, bits,
			vk.VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT()), "No image memory type")
		+memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device, size, index)
		V.Device.bind_image_memory(device, image, memory, W.zero())
		view : V.ImageView <- V.Device.create_image_view(device,
			V.ImageViewCreateInfo{image, vk.VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D(),
				V.ImageSubresourceRange{vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT(), 0, 1, 0, 1}})
		return (image, (memory, view))
```

The properties query exposes configuration support and limits. Creation independently checks its exact configuration, extent, mip count, and layer count. No caller-created support token can bypass the checked native boundary.

### Clear, transfer, observe completion, and read raw bytes

Here `command` is Initial, `fence` is unsignaled, the image is the 4 by 3 RGBA target above, and the bound readback buffer has at least 48 bytes. Its allocation is host-visible. UNDEFINED is legitimate because this call discards the target's previous contents.

```python
def clear_read(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer,
	+image: V.Image, +buffer: V.Buffer, +memory: V.DeviceMemory,
	+fence: V.Fence) -> V.Action(List<U32>):
	+top = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT()
	+transfer = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT()
	+host = vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT()
	+transfer_write = vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT()
	+transfer_read = vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()
	+host_read = vk.VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT()
	+undefined = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED()
	+transfer_dst = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL()
	+transfer_src = vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL()
	+color = vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT()
	+color_range = V.ImageSubresourceRange{color, 0, 1, 0, 1}
	do V.Action<List<U32>>:
		V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, top, transfer, [], [],
			[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, undefined, transfer_dst,
				color_range, 0, transfer_write}])
		V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, transfer_dst,
			V.ClearColor{1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0}, [color_range])
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, transfer, transfer, [], [],
			[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, transfer_dst, transfer_src,
				color_range, transfer_write, transfer_read}])
		V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, image, transfer_src, buffer,
			[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(), 0, 0,
				V.ImageSubresourceLayers{color, 0, 0, 1},
				V.Offset2D{0, 0}, V.Extent2D{4, 3}}])
		V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, transfer, host,
			[V.MemoryBarrier{transfer_write, host_read}], [], [])
		V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
		V.Device.submit(device, command, fence)
		status : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence, Core.whole_size())
		require(U32.is_eq(status, vk.VK_SUCCESS()), "Fence did not complete")
		bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), 48)
		V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
		V.Fence.reset(fence)
		return bytes
```

`require` is example-local, as in the current buffer example. Every group of four returned bytes must equal `[255,0,0,255]`. Reading follows a successful completion observation and the existing noncoherent invalidation path. A timeout never licenses host access. Successful reset releases retention but does not alter an image layout.

### Clear color and depth through a real render pass

`color_view` and `depth_view` select one mip and one layer of bound RGBA8 and D32_SFLOAT images. The caller first checks D32 configuration support. It uses D16 if D32 is unavailable. Two ordinary `pipeline_barrier` image entries explicitly transition the corresponding images to color-attachment and depth-stencil-attachment layouts before this snippet. Those barriers target color-output and both early and late fragment-test stages with attachment-write access.

```python
def render_clear(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer,
	color_view: V.ImageView, depth_view: V.ImageView) ->
	V.Action(V.RenderPass & V.Framebuffer):
	do V.Action<V.RenderPass & V.Framebuffer>:
		+pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,
			V.RenderPassCreateInfo{
				[V.ColorAttachment{vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM(),
					V.ClearLoad{}, V.Store{}}],
				Some{V.DepthAttachment{vk.VK_FORMAT_D32_SFLOAT(),
					V.ClearLoad{}, V.Store{}}}})
		+framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,
			V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass, [color_view, depth_view],
				V.Extent2D{4, 3}, 1})
		V.CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command, framebuffer,
			V.RenderArea{V.Offset2D{0, 0}, V.Extent2D{4, 3}},
			[V.ColorClear{V.ClearColor{0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0}}, V.DepthClear{0.5}])
		V.CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)
		return (pass, framebuffer)
```

The command is already Recording Outside. After the snippet the caller records explicit attachment-write to transfer-read image barriers, copies both attachments, ends, submits, and waits. D32 depth bytes must encode `0x3f000000`. The render-pass description holds no initial or final layout options. Both equal that attachment's fixed attachment-optimal layout. The framebuffer supplies its render pass to begin, so the public call cannot pass a second incompatible render pass.

## Problem and evidence

The local wrapper's authoritative state is its checked native registry and command submission state. Handles are copyable registry keys, so checks remain native even when Bend types differ. `bv_prepare_refs` stages direct references before void commands. `bv_memory_busy` currently follows only a direct allocation reference or one `bound` pointer. `bv_referenced` scans direct references. These mechanisms cannot infer framebuffer to view to image to allocation protection without a new representation. See [native registry and reference code](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/src/native.c:17) and [local grounding](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-local.md).

The existing command phase owns Pending and Uncertain associations. Fence success or successful device idle is the completion observation. Retention survives completion and failed resets. The new design preserves these rules. It adds no pending count, device busy flag, fence backpointer, or global layout value. See [shared explanation](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md).

The pinned Voltra reference contributes the explicit create, requirements, allocate, bind, view, staging, and independent pixel-check sequence. Its Vulkan 1.3 dynamic rendering, U32 sizes, swizzles, and weaker ownership are excluded. This design was grounded in its [target creation](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/voltra/gpu.bend:306), [readback](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/voltra/gpu.bend:1236), and [barrier policy](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/voltra/commands.bend:115), plus the full [Voltra exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-voltra.md). No implementation is copied.

The [shared task](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/design-task.md) and [framing](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md) require executable color and depth render-pass clears in milestone 2. Begin and end move out of the milestone 3 roadmap list. Shaders, pipelines, draws, meshing, and presentation remain later work.

## Whole designs compared

| Whole shape | Persistent dependencies | Command dependencies | Layout responsibility | Main cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Selected typed dependencies with flat retention | Fixed typed fields and immutable attachment arrays. Binding is one-way. | Each recorded command owns a deduplicated complete set. Expansion follows the known type shape once at recording. | Caller supplies old and new layouts and execution-time copy layouts. | Recording allocates and stores more references. |
| Generic direct DAG with traversal | Every resource stores generic direct `BvUse` edges. Bind, view, and framebuffer construction publish edges. | Command stores only direct roots. Host-busy and destruction queries follow reachability. | Caller supplies layouts. | Traversal needs recursion or scratch storage, cycle policy, and fallible query behavior. |
| Owned offscreen-target aggregate with command-local layouts | A target owns image, memory, view, pass, and framebuffer as one object. | Command retains targets and buffers. A transition ledger follows target subresources. | Recording checks a local ledger, and submit reconciles preconditions and completion. | It hides Vulkan setup but exposes a second ownership path when callers need independent image, view, and pass handles. |

The direct DAG is viable, but loses for this milestone. It makes each resource extension uniform while making each safety query harder. Persistent destruction only needs incoming direct references. Host access needs allocation reachability under active submission, including all attachments. A general graph makes these different queries depend on a shared traversal mechanism. An allocation failure during a safety query cannot be allowed to turn protection off.

The aggregate design has the deepest convenience interface, but it fails the intended explicit wrapper boundary. It either omits the four independent handle lifecycles or supports both independent and aggregate owners. Its layout ledger also needs submit preconditions, uncertainty handling, and ownership of observations. That work is unnecessary to meet the explicit Vulkan API contract.

The selected interface hides marshalling, compatibility checks, dependency expansion, rollback, and active-allocation protection. Callers retain responsibility for synchronization and initialization. The API remains close enough to Vulkan for the next indexed graphics stage to add pipeline and draw commands without replacing image ownership.

## Supported image profile

The following limits are deliberate milestone 2 policy, enforced before unsafe Vulkan calls.

| Property | Accepted profile |
|---|---|
| Type and dimensions | 2D, positive width and height, depth fixed at one. Dimensions must fit queried image and framebuffer limits where applicable. |
| Mips and layers | Positive explicit counts. Mips cannot exceed the full mip chain or queried limits. Array layers must fit queried limits. |
| Samples and tiling | One sample, optimal tiling. No direct image mapping. |
| Formats | R8G8B8A8_UNORM, B8G8R8A8_UNORM, R8G8B8A8_SRGB, B8G8R8A8_SRGB, D16_UNORM, and D32_SFLOAT, each conditional on driver support for the complete requested usage. |
| Usages | TRANSFER_SRC, TRANSFER_DST, SAMPLED, COLOR_ATTACHMENT, and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT. Nonzero, no unknown bits. Color and depth attachment usage must match the format class. SAMPLED is useful for later work, without adding descriptors now. |
| Flags and sharing | Flags zero, exclusive sharing on the selected queue. Initial layout UNDEFINED. No sparse, aliasing flags, protected, mutable-format, cube, or external images. |
| Aspects | Exactly COLOR for the four color formats or DEPTH for the two depth formats. No stencil, compressed, packed depth-stencil, or multiplanar formats. |
| Views | Same format as the image, identity component mapping, 2D or 2D_ARRAY. Explicit positive range counts. A 2D view has one layer. A framebuffer view has exactly one mip. |
| Framebuffers | Positive width, height, and layers within every view's selected mip and layer range and physical limits. Multiple colors up to maxColorAttachments and optional depth. At least one attachment. |
| Render pass | One graphics subpass, single-sample colors, optional single-sample depth, no resolves, input attachments, preserves, or subpass changes. |

This profile supports the next non-MSAA indexed color and depth stage. More formats can extend the native traits table. 1D, 3D, cube, MSAA, stencil, and mutable views require explicit feature work, not pretend support through unchecked constants.

One native format-traits table owns the six supported formats, aspect, texel bytes, numeric class, and encoding. It uses generated enum constants. No second Bend whitelist or copied per-view traits are maintained. Querying other valid Vulkan 1.0 configurations is allowed by the generic query effect. A successful query does not promise that wrapper creation implements that broader profile.

## Problem and evidence

The local wrapper's authoritative state is its checked native registry and command submission state. Handles are copyable registry keys, so checks remain native even when Bend types differ. `bv_prepare_refs` stages direct references before void commands. `bv_memory_busy` currently follows only a direct allocation reference or one `bound` pointer. `bv_referenced` scans direct references. These mechanisms cannot infer framebuffer to view to image to allocation protection without a new representation. See [native registry and reference code](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/src/native.c:17) and [local grounding](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-local.md).

The existing command phase owns Pending and Uncertain associations. Fence success or successful device idle is the completion observation. Retention survives completion and failed resets. The new design preserves these rules. It adds no pending count, device busy flag, fence backpointer, or global layout value. See [shared explanation](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md).

The pinned Voltra reference contributes the explicit create, requirements, allocate, bind, view, staging, and independent pixel-check sequence. Its Vulkan 1.3 dynamic rendering, U32 sizes, swizzles, and weaker ownership are excluded. This design was grounded in its [target creation](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/voltra/gpu.bend:306), [readback](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/voltra/gpu.bend:1236), and [barrier policy](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/voltra/commands.bend:115), plus the full [Voltra exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-voltra.md). No implementation is copied.

The [shared task](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/design-task.md) and [framing](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md) require executable color and depth render-pass clears in milestone 2. Begin and end move out of the milestone 3 roadmap list. Shaders, pipelines, draws, meshing, and presentation remain later work.

## Whole designs compared

| Whole shape | Persistent dependencies | Command dependencies | Layout responsibility | Main cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Selected typed dependencies with flat retention | Fixed typed fields and immutable attachment arrays. Binding is one-way. | Each recorded command owns a deduplicated complete set. Expansion follows the known type shape once at recording. | Caller supplies old and new layouts and execution-time copy layouts. | Recording allocates and stores more references. |
| Generic direct DAG with traversal | Every resource stores generic direct `BvUse` edges. Bind, view, and framebuffer construction publish edges. | Command stores only direct roots. Host-busy and destruction queries follow reachability. | Caller supplies layouts. | Traversal needs recursion or scratch storage, cycle policy, and fallible query behavior. |
| Owned offscreen-target aggregate with command-local layouts | A target owns image, memory, view, pass, and framebuffer as one object. | Command retains targets and buffers. A transition ledger follows target subresources. | Recording checks a local ledger, and submit reconciles preconditions and completion. | It hides Vulkan setup but exposes a second ownership path when callers need independent image, view, and pass handles. |

The direct DAG is viable, but loses for this milestone. It makes each resource extension uniform while making each safety query harder. Persistent destruction only needs incoming direct references. Host access needs allocation reachability under active submission, including all attachments. A general graph makes these different queries depend on a shared traversal mechanism. An allocation failure during a safety query cannot be allowed to turn protection off.

The aggregate design has the deepest convenience interface, but it fails the intended explicit wrapper boundary. It either omits the four independent handle lifecycles or supports both independent and aggregate owners. Its layout ledger also needs submit preconditions, uncertainty handling, and ownership of observations. That work is unnecessary to meet the explicit Vulkan API contract.

The selected interface hides marshalling, compatibility checks, dependency expansion, rollback, and active-allocation protection. Callers retain responsibility for synchronization and initialization. The API remains close enough to Vulkan for the next indexed graphics stage to add pipeline and draw commands without replacing image ownership.

## Supported image profile

The following limits are deliberate milestone 2 policy, enforced before unsafe Vulkan calls.

| Property | Accepted profile |
|---|---|
| Type and dimensions | 2D, positive width and height, depth fixed at one. Dimensions must fit queried image and framebuffer limits where applicable. |
| Mips and layers | Positive explicit counts. Mips cannot exceed the full mip chain or queried limits. Array layers must fit queried limits. |
| Samples and tiling | One sample, optimal tiling. No direct image mapping. |
| Formats | R8G8B8A8_UNORM, B8G8R8A8_UNORM, R8G8B8A8_SRGB, B8G8R8A8_SRGB, D16_UNORM, and D32_SFLOAT, each conditional on driver support for the complete requested usage. |
| Usages | TRANSFER_SRC, TRANSFER_DST, SAMPLED, COLOR_ATTACHMENT, and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT. Nonzero, no unknown bits. Color and depth attachment usage must match the format class. SAMPLED is useful for later work, without adding descriptors now. |
| Flags and sharing | Flags zero, exclusive sharing on the selected queue. Initial layout UNDEFINED. No sparse, aliasing flags, protected, mutable-format, cube, or external images. |
| Aspects | Exactly COLOR for the four color formats or DEPTH for the two depth formats. No stencil, compressed, packed depth-stencil, or multiplanar formats. |
| Views | Same format as the image, identity component mapping, 2D or 2D_ARRAY. Explicit positive range counts. A 2D view has one layer. A framebuffer view has exactly one mip. |
| Framebuffers | Positive width, height, and layers within every view's selected mip and layer range and physical limits. Multiple colors up to maxColorAttachments and optional depth. At least one attachment. |
| Render pass | One graphics subpass, single-sample colors, optional single-sample depth, no resolves, input attachments, preserves, or subpass changes. |

This profile supports the next non-MSAA indexed color and depth stage. More formats can extend the native traits table. 1D, 3D, cube, MSAA, stencil, and mutable views require explicit feature work, not pretend support through unchecked constants.

One native format-traits table owns the six supported formats, aspect, texel bytes, numeric class, and encoding. It uses generated enum constants. No second Bend whitelist or copied per-view traits are maintained. Querying other valid Vulkan 1.0 configurations is allowed by the generic query effect. A successful query does not promise that wrapper creation implements that broader profile.

## Tagged render state and compatibility

Recording scope lives only inside the Recording command-state variant. Pending and Uncertain continue to own only their existing fence association. Retention lives outside the variant because it survives every phase until successful reset or pool destruction. The active framebuffer pointer inside the scope is recording context, not a second ownership edge.

| Trigger | Valid state | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Begin command | Initial | Driver success enters Recording Outside. Failure enters Invalid. |
| Begin render pass | Recording Outside | Stage complete framebuffer retention, dispatch `CmdBeginRenderPass` INLINE, enter Recording Inside. |
| Nested begin | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch or metadata change. |
| End render pass | Recording Inside | Dispatch `CmdEndRenderPass`, return to Outside. Retention stays. |
| Unmatched end render pass | Any state other than Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier | Recording Outside | Validate, marshal, stage retention, dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. This subset has no subpass-local barriers. |
| End command inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME. Caller may end the pass or reset. |
| End command outside | Recording Outside | Driver success enters Executable. Failure enters Invalid with retention intact. |
| Reset | Healthy device and any nonactive command state, including Recording Inside | Success enters Initial and frees retention. Driver failure enters Invalid and preserves retention. |
| Submit and completion | Existing Executable, Pending, Uncertain rules | Existing machinery remains authoritative. Completion retains resources. |
| Device loss | Any phase | Sticky Lost and Invalid commands, association cleared as now, retention preserved until pool destruction or scoped teardown. Reset returns exact loss bits. |

Resetting an unsubmitted Recording Inside command discards its recording without issuing a synthetic end-render-pass. It follows native `vkResetCommandBuffer` rules. An ordinary argument failure never poisons an otherwise valid recording.

Submission success enters Pending. Submit OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY or OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY leaves Executable and the fence unchanged. Unexpected submit errors enter Uncertain. A Pending fence SUCCESS enters Completed. NOT_READY, TIMEOUT, and ordinary observation errors preserve Pending and protection. Uncertain rejects fence observation. Successful device idle changes Pending to Completed and Uncertain to Invalid. None of these observations releases retention. Active associations continue to block command reset, affected pool destruction, fence reset or destruction, and another submission on that device.

layer_stride = I * row_stride

| Addressing and orientation | Fill an upload buffer with asymmetric position-coded RGBA bytes. Copy a 3 by 2 region at nonzero image offset (1,1) into a larger initialized image using buffer offset 12, row length 7, image height 5, and two layers when supported. Use a distinct padded readback layout. Assert literal expected pixels at every image coordinate and untouched padding sentinels. | Persistent lifetime chain | Without commands, a framebuffer blocks pass and view destruction, a view blocks image destruction, and a bound image blocks memory free. Destroy framebuffer, then pass/views, then images, then memory successfully. Wrong order makes no driver destructor call. |
| Command chain retention | Record only begin/end of the framebuffer, then try destroying framebuffer, pass, view, image, and memory before submit, after completion, after failed reset, and after successful reset. ## Tagged render state and compatibility

Recording scope lives only inside the Recording command-state variant. Pending and Uncertain continue to own only their existing fence association. Retention lives outside the variant because it survives every phase until successful reset or pool destruction. The active framebuffer pointer inside the scope is recording context, not a second ownership edge.

| Trigger | Valid state | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Begin command | Initial | Driver success enters Recording Outside. Failure enters Invalid. |
| Begin render pass | Recording Outside | Stage complete framebuffer retention, dispatch `CmdBeginRenderPass` INLINE, enter Recording Inside. |
| Nested begin | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch or metadata change. |
| End render pass | Recording Inside | Dispatch `CmdEndRenderPass`, return to Outside. Retention stays. |
| Unmatched end render pass | Any state other than Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier | Recording Outside | Validate, marshal, stage retention, dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. This subset has no subpass-local barriers. |
| End command inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME. Caller may end the pass or reset. |
| End command outside | Recording Outside | Driver success enters Executable. Failure enters Invalid with retention intact. |
| Reset | Healthy device and any nonactive command state, including Recording Inside | Success enters Initial and frees retention. Driver failure enters Invalid and preserves retention. |
| Submit and completion | Existing Executable, Pending, Uncertain rules | Existing machinery remains authoritative. Completion retains resources. |
| Device loss | Any phase | Sticky Lost and Invalid commands, association cleared as now, retention preserved until pool destruction or scoped teardown. Reset returns exact loss bits. |

Resetting an unsubmitted Recording Inside command discards its recording without issuing a synthetic end-render-pass. It follows native `vkResetCommandBuffer` rules. An ordinary argument failure never poisons an otherwise valid recording.

Submission success enters Pending. Submit OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY or OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY leaves Executable and the fence unchanged. Unexpected submit errors enter Uncertain. A Pending fence SUCCESS enters Completed. NOT_READY, TIMEOUT, and ordinary observation errors preserve Pending and protection. Uncertain rejects fence observation. Successful device idle changes Pending to Completed and Uncertain to Invalid. None of these observations releases retention. Active associations continue to block command reset, affected pool destruction, fence reset or destruction, and another submission on that device.

It creates one graphics subpass and no explicit subpass dependencies. The caller's outside barriers establish attachment synchronization. No automatic layout transitions are exposed through render-pass options.

Framebuffer construction checks exact attachment count, order, format, samples, and device. Every color view needs COLOR_ATTACHMENT usage and COLOR aspect. Optional depth needs DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT usage and DEPTH aspect. Every view selects one mip. Each selected mip is at least framebuffer extent and each view supplies enough layers. Each attachment must be bound. Reject any pair of attachments that selects overlapping mip and layer subresources of the same image. Different images cannot overlap memory by binding policy.

## U64 addressing, regions, queue checks, and allocations

All arithmetic uses checked uint64_t operations after U64 limb decoding. Narrowing to Vulkan U32 stride fields occurs only from their declared U32 fields. Format byte sizes come from the single native traits table. D16 uses two bytes per depth texel and D32 uses four. The four RGBA and BGRA formats use four bytes. There is no inferred physical row pitch for optimal-tiled images.

For one BufferImageCopy, let `O` be buffer_offset, `B` texel bytes, `W,H` copy extent, `L` layer_count, `R` the nonzero buffer_row_length or W, and `I` the nonzero buffer_image_height or H. Require W,H,L positive, R at least W, and I at least H. Compute these values with checked operations.

```text
row_stride   = R * B
layer_stride = I * row_stride
span         = (L - 1) * layer_stride + (H - 1) * row_stride + W * B
end          = O + span
```

The last copied row contributes its actual bytes, not a full padded stride. Require end within the buffer's logical size and binding allocation bounds. Keep row_stride at most INT32_MAX as a conservative supported-copy limit. Add the buffer binding offset with checked arithmetic before allocation-relative comparisons. Raw U64 overflow returns BV_ARGUMENT and never wraps. Neither `optimalBufferCopyRowPitchAlignment` nor `optimalBufferCopyOffsetAlignment` is treated as a mandatory Vulkan alignment rule.

Require buffer_offset divisible by four for all supported copies. This deliberately applies one conservative rule even for D16 on graphics. Require mip index and layer range in bounds. Compute each selected mip dimension as max(1, base dimension shifted by mip), without an unchecked shift. Image offset and extent must fit that mip using subtraction-based or checked bounds. Copy aspect matches the format. Buffer and image usages match direction. All resources share the command's device and are bound.

The selected queue must support transfers. Cache its actual minImageTransferGranularity. For (0,0,0), accept only whole-mip x, y, and z offset and extent. For positive granularity, require aligned offsets and extent multiples, allowing the documented edge exception independently per axis. Our 2D z is zero and depth is one, which still needs the z edge check. Require GRAPHICS for any depth copy in either direction and for clear_depth_image. Require GRAPHICS or COMPUTE for clear_color_image. Transfer-only color copies are supported when granularity permits them. These checks preserve the Vulkan 1.0 queue rules without relying on later maintenance features. See [queue granularity](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkQueueFamilyProperties.html), [color-clear queue support](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearColorImage.html), and [depth-clear requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage.html).

Copy lists must be nonempty and have at most 4096 regions. Detect overlapping destination image boxes when mip, aspect, and layer ranges overlap. Detect overlapping destination buffer spans for image readback. The buffer check conservatively treats row and layer padding within the computed envelope as occupied. Source overlap is permitted, provided destination regions do not overlap. Within one clear call, reject overlapping subresource ranges. All checks and allocations complete before dispatch. Vulkan's region fields express row length and image height in texels, not bytes. See [VkBufferImageCopy](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html).

### Shared-allocation policy

Keep existing legal buffer-to-buffer aliasing and existing copy-buffer allocation-relative overlap checks. Introduce this policy in both bind_image_memory and bind_buffer_memory.

1. Use native memory requirement size, not logical buffer size or width times height, as the reserved binding interval.
2. If either member of an existing/new pair is an image, reject overlapping reserved byte intervals. Images cannot alias buffers or other images in this subset.
3. For a buffer and an optimal image in the same allocation, additionally require disjoint bufferImageGranularity pages. With granularity G and reserved interval [offset,end), the occupied pages are [offset/G,(end-1)/G]. Compare by division, avoiding round-up overflow.
4. Two nonoverlapping optimal images need no extra buffer-to-optimal page separation in this profile. Two buffers retain the milestone 1 policy.

Scan the already bound rows of the same allocation before either bind. Check memory type bits and requirement alignment separately. Driver bind failure leaves no persistent binding record. Since a buffer and image cannot occupy the same bytes, source-destination memory aliasing is ruled out before either buffer-image copy, even though optimal image storage cannot be described by linear row addresses. Shared but disjoint allocations remain useful. Host exclusion is intentionally whole-allocation, so an active image also blocks host access through a disjoint bound buffer in that allocation.

The `bufferImageGranularity` rule separates linear resource and optimal image placements. See the Khronos [buffer-image granularity rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/resources.html#resources-bufferimagegranularity). The explicit image nonalias policy is stronger wrapper policy and does not claim all Vulkan-valid aliasing is supported.

## Tagged render state and compatibility

Recording scope lives only inside the Recording command-state variant. Pending and Uncertain continue to own only their existing fence association. Retention lives outside the variant because it survives every phase until successful reset or pool destruction. The active framebuffer pointer inside the scope is recording context, not a second ownership edge.

| Trigger | Valid state | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Begin command | Initial | Driver success enters Recording Outside. Failure enters Invalid. |
| Begin render pass | Recording Outside | Stage complete framebuffer retention, dispatch `CmdBeginRenderPass` INLINE, enter Recording Inside. |
| Nested begin | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch or metadata change. |
| End render pass | Recording Inside | Dispatch `CmdEndRenderPass`, return to Outside. Retention stays. |
| Unmatched end render pass | Any state other than Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier | Recording Outside | Validate, marshal, stage retention, dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. This subset has no subpass-local barriers. |
| End command inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME. Caller may end the pass or reset. |
| End command outside | Recording Outside | Driver success enters Executable. Failure enters Invalid with retention intact. |
| Reset | Healthy device and any nonactive command state, including Recording Inside | Success enters Initial and frees retention. Driver failure enters Invalid and preserves retention. |
| Submit and completion | Existing Executable, Pending, Uncertain rules | Existing machinery remains authoritative. Completion retains resources. |
| Device loss | Any phase | Sticky Lost and Invalid commands, association cleared as now, retention preserved until pool destruction or scoped teardown. Reset returns exact loss bits. |

Resetting an unsubmitted Recording Inside command discards its recording without issuing a synthetic end-render-pass. It follows native `vkResetCommandBuffer` rules. An ordinary argument failure never poisons an otherwise valid recording.

Submission success enters Pending. Submit OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY or OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY leaves Executable and the fence unchanged. Unexpected submit errors enter Uncertain. A Pending fence SUCCESS enters Completed. NOT_READY, TIMEOUT, and ordinary observation errors preserve Pending and protection. Uncertain rejects fence observation. Successful device idle changes Pending to Completed and Uncertain to Invalid. None of these observations releases retention. Active associations continue to block command reset, affected pool destruction, fence reset or destruction, and another submission on that device.

It creates one graphics subpass and no explicit subpass dependencies. The caller's outside barriers establish attachment synchronization. No automatic layout transitions are exposed through render-pass options.

Optional depth needs DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT usage and DEPTH aspect. Every view selects one mip. Each selected mip is at least framebuffer extent and each view supplies enough layers. ## U64 addressing, regions, queue checks, and allocations

All arithmetic uses checked uint64_t operations after U64 limb decoding. Narrowing to Vulkan U32 stride fields occurs only from their declared U32 fields. Format byte sizes come from the single native traits table. D16 uses two bytes per depth texel and D32 uses four. The four RGBA and BGRA formats use four bytes. There is no inferred physical row pitch for optimal-tiled images.

For one BufferImageCopy, let `O` be buffer_offset, `B` texel bytes, `W,H` copy extent, `L` layer_count, `R` the nonzero buffer_row_length or W, and `I` the nonzero buffer_image_height or H. Require W,H,L positive, R at least W, and I at least H. Compute these values with checked operations.

```text
row_stride   = R * B
layer_stride = I * row_stride
span         = (L - 1) * layer_stride + (H - 1) * row_stride + W * B
end          = O + span
```

The last copied row contributes its actual bytes, not a full padded stride. Require end within the buffer's logical size and binding allocation bounds. Keep row_stride at most INT32_MAX as a conservative supported-copy limit. Add the buffer binding offset with checked arithmetic before allocation-relative comparisons. Raw U64 overflow returns BV_ARGUMENT and never wraps. Neither `optimalBufferCopyRowPitchAlignment` nor `optimalBufferCopyOffsetAlignment` is treated as a mandatory Vulkan alignment rule.

Require buffer_offset divisible by four for all supported copies. This deliberately applies one conservative rule even for D16 on graphics. Require mip index and layer range in bounds. Compute each selected mip dimension as max(1, base dimension shifted by mip), without an unchecked shift. Image offset and extent must fit that mip using subtraction-based or checked bounds. Copy aspect matches the format. Buffer and image usages match direction. All resources share the command's device and are bound.

The selected queue must support transfers. Cache its actual minImageTransferGranularity. For (0,0,0), accept only whole-mip x, y, and z offset and extent. For positive granularity, require aligned offsets and extent multiples, allowing the documented edge exception independently per axis. Our 2D z is zero and depth is one, which still needs the z edge check. Require GRAPHICS for any depth copy in either direction and for clear_depth_image. Require GRAPHICS or COMPUTE for clear_color_image. Transfer-only color copies are supported when granularity permits them. These checks preserve the Vulkan 1.0 queue rules without relying on later maintenance features. See [queue granularity](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkQueueFamilyProperties.html), [color-clear queue support](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearColorImage.html), and [depth-clear requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage.html).

Copy lists must be nonempty and have at most 4096 regions. Detect overlapping destination image boxes when mip, aspect, and layer ranges overlap. Detect overlapping destination buffer spans for image readback. The buffer check conservatively treats row and layer padding within the computed envelope as occupied. Source overlap is permitted, provided destination regions do not overlap. Within one clear call, reject overlapping subresource ranges. All checks and allocations complete before dispatch. Keep existing legal buffer-to-buffer aliasing and existing copy-buffer allocation-relative overlap checks. Introduce this policy in both bind_image_memory and bind_buffer_memory.

|---|---|---|

| Nested begin | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch or metadata change. |
| End render pass | Recording Inside | Dispatch `CmdEndRenderPass`, return to Outside. Retention stays. |
| Unmatched end render pass | Any state other than Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier | Recording Outside | Validate, marshal, stage retention, dispatch. |
| Fill, copy, clear, or barrier inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME, no dispatch. This subset has no subpass-local barriers. |
| End command inside | Recording Inside | BV_LIFETIME. Caller may end the pass or reset. |
| End command outside | Recording Outside | Driver success enters Executable. Failure enters Invalid with retention intact. |
| Reset | Healthy device and any nonactive command state, including Recording Inside | Success enters Initial and frees retention. Driver failure enters Invalid and preserves retention. |

Successful device idle changes Pending to Completed and Uncertain to Invalid. None of these observations releases retention. Active associations continue to block command reset, affected pool destruction, fence reset or destruction, and another submission on that device.

Optional depth needs DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT usage and DEPTH aspect. Every view selects one mip. Each selected mip is at least framebuffer extent and each view supplies enough layers. Each attachment must be bound. Reject any pair of attachments that selects overlapping mip and layer subresources of the same image. Different images cannot overlap memory by binding policy.
