item.stdout:
# Candidate 1. Explicit layouts and direct resource dependencies

## Usage written before the types

These are proposed caller snippets, not compiled evidence. Imports use `V` for `Vulkan.bend`, `vk` for `src/constants.bend`, `W` for upstream U64, `Core` for src/core.bend, and `T` for proposed example-specific memory-selection and assertion helpers. All operations run in `V.Action`. The surrounding example uses `Entry.with`. Its device selects a graphics queue. Constants below are generated Vulkan constants, not private numeric aliases.

### Create an optimal image, clear it, and read every pixel

The caller owns allocation and synchronization choices. `T.allocate` has the existing `tests/transfers.bend::allocate` behavior. It selects memory using the returned requirements' memory-type bits and requested flags. `readback` is a bound transfer-destination buffer of at least 128 bytes. `readback_memory` and `readback_binding_offset` identify its allocation and binding offset. The command and fence start Initial and unsignaled.

```bend
+configuration = V.ImageFormatInfo{
  vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM(), vk.VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D(),
  vk.VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL(),
  (vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT() .|. vk.VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT() : U32), 0}
+whole = V.ImageSubresourceRange{vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT(), 0, 1, 0, 1}
do V.Action<Unit>:
  supported : V.ImageFormatProperties <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_image_format_properties(instance, physical, configuration)
  +image : V.Image <- V.Device.create_image(device,
    V.ImageCreateInfo{configuration, V.Extent3D{8,4,1}, 1, 1, vk.VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT()})
  requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device, image)
  +memory : V.DeviceMemory <- T.allocate(instance, physical, device, requirements, vk.VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT())
  V.Device.bind_image_memory(device, image, memory, W.zero())
  V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,
    vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT(), vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), [], [],
    [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, whole, vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED(),
      vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(), 0, vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT()}])
  V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),
    V.ClearColor{1.0,0.0,1.0,1.0}, [whole])
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,
    vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), [], [],
    [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image, whole, vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),
      vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(), vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT(), vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()}])
  V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, image, vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(), readback,
    [V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,
      V.ImageSubresourceLayers{vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT(),0,0,1},
      V.ImageOffset3D{0,0,0},V.Extent3D{8,4,1}}])
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT(),
    [], [V.BufferMemoryBarrier{readback,W.zero(),W.of_u32(128),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT()}], [])
  V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
  V.Device.submit(device, command, fence)
  completion : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence, Core.whole_size())
  T.require(U32.is_eq(completion,vk.VK_SUCCESS()), "Fence must complete")
  bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device, readback_memory, readback_binding_offset, 128)
  T.expect_rgba8(bytes,8,4,255,0,255,255)
  V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
  V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
  V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
  return Unit{}
```

`T.expect_rgba8` compares all 128 literal expected bytes, including alpha. The query result can guide application selection. Creation repeats the native configuration check, so a caller cannot bypass validation by omitting the query. Repeated cycles reset the fence as well as the command before reuse.

### Preserve an image while uploading a padded rectangle

A previous successful, observed submission left this RGBA8 image in TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL with defined contents. This example resets and begins its command, then uploads a 3 by 2 rectangle at image coordinate 2,1. A source buffer has row length 7 texels, image height 5 rows, and a 12-byte initial offset. These fields are in texels and bytes as named. The two layers exercise image-height padding. The selected image has at least two array layers and the addressed mip is at least 5 by 3.

```bend
+layers = V.ImageSubresourceLayers{vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT(),0,0,2}
+range = V.ImageSubresourceRange{vk.VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT(),0,1,0,2}
+patch = V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(12),7,5,layers,V.ImageOffset3D{2,1,0},V.Extent3D{3,2,1}}
do V.Action<Unit>:
  V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
  V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT(), vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(),
    [], [V.BufferMemoryBarrier{upload,W.zero(),Core.whole_size(),vk.VK_ACCESS_HOST_WRITE_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()}], [])
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), [], [],
    [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(),
      vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT()}])
  V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command,upload,image,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),[patch])
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(), [], [],
    [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),
      vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()}])
  V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(),readback,
    [V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(20),9,6,layers,V.ImageOffset3D{2,1,0},V.Extent3D{3,2,1}}])
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(),vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT(),
    [],[V.BufferMemoryBarrier{readback,W.zero(),Core.whole_size(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT()}],[])
  V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
  V.Device.submit_and_wait(device,command)
  return Unit{}
```

The upload bytes are a different function of x, y, channel, and layer. Initialize staging and output padding to distinct sentinels. Check payload and untouched output padding independently, then read the full image to prove untouched texels survived. The source's exclusive end is 192 bytes. The destination's exclusive end is 284 bytes. Those values follow the span formula below. Buffer bind offsets are additional allocation offsets and do not appear in `buffer_offset`.

### Clear color and depth through an actual render pass

Color and depth images are separately created, allocated, and bound using the first example's sequence. The color image has COLOR_ATTACHMENT and TRANSFER_SRC usages. The depth image has DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT and preferably TRANSFER_SRC usages. Format configuration queries select RGBA8 UNORM and D32_SFLOAT if supported. The views below expose one mip and one layer. `color_range` and `depth_range` name those same subresources.

```bend
do V.Action<Unit>:
  +color_view : V.ImageView <- V.Device.create_image_view(device,
    V.ImageViewCreateInfo{color,vk.VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D(),vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM(),color_range})
  +depth_view : V.ImageView <- V.Device.create_image_view(device,
    V.ImageViewCreateInfo{depth,vk.VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D(),depth_format,depth_range})
  +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{
    [V.ColorAttachmentInfo{vk.VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM(),vk.VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR(),vk.VK_ATTACHMENT_STORE_OP_STORE()}],
    Some{V.DepthStencilAttachmentInfo{depth_format,vk.VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR(),vk.VK_ATTACHMENT_STORE_OP_STORE(),
      vk.VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_DONT_CARE(),vk.VK_ATTACHMENT_STORE_OP_DONT_CARE()}}})
  +framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[color_view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
  V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT(),
    (vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT() .|. vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_EARLY_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT() .|. vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT() : U32),[],[],
    [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{color,color_range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED(),vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL(),0,vk.VK_ACCESS_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT()},
     V.ImageMemoryBarrier{depth,depth_range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED(),vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL(),0,vk.VK_ACCESS_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT()}])
  V.CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command,framebuffer,V.RenderArea{0,0,8,4},
    [V.ClearColorValue{V.ClearColor{0.0,1.0,0.0,1.0}},V.ClearDepthStencilValue{V.ClearDepthStencil{0.5,0}}])
  V.CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,
    (vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT() .|. vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_EARLY_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT() .|. vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT() : U32),
    vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(),[],[],
    [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{color,color_range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL(),vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(),vk.VK_ACCESS_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()},
     V.ImageMemoryBarrier{depth,depth_range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL(),vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL(),vk.VK_ACCESS_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT(),vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT()}])
  V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
  V.Device.submit_and_wait(device,command)
  return Unit{}
```

This snippet ends with images ready for explicit copies. The acceptance test records both copies and their host barrier before `end`. The D32 expected representation of 0.5 is exactly `0x3f000000`. The example reads its bytes as `00 00 00 3f` on the target little-endian x86_64 machine. Submit completion alone establishes neither CPU visibility nor pixel correctness. Destruction follows command reset, framebuffer, views and render pass, images, then allocations. Deleting just a framebuffer does not release the views' ownership of their images.

## Problem and grounding

Milestone 2 adds offscreen image transfers and executable color/depth attachment clears to a checked Vulkan 1.0 wrapper. The next consumer needs indexed graphics without replacing image ownership. The challenge is preserving the existing submission and affine-array contracts through indirect image dependencies and new compiler layouts.

Observed grounding came from the full [contract](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/design-task.md), [framing](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md), [synthesis](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md), [local exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-local.md), and [Voltra exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-voltra.md). Direct inspection covered [Vulkan.bend](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/Vulkan.bend), [native.c](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/src/native.c), the manifest, generator, verifier, current tests and laws, and the roadmap/design documents. I also inspected the pinned Voltra command policy, offscreen constructor, and native clear/copy path. `bend guide` was informational. This runner performed no builds, tests, git operations, repository edits, or nested delegation.

The current native registry has monotonic keys, device ownership checks, command-owned submission associations, persistent recording references, and staged metadata before void commands. Host-busy traversal currently stops after a buffer binding. Layout tracking and render scope do not exist. The emitted buffer ABI already flattens U64 limbs. These observed constraints motivate extending the existing machinery rather than creating a renderer framework.

Voltra contributes the explicit staging sequence and independent pixel comparison. This proposal uses fresh marshalling against Khronos headers. It adopts none of Voltra's Vulkan 1.3 dynamic rendering, packed UI-color policy, truncated sizes, or weaker ownership behavior. The reference remains pinned at `8900b07`.

Throughput checkpoint. Grounding precedes implementation. Candidate artifacts have separate owners. This runner writes only its assigned directory. A single later implementation owner changes the coupled public/native/manifest/tests/docs boundary in ordered commits. Bend's IO event loop remains the only registry writer. Pure expected-pixel generation and independent arithmetic preparation may use balanced parallel calls. Dependent Vulkan effects stay sequenced.

## Chosen shape

Callers specify layouts at every image command and old/new layouts in barriers. There is no global image-layout field and no command-local layout ledger. A direct native dependency graph represents bindings, persistent object dependencies, and recorded operands. Host protection follows that graph transitively from the already authoritative Pending or Uncertain command.

One barrier effect accepts memory, buffer, and image lists. One Vulkan 1.0 render-pass path uses a single graphics subpass with fixed attachment layouts. Initial, subpass, and final layouts are identical. Callers supply transitions before and after the pass. There are no implicit barriers in `CommandBuffer.end`, hidden transfer transitions, or duplicate legacy barrier entry points.

This concentrates validation, byte addressing, lifetime traversal, and transactional recording behind the existing wrapper boundary. Callers still know Vulkan synchronization and choose memory. That is the accepted ash-like cost. The wrapper does not claim to prove execution layout or initialized contents.

### Exact Bend type sketch

These source-level declarations are the proposed contract. Foreign bodies and ordinary adapters are omitted here. Compiler representation is explicitly not inferred from these constructors. Existing handles and `MemoryRequirements`, `MemoryBarrier`, and `BufferMemoryBarrier` stay as defined today.

```bend
type Image is Data:
  Image{key: U32}
type ImageView is Data:
  ImageView{key: U32}
type RenderPass is Data:
  RenderPass{key: U32}
type Framebuffer is Data:
  Framebuffer{key: U32}

type Extent2D is Data:
  Extent2D{width: U32, height: U32}
type Extent3D is Data:
  Extent3D{width: U32, height: U32, depth: U32}
type ImageOffset3D is Data:
  ImageOffset3D{x: U32, y: U32, z: U32}
type RenderArea is Data:
  RenderArea{x: U32, y: U32, width: U32, height: U32}

type ImageFormatInfo is Data:
  ImageFormatInfo{format: U32, image_type: U32, tiling: U32, usage: U32, flags: U32}
type ImageFormatProperties is Data:
  ImageFormatProperties{max_extent: Extent3D, max_mip_levels: U32,
    max_array_layers: U32, sample_counts: U32, max_resource_size: W.U64}
type ImageCreateInfo is Data:
  ImageCreateInfo{configuration: ImageFormatInfo, extent: Extent3D,
    mip_levels: U32, array_layers: U32, samples: U32}

type ImageSubresourceRange is Data:
  ImageSubresourceRange{aspects: U32, base_mip_level: U32, level_count: U32,
    base_array_layer: U32, layer_count: U32}
type ImageSubresourceLayers is Data:
  ImageSubresourceLayers{aspect: U32, mip_level: U32, base_array_layer: U32, layer_count: U32}
type ImageViewCreateInfo is Data:
  ImageViewCreateInfo{image: Image, view_type: U32, format: U32, range: ImageSubresourceRange}
type ImageMemoryBarrier is Data:
  ImageMemoryBarrier{image: Image, range: ImageSubresourceRange,
    old_layout: U32, new_layout: U32, src_access: U32, dst_access: U32}
type BufferImageCopy is Data:
  BufferImageCopy{buffer_offset: W.U64, buffer_row_length: U32, buffer_image_height: U32,
    image_subresource: ImageSubresourceLayers, image_offset: ImageOffset3D, image_extent: Extent3D}

type ClearColor is Data:
  ClearColor{r: F32, g: F32, b: F32, a: F32}
type ClearDepthStencil is Data:
  ClearDepthStencil{depth: F32, stencil: U32}
type ClearValue is Data:
  ClearColorValue{value: ClearColor}
  ClearDepthStencilValue{value: ClearDepthStencil}
  UnusedClearValue{}

type ColorAttachmentInfo is Data:
  ColorAttachmentInfo{format: U32, load_op: U32, store_op: U32}
type DepthStencilAttachmentInfo is Data:
  DepthStencilAttachmentInfo{format: U32, depth_load_op: U32, depth_store_op: U32,
    stencil_load_op: U32, stencil_store_op: U32}
type RenderPassCreateInfo is Type:
  RenderPassCreateInfo{colors: List<ColorAttachmentInfo>, depth_stencil: Maybe<DepthStencilAttachmentInfo>}
type FramebufferCreateInfo is Type:
  FramebufferCreateInfo{render_pass: RenderPass, attachments: List<ImageView>, extent: Extent2D}

def ImageFormatWords() -> Type:
  (U32 & U32) & ((U32 & U32) & ((U32 & U32) & (U32 & U32)))
```

Unsigned image offsets intentionally represent the supported nonnegative copy coordinates. Before C casts to `int32_t`, reject values above INT32_MAX. Render-area offsets receive the same check. ## Problem and grounding

Milestone 2 adds offscreen image transfers and executable color/depth attachment clears to a checked Vulkan 1.0 wrapper. The next consumer needs indexed graphics without replacing image ownership. The challenge is preserving the existing submission and affine-array contracts through indirect image dependencies and new compiler layouts.

Observed grounding came from the full [contract](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/design-task.md), [framing](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md), [synthesis](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md), [local exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-local.md), and [Voltra exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-voltra.md). Direct inspection covered [Vulkan.bend](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/Vulkan.bend), [native.c](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/src/native.c), the manifest, generator, verifier, current tests and laws, and the roadmap/design documents. I also inspected the pinned Voltra command policy, offscreen constructor, and native clear/copy path. `bend guide` was informational. This runner performed no builds, tests, git operations, repository edits, or nested delegation.

The current native registry has monotonic keys, device ownership checks, command-owned submission associations, persistent recording references, and staged metadata before void commands. Host-busy traversal currently stops after a buffer binding. Layout tracking and render scope do not exist. The emitted buffer ABI already flattens U64 limbs. These observed constraints motivate extending the existing machinery rather than creating a renderer framework.

Voltra contributes the explicit staging sequence and independent pixel comparison. This proposal uses fresh marshalling against Khronos headers. It adopts none of Voltra's Vulkan 1.3 dynamic rendering, packed UI-color policy, truncated sizes, or weaker ownership behavior. The reference remains pinned at `8900b07`.

Throughput checkpoint. Grounding precedes implementation. Candidate artifacts have separate owners. This runner writes only its assigned directory. A single later implementation owner changes the coupled public/native/manifest/tests/docs boundary in ordered commits. Bend's IO event loop remains the only registry writer. Pure expected-pixel generation and independent arithmetic preparation may use balanced parallel calls. Dependent Vulkan effects stay sequenced.

## Chosen shape

Callers specify layouts at every image command and old/new layouts in barriers. There is no global image-layout field and no command-local layout ledger. A direct native dependency graph represents bindings, persistent object dependencies, and recorded operands. Host protection follows that graph transitively from the already authoritative Pending or Uncertain command.

One barrier effect accepts memory, buffer, and image lists. One Vulkan 1.0 render-pass path uses a single graphics subpass with fixed attachment layouts. Initial, subpass, and final layouts are identical. Callers supply transitions before and after the pass. There are no implicit barriers in `CommandBuffer.end`, hidden transfer transitions, or duplicate legacy barrier entry points.

This concentrates validation, byte addressing, lifetime traversal, and transactional recording behind the existing wrapper boundary. Callers still know Vulkan synchronization and choose memory. That is the accepted ash-like cost. The wrapper does not claim to prove execution layout or initialized contents.

## Problem and grounding

Milestone 2 adds offscreen image transfers and executable color/depth attachment clears to a checked Vulkan 1.0 wrapper. The next consumer needs indexed graphics without replacing image ownership. The challenge is preserving the existing submission and affine-array contracts through indirect image dependencies and new compiler layouts.

Observed grounding came from the full [contract](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/design-task.md), [framing](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md), [synthesis](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md), [local exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-local.md), and [Voltra exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-voltra.md). Direct inspection covered [Vulkan.bend](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/Vulkan.bend), [native.c](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/src/native.c), the manifest, generator, verifier, current tests and laws, and the roadmap/design documents. I also inspected the pinned Voltra command policy, offscreen constructor, and native clear/copy path. `bend guide` was informational. This runner performed no builds, tests, git operations, repository edits, or nested delegation.

The current native registry has monotonic keys, device ownership checks, command-owned submission associations, persistent recording references, and staged metadata before void commands. Host-busy traversal currently stops after a buffer binding. Layout tracking and render scope do not exist. The emitted buffer ABI already flattens U64 limbs. These observed constraints motivate extending the existing machinery rather than creating a renderer framework.

Voltra contributes the explicit staging sequence and independent pixel comparison. This proposal uses fresh marshalling against Khronos headers. It adopts none of Voltra's Vulkan 1.3 dynamic rendering, packed UI-color policy, truncated sizes, or weaker ownership behavior. The reference remains pinned at `8900b07`.

Throughput checkpoint. Grounding precedes implementation. Candidate artifacts have separate owners. This runner writes only its assigned directory. A single later implementation owner changes the coupled public/native/manifest/tests/docs boundary in ordered commits. Bend's IO event loop remains the only registry writer. Pure expected-pixel generation and independent arithmetic preparation may use balanced parallel calls. Dependent Vulkan effects stay sequenced.

## Chosen shape

Callers specify layouts at every image command and old/new layouts in barriers. There is no global image-layout field and no command-local layout ledger. A direct native dependency graph represents bindings, persistent object dependencies, and recorded operands. Host protection follows that graph transitively from the already authoritative Pending or Uncertain command.

One barrier effect accepts memory, buffer, and image lists. One Vulkan 1.0 render-pass path uses a single graphics subpass with fixed attachment layouts. Initial, subpass, and final layouts are identical. Callers supply transitions before and after the pass. There are no implicit barriers in `CommandBuffer.end`, hidden transfer transitions, or duplicate legacy barrier entry points.

This concentrates validation, byte addressing, lifetime traversal, and transactional recording behind the existing wrapper boundary. Callers still know Vulkan synchronization and choose memory. That is the accepted ash-like cost. The wrapper does not claim to prove execution layout or initialized contents.

## Problem and grounding

Milestone 2 adds offscreen image transfers and executable color/depth attachment clears to a checked Vulkan 1.0 wrapper. The next consumer needs indexed graphics without replacing image ownership. The challenge is preserving the existing submission and affine-array contracts through indirect image dependencies and new compiler layouts.

Observed grounding came from the full [contract](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/design-task.md), [framing](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md), [synthesis](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-explanation.md), [local exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-local.md), and [Voltra exploration](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/how-voltra.md). ## Chosen shape

Callers specify layouts at every image command and old/new layouts in barriers. There is no global image-layout field and no command-local layout ledger. A direct native dependency graph represents bindings, persistent object dependencies, and recorded operands. Host protection follows that graph transitively from the already authoritative Pending or Uncertain command.

One barrier effect accepts memory, buffer, and image lists. One Vulkan 1.0 render-pass path uses a single graphics subpass with fixed attachment layouts. Initial, subpass, and final layouts are identical. Callers supply transitions before and after the pass. There are no implicit barriers in `CommandBuffer.end`, hidden transfer transitions, or duplicate legacy barrier entry points.

This concentrates validation, byte addressing, lifetime traversal, and transactional recording behind the existing wrapper boundary. Callers still know Vulkan synchronization and choose memory. That is the accepted ash-like cost. The wrapper does not claim to prove execution layout or initialized contents.

### Explicit layout semantics

Every barrier carries a finite validated range. Reject zero counts, VK_REMAINING sentinel counts, and arithmetic overflow rather than silently normalizing them. A clear list must be nonempty; reject overlapping selected ranges within that single call for a consistent boundary. Separate calls can deliberately clear the same subresource again. Color ranges use COLOR. Depth-only ranges use DEPTH. Combined depth/stencil image barriers require both aspects in Vulkan 1.0. Copy subresources select one aspect. Clear ranges may select either or both existing depth/stencil aspects. A depth/stencil framebuffer view must cover the attachment's required aspects.

Accepted old layouts are UNDEFINED, GENERAL, COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, subject to format/usage compatibility. New layout cannot be UNDEFINED. PREINITIALIZED and presentation/extension layouts reject. Validate both old and new layout's required image usages. Depth/stencil-only layouts on color images and color attachment layout on depth images reject. With UNDEFINED, require source access 0 to keep discard semantics unambiguous. Otherwise existing stage/access validation applies without pretending that access masks prove an actual layout.

`old_layout` is the caller's assertion about the addressed subresources at execution. UNDEFINED explicitly discards their prior contents. It may be used after previous use only with a valid execution dependency on that use. Equal old/new is an ordinary memory dependency. Overlapping barriers for the same image/aspect/mip/layer inside one call reject rather than pretending their array order establishes transition order. Sequential transitions use successive pipeline-barrier effects.

Image barriers, clears, and copies require a bound image before dispatch. `clear_*` and copies accept GENERAL or the matching transfer optimal layout. They neither insert a transition nor update a cache. A caller that supplies the wrong old/current layout can pass wrapper validation and still issue invalid Vulkan. The docs must say this directly. The underlying command's layout parameter describes execution-time use, as specified by [vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer.html). Baseline combined-aspect barrier requirements come from [VkImageMemoryBarrier](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImageMemoryBarrier.html).

Recording, failed recording, successful reset, failed reset, OOM submit, uncertain submit, and completion change no stored image layout because none exists. Two separately recorded commands may both mention an image. The caller submits a sequence whose assertions agree with actual prior execution. Following an uncertain submission, the caller must not preserve assumed contents. After successful idle recovery, re-record a complete overwrite with an appropriately scoped UNDEFINED discard transition, or destroy and recreate. Device loss requires teardown/recreation. Completion does not repair an incorrect barrier.

## Render-pass compatibility and clear values

A render pass owns one immutable schema. Its colors appear first, optional depth/stencil last. All descriptions use one sample and flags 0. There is exactly one graphics subpass with ordered color references and an optional depth/stencil reference. No resolve, input, preserve attachments, subpass changes, or attachment aliasing exists in M2.

The color description's initial/reference/final layout is COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL. The depth/stencil description uses DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL for all three. The pass has zero subpass dependencies because callers explicitly synchronize outside the pass and no automatic layout transition is requested. M2 load/store attachment clears occur through begin/end. A separate in-pass clear-attachments command is outside this milestone's chosen operation set. This is an architectural choice, not a universal Vulkan rule. The [render-pass synchronization specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/renderpass.html) distinguishes subpass dependencies and layout transitions.

At pass creation, validate recognized load/store ops, color versus depth formats, color count, graphics capability, and selected format attachment features. Reject non-DONT_CARE stencil operations on depth-only formats. At least one color or depth attachment exists. No generic F32 clear union is repurposed as integer-color storage.

At framebuffer creation, require the same device for pass and all views. Attachment count and order must match the exact pass schema. Each view's format and samples match its slot. Its image is bound, has the appropriate attachment usage, and exposes the required aspects. A color view exposes COLOR. A depth-only view exposes DEPTH. A combined attachment exposes DEPTH|STENCIL. View range is one mip, one layer, type 2D. Effective mip dimensions must contain framebuffer extent. Framebuffer dimensions satisfy maxFramebufferWidth/Height and are nonzero. Fixed framebuffer layers is one.

Reject duplicate or overlapping image subresources across framebuffer slots, even when the caller uses distinct views. Distinct nonoverlapping mips/layers of the same image are allowed if each fits. Binding rules already reject physical image allocation aliasing. The graph retains the exact pass and each view for the framebuffer's entire life. `begin_render_pass` always uses that exact pass, so compatibility between different pass objects is not part of this API.

At begin, validate a live same-device framebuffer, graphics queue, Outside scope, nonnegative signed-representable area offsets, positive area extent, and checked area containment in the framebuffer. Clear values have exactly one entry per attachment slot. A CLEAR color slot requires ClearColorValue. A depth/stencil slot requires ClearDepthStencilValue if either represented aspect has CLEAR load. Other slots require UnusedClearValue. Native code supplies a zeroed unused VkClearValue in those slots. This stricter count policy avoids a hidden Vulkan highest-cleared-index convention in callers.

Float color clears are finite linear numeric R,G,B,A values, following [VkClearColorValue](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkClearColorValue.html). UNORM/sRGB formats use float clear semantics. UNORM conversion follows the format. sRGB color components are encoded by the format's clear conversion, and alpha remains linear. Finite out-of-range values are accepted for color and converted by Vulkan; NaN/infinity reject. Depth must be finite in [0,1]. Stencil is a raw integer within 0..255 for the supported stencil formats. The unused stencil of a depth-only clear must be zero. There is no UI packed-color normalization or channel swizzle.

The example's 0 and 1 color channels eliminate UNORM/sRGB rounding ambiguity. Depth 0.5 is an exact binary float. Ordinary non-endpoint F32 values, signed zero, and depth/stencil values still need explicit ABI probe evidence. D24 depth readback's unused high bits are not compared as if they were defined payload. General direct float clear semantics are informed by the core clear commands, including [vkCmdClearColorImage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearColorImage.html) and [vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage.html).

## Buffer-image addressing and queue rules

The native validator converts every offset and stride product to checked uint64_t before arithmetic. U32 row length/image height remain the Vulkan fields, while their byte strides and required span are U64. A row's buffer bound is checked against its logical buffer size. Binding requirements and the allocation interval are checked separately.

For an accepted format's chosen aspect, let B be the copied element size, w/h the region extent, and L the layer count. Because this profile is 2D, z=0 and depth=1. Let R equal buffer_row_length when nonzero and w otherwise. Let H equal buffer_image_height when nonzero and h otherwise. Require R>=w and H>=h.

```text
row_bytes   = checked_mul(R, B)
layer_bytes = checked_mul(H, row_bytes)
last_layer  = checked_mul(L - 1, layer_bytes)
last_row    = checked_mul(h - 1, row_bytes)
row_payload = checked_mul(w, B)
span        = checked_add(checked_add(last_layer,last_row),row_payload)
end         = checked_add(buffer_offset,span)
```

The formula includes neither trailing padding after the final copied row nor a full unused layer tail. It rejects every overflow. Require end <= buffer.size. A deliberately conservative M2 rule requires buffer_offset to be a multiple of four for every supported format, which also covers the accepted four-byte color elements and depth/stencil baseline requirements. D16 and stencil retain two/one-byte row payloads. Require row_bytes <= INT32_MAX as a conservative consistent stride limit. Do not enforce optimalBufferCopyOffsetAlignment or optimalBufferCopyRowPitchAlignment as mandatory correctness constraints.

Ranges must have one supported aspect bit, positive extent/layer count, valid mip/layer indices, and an extent within `max(1,baseExtent >> mip)`. Check offset representability before casting. No addition is allowed to wrap to appear in range. Format/aspect B comes from the table, not storage size. [VkBufferImageCopy](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html) defines the row/image-height units and single-aspect rule.

Reject overlapping destination image boxes in buffer-to-image across all region pairs sharing mip, aspect, and overlapping layers. Buffer-to-image source reuse is allowed. For image-to-buffer, reject overlapping destination buffer bounding intervals across all region pairs. This intentionally also rejects overlap of padding-only portions of their conservative bounds. Image source reuse is allowed. No per-row enumeration is necessary for validation. Document this conservative rejection rather than claiming exact byte-set overlap acceptance. Neither direction permits buffer/image allocation alias overlap under the binding policy.

Cache the selected queue's full `VkQueueFamilyProperties` during device creation, before freeing the enumeration array. The public M1 queue tuple API can stay unchanged. Its selection helper remains valid. New commands check cached properties.

## Alternatives considered and where this candidate loses

These are whole designs, not renamed versions of the chosen graph.

| Design | Caller responsibility and hidden complexity | Why it loses here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chosen explicit resources/layouts plus direct native graph | Caller selects memory, layouts, barriers, and execution order. Native code hides validation, ownership closure, scope, and marshalling. | It provides fewer synchronization diagnostics and repeats caller barrier code. It is the smallest extension of the present checked Vulkan boundary without a second mutable model. |
| Command-local transition plans with submit-time preconditions and completion-time image versions, plus expanded retained closures | Caller declares desired image uses. A planner generates barriers, retains all reached objects, and tracks entry/exit subresource versions. It must define when two recordings conflict, how reset retracts a plan, how OOM preserves a plan, how uncertain submission poisons layouts, and how pass final transitions merge. | This can offer a deeper command interface and catch wrong-layout mistakes. It introduces a new scheduling/version system beside the authoritative command state and much larger subresource metadata. It would win for a renderer framework with many generated passes. M2 does not yet have that consumer. |
| Owned OffscreenTarget aggregate with atomic create/allocate/view/pass/framebuffer and a render/readback operation | Caller selects target size/format and calls clear/read. Aggregate code hides nearly all resource coordination and can own a layout state safely only if it monopolizes recording/submission. A target command list retains the whole aggregate. | It has the smallest caller interface and would win for a fixed offscreen tool. To coexist with public image/barrier/memory APIs it needs escape hatches or parallel ownership/layout routes. Monopolizing submission would replace the M1 wrapper contract and restrict M3 attachment reuse. |

Direct-edge queries scan live rows and direct edges. Busy traversal can revisit shared descendants through multiple framebuffer/view paths. The DAG bounds path depth, while the cost still scales with traversed paths. Expanded command closures or incoming counters would speed some lookups. They also duplicate reachability information that must survive creation rollback and reset. The fixed DAG and existing single active command make direct traversal a better M2 trade. No benchmark evidence is claimed.

The fixed pass layouts lose automatic UNDEFINED-to-attachment and final transfer transitions. Callers write barriers even for simple clears. In exchange, transfer and pass callers share one explicit transition route. Supporting arbitrary initial/final layouts later would be a deliberate API expansion with dependency policy, not an incidental metadata field.

Exact render-pass identity loses Vulkan's compatible-pass reuse. Fixed one-layer framebuffers and one sample lose layered rendering and MSAA. The next indexed-graphics stage uses neither. General mips/layers, 2D-array views, multiple colors, schema metadata, and full image usage metadata keep ordinary future graphics additions in the existing architecture.

Disallowing image aliasing loses temporary render-target memory reuse. Conservative copy destination intervals can reject safe padding interleaving. Allocation-wide host exclusion can block an unrelated buffer in the same allocation. These rules buy a readable safety boundary without an optimal-image memory-layout oracle, byte-set solver, or new active-range truth. They are documented limits, not hidden driver assumptions.

Finite float clear values lose NaN/Infinity payload testing and integer-color clears. The supported format list makes that boundary explicit. Wider formats need a numeric clear variant and an ABI probe rather than treating bitwise U32 words as convenient colors.

The native file grows. The design keeps direct effect-to-handler paths and one authoritative graph, but a future audited file split may improve maintainability once the emitted C include behavior is established.

Every barrier carries a finite validated range. Reject zero counts, VK_REMAINING sentinel counts, and arithmetic overflow rather than silently normalizing them. Clear ranges may select either or both existing depth/stencil aspects. A depth/stencil framebuffer view must cover the attachment's required aspects.

Accepted old layouts are UNDEFINED, GENERAL, COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, subject to format/usage compatibility. ## Render-pass compatibility and clear values

A render pass owns one immutable schema. Its colors appear first, optional depth/stencil last. All descriptions use one sample and flags 0. There is exactly one graphics subpass with ordered color references and an optional depth/stencil reference. No resolve, input, preserve attachments, subpass changes, or attachment aliasing exists in M2.

The color description's initial/reference/final layout is COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL. The depth/stencil description uses DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL for all three. The pass has zero subpass dependencies because callers explicitly synchronize outside the pass and no automatic layout transition is requested. M2 load/store attachment clears occur through begin/end. A separate in-pass clear-attachments command is outside this milestone's chosen operation set. This is an architectural choice, not a universal Vulkan rule. The [render-pass synchronization specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/renderpass.html) distinguishes subpass dependencies and layout transitions.

At pass creation, validate recognized load/store ops, color versus depth formats, color count, graphics capability, and selected format attachment features. Reject non-DONT_CARE stencil operations on depth-only formats. At least one color or depth attachment exists. No generic F32 clear union is repurposed as integer-color storage.

At framebuffer creation, require the same device for pass and all views. Attachment count and order must match the exact pass schema. Each view's format and samples match its slot. Its image is bound, has the appropriate attachment usage, and exposes the required aspects. A color view exposes COLOR. A depth-only view exposes DEPTH. A combined attachment exposes DEPTH|STENCIL. View range is one mip, one layer, type 2D. Effective mip dimensions must contain framebuffer extent. Framebuffer dimensions satisfy maxFramebufferWidth/Height and are nonzero. Fixed framebuffer layers is one.

## Buffer-image addressing and queue rules

The native validator converts every offset and stride product to checked uint64_t before arithmetic. U32 row length/image height remain the Vulkan fields, while their byte strides and required span are U64. A row's buffer bound is checked against its logical buffer size. Binding requirements and the allocation interval are checked separately.

For an accepted format's chosen aspect, let B be the copied element size, w/h the region extent, and L the layer count. Because this profile is 2D, z=0 and depth=1. Let R equal buffer_row_length when nonzero and w otherwise. Let H equal buffer_image_height when nonzero and h otherwise. Require R>=w and H>=h.

```text
row_bytes   = checked_mul(R, B)
layer_bytes = checked_mul(H, row_bytes)
last_layer  = checked_mul(L - 1, layer_bytes)
last_row    = checked_mul(h - 1, row_bytes)
row_payload = checked_mul(w, B)
span        = checked_add(checked_add(last_layer,last_row),row_payload)
end         = checked_add(buffer_offset,span)
```

The formula includes neither trailing padding after the final copied row nor a full unused layer tail. It rejects every overflow. Require end <= buffer.size. A deliberately conservative M2 rule requires buffer_offset to be a multiple of four for every supported format, which also covers the accepted four-byte color elements and depth/stencil baseline requirements. D16 and stencil retain two/one-byte row payloads. Require row_bytes <= INT32_MAX as a conservative consistent stride limit. Do not enforce optimalBufferCopyOffsetAlignment or optimalBufferCopyRowPitchAlignment as mandatory correctness constraints.

Ranges must have one supported aspect bit, positive extent/layer count, valid mip/layer indices, and an extent within `max(1,baseExtent >> mip)`. Check offset representability before casting. No addition is allowed to wrap to appear in range. Format/aspect B comes from the table, not storage size. [VkBufferImageCopy](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html) defines the row/image-height units and single-aspect rule.

Reject overlapping destination image boxes in buffer-to-image across all region pairs sharing mip, aspect, and overlapping layers. Buffer-to-image source reuse is allowed. For image-to-buffer, reject overlapping destination buffer bounding intervals across all region pairs. This intentionally also rejects overlap of padding-only portions of their conservative bounds. Image source reuse is allowed. No per-row enumeration is necessary for validation. Document this conservative rejection rather than claiming exact byte-set overlap acceptance. Neither direction permits buffer/image allocation alias overlap under the binding policy.

### Destruction and cleanup

Each explicit destroy verifies device/kind, then rejects any incoming graph edge with BV_LIFETIME. Memory free uses the same incoming-edge query, so every bound image or buffer protects its allocation. Image/view/pass/framebuffer destruction never silently destroys dependencies. Removal frees its outgoing edges and owned metadata only after the native object's destroy call.

Entry cleanup first uses existing idle/loss recovery. For a safe device, destroy pools and command rows first, then fences, framebuffers, image views, render passes, images and buffers, allocations, and the device. Framebuffers disappear before their pass/views. Views disappear before images. All bound resources disappear before allocation free. Remove edges as each dependent dies. Private convenience-fence handling remains unchanged.

An ordinary idle error stops cleanup with the remaining device/entry and graph live for retry. Previously cleaned devices may already be gone, matching M1 partial cleanup behavior. Known device loss permits the same ordered teardown and reports exact loss bits. A callback failure keeps its original error and appends cleanup diagnostics. Explicit Device.destroy still requires public children gone. No new destructor turns a failed wait or timeout into assumed completion.

## Alternatives considered and where this candidate loses

These are whole designs, not renamed versions of the chosen graph.

| Design | Caller responsibility and hidden complexity | Why it loses here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chosen explicit resources/layouts plus direct native graph | Caller selects memory, layouts, barriers, and execution order. Native code hides validation, ownership closure, scope, and marshalling. | It provides fewer synchronization diagnostics and repeats caller barrier code. It is the smallest extension of the present checked Vulkan boundary without a second mutable model. |
| Command-local transition plans with submit-time preconditions and completion-time image versions, plus expanded retained closures | Caller declares desired image uses. A planner generates barriers, retains all reached objects, and tracks entry/exit subresource versions. It must define when two recordings conflict, how reset retracts a plan, how OOM preserves a plan, how uncertain submission poisons layouts, and how pass final transitions merge. | This can offer a deeper command interface and catch wrong-layout mistakes. It introduces a new scheduling/version system beside the authoritative command state and much larger subresource metadata. It would win for a renderer framework with many generated passes. M2 does not yet have that consumer. |
| Owned OffscreenTarget aggregate with atomic create/allocate/view/pass/framebuffer and a render/readback operation | Caller selects target size/format and calls clear/read. Aggregate code hides nearly all resource coordination and can own a layout state safely only if it monopolizes recording/submission. A target command list retains the whole aggregate. | It has the smallest caller interface and would win for a fixed offscreen tool. To coexist with public image/barrier/memory APIs it needs escape hatches or parallel ownership/layout routes. Monopolizing submission would replace the M1 wrapper contract and restrict M3 attachment reuse. |

Direct-edge queries scan live rows and direct edges. Busy traversal can revisit shared descendants through multiple framebuffer/view paths. The DAG bounds path depth, while the cost still scales with traversed paths. Expanded command closures or incoming counters would speed some lookups. They also duplicate reachability information that must survive creation rollback and reset. The fixed DAG and existing single active command make direct traversal a better M2 trade. No benchmark evidence is claimed.

The fixed pass layouts lose automatic UNDEFINED-to-attachment and final transfer transitions. Callers write barriers even for simple clears. In exchange, transfer and pass callers share one explicit transition route. Supporting arbitrary initial/final layouts later would be a deliberate API expansion with dependency policy, not an incidental metadata field.

Exact render-pass identity loses Vulkan's compatible-pass reuse. Fixed one-layer framebuffers and one sample lose layered rendering and MSAA. The next indexed-graphics stage uses neither. General mips/layers, 2D-array views, multiple colors, schema metadata, and full image usage metadata keep ordinary future graphics additions in the existing architecture.

Disallowing image aliasing loses temporary render-target memory reuse. Conservative copy destination intervals can reject safe padding interleaving. Allocation-wide host exclusion can block an unrelated buffer in the same allocation. These rules buy a readable safety boundary without an optimal-image memory-layout oracle, byte-set solver, or new active-range truth. They are documented limits, not hidden driver assumptions.

Finite float clear values lose NaN/Infinity payload testing and integer-color clears. The supported format list makes that boundary explicit. Wider formats need a numeric clear variant and an ABI probe rather than treating bitwise U32 words as convenient colors.

The native file grows. The design keeps direct effect-to-handler paths and one authoritative graph, but a future audited file split may improve maintainability once the emitted C include behavior is established.

## Principles that changed this design

I read the leaf skills named here in this session.

- Foundational Thinking put the graph, supported image profile, and ABI probe before new command handlers.
- Model the Domain selected a typed dependency DAG and a Recording-only Outside/Inside payload instead of a collection of independent busy/render booleans.

- Prove It Works requires literal full readback, nonuniform addressing, native dispatch counters, and row/edge evidence. This design document itself is not runtime evidence.

### Explicit layout semantics

Every barrier carries a finite validated range. Reject zero counts, VK_REMAINING sentinel counts, and arithmetic overflow rather than silently normalizing them. A clear list must be nonempty; reject overlapping selected ranges within that single call for a consistent boundary. Separate calls can deliberately clear the same subresource again. Color ranges use COLOR. Depth-only ranges use DEPTH. Combined depth/stencil image barriers require both aspects in Vulkan 1.0. Copy subresources select one aspect. Clear ranges may select either or both existing depth/stencil aspects. A depth/stencil framebuffer view must cover the attachment's required aspects.

Accepted old layouts are UNDEFINED, GENERAL, COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, subject to format/usage compatibility. New layout cannot be UNDEFINED. PREINITIALIZED and presentation/extension layouts reject. Validate both old and new layout's required image usages. Depth/stencil-only layouts on color images and color attachment layout on depth images reject. With UNDEFINED, require source access 0 to keep discard semantics unambiguous. Otherwise existing stage/access validation applies without pretending that access masks prove an actual layout.

`old_layout` is the caller's assertion about the addressed subresources at execution. UNDEFINED explicitly discards their prior contents. It may be used after previous use only with a valid execution dependency on that use. Equal old/new is an ordinary memory dependency. Overlapping barriers for the same image/aspect/mip/layer inside one call reject rather than pretending their array order establishes transition order. Sequential transitions use successive pipeline-barrier effects.

Image barriers, clears, and copies require a bound image before dispatch. `clear_*` and copies accept GENERAL or the matching transfer optimal layout. They neither insert a transition nor update a cache. A caller that supplies the wrong old/current layout can pass wrapper validation and still issue invalid Vulkan. The docs must say this directly. The underlying command's layout parameter describes execution-time use, as specified by [vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer.html). Baseline combined-aspect barrier requirements come from [VkImageMemoryBarrier](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImageMemoryBarrier.html).

Recording, failed recording, successful reset, failed reset, OOM submit, uncertain submit, and completion change no stored image layout because none exists. Two separately recorded commands may both mention an image. The caller submits a sequence whose assertions agree with actual prior execution. Following an uncertain submission, the caller must not preserve assumed contents. After successful idle recovery, re-record a complete overwrite with an appropriately scoped UNDEFINED discard transition, or destroy and recreate. Device loss requires teardown/recreation. Completion does not repair an incorrect barrier.

## Render-pass compatibility and clear values

A render pass owns one immutable schema. Its colors appear first, optional depth/stencil last. All descriptions use one sample and flags 0. There is exactly one graphics subpass with ordered color references and an optional depth/stencil reference. No resolve, input, preserve attachments, subpass changes, or attachment aliasing exists in M2.

The color description's initial/reference/final layout is COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL. The depth/stencil description uses DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL for all three. The pass has zero subpass dependencies because callers explicitly synchronize outside the pass and no automatic layout transition is requested. M2 load/store attachment clears occur through begin/end. A separate in-pass clear-attachments command is outside this milestone's chosen operation set. This is an architectural choice, not a universal Vulkan rule. The [render-pass synchronization specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/renderpass.html) distinguishes subpass dependencies and layout transitions.

At pass creation, validate recognized load/store ops, color versus depth formats, color count, graphics capability, and selected format attachment features. Reject non-DONT_CARE stencil operations on depth-only formats. At least one color or depth attachment exists. No generic F32 clear union is repurposed as integer-color storage.

At framebuffer creation, require the same device for pass and all views. Attachment count and order must match the exact pass schema. Each view's format and samples match its slot. Its image is bound, has the appropriate attachment usage, and exposes the required aspects. A color view exposes COLOR. A depth-only view exposes DEPTH. A combined attachment exposes DEPTH|STENCIL. View range is one mip, one layer, type 2D. Effective mip dimensions must contain framebuffer extent. Framebuffer dimensions satisfy maxFramebufferWidth/Height and are nonzero. Fixed framebuffer layers is one.

Reject duplicate or overlapping image subresources across framebuffer slots, even when the caller uses distinct views. Distinct nonoverlapping mips/layers of the same image are allowed if each fits. Binding rules already reject physical image allocation aliasing. The graph retains the exact pass and each view for the framebuffer's entire life. `begin_render_pass` always uses that exact pass, so compatibility between different pass objects is not part of this API.

At begin, validate a live same-device framebuffer, graphics queue, Outside scope, nonnegative signed-representable area offsets, positive area extent, and checked area containment in the framebuffer. Clear values have exactly one entry per attachment slot. A CLEAR color slot requires ClearColorValue. A depth/stencil slot requires ClearDepthStencilValue if either represented aspect has CLEAR load. Other slots require UnusedClearValue. Native code supplies a zeroed unused VkClearValue in those slots. This stricter count policy avoids a hidden Vulkan highest-cleared-index convention in callers.

Float color clears are finite linear numeric R,G,B,A values, following [VkClearColorValue](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkClearColorValue.html). UNORM/sRGB formats use float clear semantics. UNORM conversion follows the format. sRGB color components are encoded by the format's clear conversion, and alpha remains linear. Finite out-of-range values are accepted for color and converted by Vulkan; NaN/infinity reject. Depth must be finite in [0,1]. Stencil is a raw integer within 0..255 for the supported stencil formats. The unused stencil of a depth-only clear must be zero. There is no UI packed-color normalization or channel swizzle.

The example's 0 and 1 color channels eliminate UNORM/sRGB rounding ambiguity. Depth 0.5 is an exact binary float. Ordinary non-endpoint F32 values, signed zero, and depth/stencil values still need explicit ABI probe evidence. D24 depth readback's unused high bits are not compared as if they were defined payload. General direct float clear semantics are informed by the core clear commands, including [vkCmdClearColorImage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearColorImage.html) and [vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearDepthStencilImage.html).

## Buffer-image addressing and queue rules

The native validator converts every offset and stride product to checked uint64_t before arithmetic. U32 row length/image height remain the Vulkan fields, while their byte strides and required span are U64. A row's buffer bound is checked against its logical buffer size. Binding requirements and the allocation interval are checked separately.

For an accepted format's chosen aspect, let B be the copied element size, w/h the region extent, and L the layer count. Because this profile is 2D, z=0 and depth=1. Let R equal buffer_row_length when nonzero and w otherwise. Let H equal buffer_image_height when nonzero and h otherwise. Require R>=w and H>=h.

```text
row_bytes   = checked_mul(R, B)
layer_bytes = checked_mul(H, row_bytes)
last_layer  = checked_mul(L - 1, layer_bytes)
last_row    = checked_mul(h - 1, row_bytes)
row_payload = checked_mul(w, B)
span        = checked_add(checked_add(last_layer,last_row),row_payload)
end         = checked_add(buffer_offset,span)
```

The formula includes neither trailing padding after the final copied row nor a full unused layer tail. It rejects every overflow. Require end <= buffer.size. A deliberately conservative M2 rule requires buffer_offset to be a multiple of four for every supported format, which also covers the accepted four-byte color elements and depth/stencil baseline requirements. D16 and stencil retain two/one-byte row payloads. Require row_bytes <= INT32_MAX as a conservative consistent stride limit. Do not enforce optimalBufferCopyOffsetAlignment or optimalBufferCopyRowPitchAlignment as mandatory correctness constraints.

Ranges must have one supported aspect bit, positive extent/layer count, valid mip/layer indices, and an extent within `max(1,baseExtent >> mip)`. Check offset representability before casting. No addition is allowed to wrap to appear in range. Format/aspect B comes from the table, not storage size. [VkBufferImageCopy](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html) defines the row/image-height units and single-aspect rule.

Reject overlapping destination image boxes in buffer-to-image across all region pairs sharing mip, aspect, and overlapping layers. Buffer-to-image source reuse is allowed. For image-to-buffer, reject overlapping destination buffer bounding intervals across all region pairs. This intentionally also rejects overlap of padding-only portions of their conservative bounds. Image source reuse is allowed. No per-row enumeration is necessary for validation. Document this conservative rejection rather than claiming exact byte-set overlap acceptance. Neither direction permits buffer/image allocation alias overlap under the binding policy.

Direct-edge queries scan live rows and direct edges. Busy traversal can revisit shared descendants through multiple framebuffer/view paths. The DAG bounds path depth, while the cost still scales with traversed paths. Expanded command closures or incoming counters would speed some lookups. They also duplicate reachability information that must survive creation rollback and reset. The fixed DAG and existing single active command make direct traversal a better M2 trade. No benchmark evidence is claimed.

The fixed pass layouts lose automatic UNDEFINED-to-attachment and final transfer transitions. Callers write barriers even for simple clears. In exchange, transfer and pass callers share one explicit transition route. Supporting arbitrary initial/final layouts later would be a deliberate API expansion with dependency policy, not an incidental metadata field.

Exact render-pass identity loses Vulkan's compatible-pass reuse. Fixed one-layer framebuffers and one sample lose layered rendering and MSAA. The next indexed-graphics stage uses neither. General mips/layers, 2D-array views, multiple colors, schema metadata, and full image usage metadata keep ordinary future graphics additions in the existing architecture.

Disallowing image aliasing loses temporary render-target memory reuse. Conservative copy destination intervals can reject safe padding interleaving. Allocation-wide host exclusion can block an unrelated buffer in the same allocation. These rules buy a readable safety boundary without an optimal-image memory-layout oracle, byte-set solver, or new active-range truth. They are documented limits, not hidden driver assumptions.

Finite float clear values lose NaN/Infinity payload testing and integer-color clears. The supported format list makes that boundary explicit. Wider formats need a numeric clear variant and an ABI probe rather than treating bitwise U32 words as convenient colors.

The native file grows. The design keeps direct effect-to-handler paths and one authoritative graph, but a future audited file split may improve maintainability once the emitted C include behavior is established.

A render pass owns one immutable schema. Its colors appear first, optional depth/stencil last. All descriptions use one sample and flags 0. There is exactly one graphics subpass with ordered color references and an optional depth/stencil reference. No resolve, input, preserve attachments, subpass changes, or attachment aliasing exists in M2.

The pass has zero subpass dependencies because callers explicitly synchronize outside the pass and no automatic layout transition is requested. M2 load/store attachment clears occur through begin/end. A separate in-pass clear-attachments command is outside this milestone's chosen operation set. This is an architectural choice, not a universal Vulkan rule. The [render-pass synchronization specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/renderpass.html) distinguishes subpass dependencies and layout transitions.

At framebuffer creation, require the same device for pass and all views. Attachment count and order must match the exact pass schema. Each view's format and samples match its slot. Its image is bound, has the appropriate attachment usage, and exposes the required aspects. A color view exposes COLOR. A depth-only view exposes DEPTH. A combined attachment exposes DEPTH|STENCIL.
