```text
last_row    = checked_mul(h - 1, row_bytes)
row_payload = checked_mul(w, B)
span        = checked_add(checked_add(last_layer,last_row),row_payload)
end         = checked_add(buffer_offset,span)
```

The formula includes neither trailing padding after the final copied row nor a full unused layer tail. It rejects every overflow. Require end <= buffer.size. A deliberately conservative M2 rule requires buffer_offset to be a multiple of four for every supported format, which also covers the accepted four-byte color elements and depth/stencil baseline requirements. D16 and stencil retain two/one-byte row payloads. Require row_bytes <= INT32_MAX as a conservative consistent stride limit. Do not enforce optimalBufferCopyOffsetAlignment or optimalBufferCopyRowPitchAlignment as mandatory correctness constraints.

Ranges must have one supported aspect bit, positive extent/layer count, valid mip/layer indices, and an extent within `max(1,baseExtent >> mip)`. Check offset representability before casting. No addition is allowed to wrap to appear in range. Format/aspect B comes from the table, not storage size. [VkBufferImageCopy](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html) defines the row/image-height units and single-aspect rule.

Reject overlapping destination image boxes in buffer-to-image across all region pairs sharing mip, aspect, and overlapping layers. Buffer-to-image source reuse is allowed. For image-to-buffer, reject overlapping destination buffer bounding intervals across all region pairs. This intentionally also rejects overlap of padding-only portions of their conservative bounds. Image source reuse is allowed. No per-row enumeration is necessary for validation. Document this conservative rejection rather than claiming exact byte-set overlap acceptance. Neither direction permits buffer/image allocation alias overlap under the binding policy.

Cache the selected queue's full `VkQueueFamilyProperties` during device creation, before freeing the enumeration array. The public M1 queue tuple API can stay unchanged. Its selection helper remains valid. New commands check cached properties.

| Operation | Queue requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Color image clear | GRAPHICS or COMPUTE. A transfer-only queue does not suffice. |
| Depth/stencil clear and render-pass creation/begin/end | GRAPHICS. |
| Color buffer-image copies | GRAPHICS, COMPUTE, or TRANSFER, plus image transfer granularity. |
| Depth/stencil buffer-image copies | GRAPHICS for this core-1.0 subset. |
| Image barrier | Existing queue-supported stage/access policy, Outside scope, ignored family indices. |

For color transfers, validate each offset coordinate against minImageTransferGranularity. `(0,0,0)` accepts only a whole mip in x/y/z, still for a selected layer interval. Nonzero components require aligned offsets and aligned extents or an extent ending exactly at that mip's boundary. This covers transfer-only queues with coarser restrictions. Graphics/compute queues normally report `(1,1,1)`, but the implementation uses the cached value, not that expectation. The [queue-family definition](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkQueueFamilyProperties.html) gives the edge exception. Depth copying remains graphics-only without adopting later maintenance features, consistent with the baseline restriction in [vkCmdCopyBufferToImage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html).

The canonical readback convention is raw format bytes with row zero corresponding to image y=0 and x increasing within each row. A 2D image has no inherent screen-top convention. The example defines y=0 as top and proves it with a nonuniform pattern. RGBA8 copies produce R,G,B,A bytes. BGRA8 produces B,G,R,A. UNORM represents normalized channel values. sRGB bytes are encoded sRGB color values. No conversion, gamma correction, or vertical flip occurs in copies or `read_memory`. Arrays may have extra capacity; only explicit byte lengths and actual copied texels are logical data.

## ABI, generator, and file boundaries

The installed Bend 2.0.37 ABI is a hard gate. This runner has not emitted any new probe, as builds/tests are excluded. Before implementing decoders, create a small emitted-C probe that actually references every proposed composite, variant, list, and optional field. Force both Maybe alternatives and all ClearValue variants. Capture unpack count, packed handle treatment, flattening, constructor tags, and the F32 bit representation. A source declaration is not ABI evidence.

Probe nested ImageFormatInfo/Extent3D, range/layers/view/region inputs, single handles inside structs, finite F32 color and depth values, UnusedClearValue, Some depth metadata, empty and nonempty attachment lists, and new output tuples. Assert that 0.5 reaches native float bits 0x3f000000 and that color channels reach their distinct expected components. Use emitted runtime helpers for Term extraction and `memcpy` to materialize float bits when appropriate. Never cast an integer-valued Term numerically to float and never assume a guessed float-tag layout. Construct zeroed native VkClearColorValue/VkClearValue with explicit float32/depthStencil members.

Native U64 outputs stay raw limb tuples. Reuse `requirements_from_words` for image requirements and add `image_format_properties_from_words` for image limits. Do not use `CID(W.U64)` or a native constructor ID for an imported alias. Raw names remain implementation adapters in the same public module, following the current wrapper convention. They do not provide a second command path.

| File | Concrete change |
| --- | --- |
| Vulkan.bend | Four handles, domain types, typed result adapters, revised limits type, generated new effects, one extended barrier signature. |
| tools/bindings.json | Seventeen new native effect entries and appended barrier image-list argument. Existing return_owner policies remain intact. |
| tools/generate.py; registry/vk.xml and registry/README.md | Add needed core-1.0 image/layout/aspect/view/sample/load/store enum groups from the same pinned upstream registry source. Retain hash/provenance. Do not hand-edit generated constants. |
| src/constants.bend; src/native.js; generated blocks | Regenerate through the current generator. JS rejection returns correct result shapes; existing array-owner effects return owners. |
| src/native.c | New dispatch, cached queue/limits, four row metadata kinds, direct graph accessors, transitive busy checks, shared bind validator, image/pass/copy marshalling, scope guards on old commands, creation rollback and cleanup. |
| src/core.bend; LAWS.bend; PROOF.bend | Pure checked address/range calculations and float-bit/limb adapters where the installed Base supports them. State important pure contracts and prove them. No proof claims about driver state. |
| tests/image_abi.bend; tests/image_probes.c | Real emitted-layout calls, marshalling assertions, allocation/driver substitution and native graph/scope checks in the existing emitted-test translation unit. |
| tests/images.bend; tests/image_cycles.bend; examples/image_roundtrip.bend | Driver clear/readback, nonuniform subrect, real render-pass color/depth clears, cycles, public error and destruction tests. |
| tools/check_native.py; tools/verify.py | Include new probe file and explicit executed markers, add image examples/suites and sanitizer runs. Update existing allocation-rewrite anchors intentionally when BvUse becomes BvDep. |
| Existing tests, examples, docs/api.md | Append images argument to all pipeline_barrier calls. Update native test arrays and fabricated-call arities, graph inspection names, limits adapters, and discovery counts. |
| docs/design.md; docs/roadmap.md; README.md | Describe explicit layout responsibility, graph ownership, scope, supported profile, float clears, raw pixels/strides, examples, evidence, and limits. Move begin/end and actual attachment clear wording from M3 to M2. M3 retains draw/pipeline/viewport work. |

Keep the native FFI in its existing imported translation unit. A separate C include file can break arbitrary Bend output paths unless emitted include resolution is established. This design accepts a larger native.c to avoid introducing an unproven build boundary in M2. Group image policy, graph helpers, and FFI handlers visibly within the file. The next maintainer traces a public effect directly to one native handler, with shared graph/arithmetic helpers nearby. Future native-file extraction is separate, evidence-driven work.

### Pure helper boundary and dispatch changes

`src/core.bend` cannot import `Vulkan.bend`, which already imports Core. New pure helpers therefore accept numeric fields and upstream U64 directly. The following signatures avoid that import cycle and supply specific law targets.

```bend
def image_mip_dimension(base: U32, level: U32) -> U32:
def image_range_contains(limit: U32, base: U32, count: U32) -> Bool:
def image_copy_end(offset: W.U64, row_length: U32, image_height: U32,
  width: U32, height: U32, layers: U32, element_bytes: U32) -> Maybe<W.U64>:
```

`image_copy_end` returns the exclusive end or None for zero required dimensions, insufficient padding dimensions, or U64 overflow. `image_mip_dimension` floors positive dimensions at one and defines levels >=32 without an undefined shift. The native decoder independently validates the foreign boundary and uses the same mathematical contract. Runtime probes compare native results to literal expected spans at overflow and last-row boundaries. They do not treat a Bend helper's answer as native validation authority.

The instance table gains `PFN_vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties`. `BV_DEVICE_FUNCTIONS` gains CreateImage, DestroyImage, GetImageMemoryRequirements, BindImageMemory, CreateImageView, DestroyImageView, CreateRenderPass, DestroyRenderPass, CreateFramebuffer, DestroyFramebuffer, CmdClearColorImage, CmdClearDepthStencilImage, CmdCopyBufferToImage, CmdCopyImageToBuffer, CmdBeginRenderPass, and CmdEndRenderPass. Existing CmdPipelineBarrier receives its image array. Load these as required core-1.0 functions through the existing device dispatch path. Missing dispatch must roll back the device using existing rules. Native BvDevice caches the chosen VkQueueFamilyProperties and VkPhysicalDeviceLimits once; the existing family index remains the selected identity.

### Destruction and cleanup

Each explicit destroy verifies device/kind, then rejects any incoming graph edge with BV_LIFETIME. Memory free uses the same incoming-edge query, so every bound image or buffer protects its allocation. Image/view/pass/framebuffer destruction never silently destroys dependencies. Removal frees its outgoing edges and owned metadata only after the native object's destroy call.

Entry cleanup first uses existing idle/loss recovery. For a safe device, destroy pools and command rows first, then fences, framebuffers, image views, render passes, images and buffers, allocations, and the device. Framebuffers disappear before their pass/views. Views disappear before images. All bound resources disappear before allocation free. Remove edges as each dependent dies. Private convenience-fence handling remains unchanged.

An ordinary idle error stops cleanup with the remaining device/entry and graph live for retry. Previously cleaned devices may already be gone, matching M1 partial cleanup behavior. Known device loss permits the same ordered teardown and reports exact loss bits. A callback failure keeps its original error and appends cleanup diagnostics. Explicit Device.destroy still requires public children gone. No new destructor turns a failed wait or timeout into assumed completion.

### Barrier and graph migration in one wave

Replace the existing barrier signature, rather than adding an image-only effect or preserving an old wrapper. Every current source caller appends `[]` as the new image list. Known call sites include examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend, tests/native.bend, tests/transfers.bend, tests/repeated.bend, native probe argument arrays in tests/probes.c, and the docs/API declaration. Search `pipeline_barrier`, `bv_cmd_pipeline_barrier`, and its `io_eff` registrations to cover all callers. The C handler reads f[5] for images after the existing lists.

Similarly migrate `row->bound`, its binding offset, and `command->uses` in production and controlled probes to graph accessors/deps, then remove those fields. No compatibility macros remain. Keep buffer copy alias behavior, completed reference retention, failed-reset behavior, and all M1 statuses unchanged. No code outside the one IO effect writer mutates graph edges or row metadata.

## Acceptance and fault evidence

The following are implementation gates, not results claimed by this candidate.

1. Real optimal-tiled RGBA8 clear. Use endpoint float colors, explicit transitions and transfer/host barriers. Submit with a real fence. Require actual SUCCESS before reading. Compare every pixel byte and reset before destruction.
2. Reuse and churn. Run at least 32 changing clear/readback cycles with reused command/fence and fixed resources. Separately create/destroy images, views, framebuffer, pass and allocations repeatedly. Warm the existing private convenience fence before measuring rows. Assert stable live rows during reuse and the exact pre-cycle row count after each destruction round. Finish with zero wrapper rows after Entry close.
3. Nonuniform addressing. Upload the two-layer padded example, use a nonzero buffer bind offset as well as buffer offset when supported memory-type intersection permits, and read into a different padded stride/offset. Check every channel, coordinate, layer, sentinel padding byte, and untouched image pixel. Repeat on a nonzero mip. No uniform clear is counted as orientation evidence.
4. Real render pass. Run color+depth CLEAR/STORE via begin/end with zero draws, then copy color and preferably D32 depth. Compare exact expected bytes/float bits over the cleared area. Initialize full attachments first, then run a nonzero render area and verify inside versus preserved outside. If D32 plus transfer usage is unsupported, report the exact query and test a supported depth attachment. Label absent exact depth readback as a limitation rather than a pass.
5. Public negative cases. Wrong-device operands for each resource relation, forged/wrong-kind/stale keys, rejected wrapper profile, real or controlled unsupported configuration, out-of-range mip/layer/area, bad aspect/format/view compatibility, mismatched count/type of clear values, unbound image, and layout/usage incompatibility. Never send a knowingly wrong execution-time layout to the real driver to test wrapper behavior that the design cannot validate.
6. Lifetime and active host exclusion. Record only framebuffer use, submit it, then prove host access rejects the reached image allocation and a buffer bound disjointly in it. Prove an unrelated allocation remains accessible. Check Pending timeout/NOT_READY and Uncertain retain protection. On observed completion host access succeeds, while framebuffer/view/image/memory destruction still rejects in the relevant retained order. Reset releases command edges; a live framebuffer still protects pass/views. Failed reset retains refs. Pool teardown removes them when safe. Exercise explicit close, retry after ordinary idle error, and known-loss cleanup.
7. Controlled preparation failures. Fail each new allocation site in turn, including schema arrays, framebuffer edge arrays, region arrays, clear arrays, and dependency nodes. Assert no void dispatch count changed, prior refs/scope stayed intact, and live rows returned to baseline. Inject create image/view/pass/framebuffer failures, binding failure, and insertion failure if that path exists. Successful native creation followed by metadata failure destroys the native object exactly once. Failed binding leaves no graph edge. Query FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED preserves exact bits and ignores poisoned outputs.
8. Controlled dispatch structure. Inspect sType, null pNext/allocator, counts, formats, samples, identity mappings, all clear fields, explicit pass initial/final layouts, INLINE contents, queue-family IGNORED indices, U64 high limbs, row span overflow, opposite bind-order granularity rejection, and destination overlap. Use a host-only call counter to prove old fill/copy/barrier reject Inside. Injected driver loss/uncertainty reuses existing command machinery and does not claim real GPU execution.
9. Compatibility gates. Generator freshness, all existing suites, new native suites, `bend PROOF.bend`, and `tools/verify.py --sanitize`. Keep ASan/UBSan failures fatal. Existing disabled driver-global leak detection does not replace explicit row/edge teardown assertions. Khronos validation and synchronization validation are unavailable in the current environment. Record that accurately. If installed later, run them separately and state what actually executed.

Important pure laws cover raw U64 roundtrip, last-row span without trailing padding, zero row/image-height tight-packing equivalence, mip size floor one, range containment, and BGRA/RGBA byte expectation helpers. Native C independently uses checked arithmetic and is checked at literal boundaries against the same specification, not against a helper that would repeat its bug. Do not invent a theorem about native registry pointers or executed layout. `bend PROOF.bend` runs before every implementation commit.

## Ordered implementation units

Each unit has one owner and ends in verification plus a local commit. No PR workflow is assumed because no remote is configured. Add important laws as their pure functions appear.

1. Establish the ABI and direct graph foundation. Add new type/constructor ABI probes, raw tuple adapters, selected queue/limit cache, and BvDep accessors. Migrate existing buffers, commands, host-busy and destruction checks completely off bound/uses. Verify M1 real transfers, aliases, completion/failed-reset/uncertainty, all allocation-fault probes, generator freshness, and proofs. Commit the coherent graph migration with probe evidence.
2. Add image resources and configuration support. Extend instance/device dispatch, queries, image requirements/binding, views, supported-format metadata, both-order granularity checks, and ordered cleanup. Verify actual create/requirements/bind/view/destroy, unsupported-query bits, stale/wrong-device and persistent view refs, every new allocation/driver rollback path, existing suites, and proofs. Commit resources with documented profile.
3. Add image barriers, float clears, and buffer-image copies. Extend the sole barrier API and migrate all callers in this unit. Add Outside guards as preparation for passes, checked U64 region validation, new direct refs, and exact native F32 handling. Verify real every-pixel clear/readback and padded two-layer/nonzero-mip roundtrip, failed staging dispatch counters, overflow/overlap, old suites, generator freshness, sanitizers, and proofs. Commit image transfer capability and its runnable example.
4. Add render-pass/framebuffer schema and executable scope. Create persistent edges, enforce slot compatibility, marshal clear variants, implement begin/end, and extend reset/end/old-command scope guards. Update cleanup and move roadmap wording into M2. Verify real color+depth pass clears and partial render area, transitive framebuffer host-busy, nested/unmatched scope, failed-reset persistence, wrong format/aspect/clear shape, and all creation/metadata faults. Run sanitizers and proofs before committing.
5. Finish full-cycle acceptance and public documentation. Add repeated resource churn, exact live-row assertions, teardown/retry scenarios, raw pixel/stride/encoding explanation, and current validation availability. Run the complete fresh verifier with sanitizers, generator check, and proofs. Independently inspect pixel expectations and the final ownership graph. Commit the completed milestone evidence and docs.

Throughput is limited by one coupled writer and real GPU acceptance, not by candidate drafting. Pure pattern production and unrelated test input generation can be parallel. Registry scans and Vulkan calls must not move to independent workers. No measured performance claim is made.

## Alternatives considered and where this candidate loses

These are whole designs, not renamed versions of the chosen graph.

| Design | Caller responsibility and hidden complexity | Why it loses here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chosen explicit resources/layouts plus direct native graph | Caller selects memory, layouts, barriers, and execution order. Native code hides validation, ownership closure, scope, and marshalling. | It provides fewer synchronization diagnostics and repeats caller barrier code. It is the smallest extension of the present checked Vulkan boundary without a second mutable model. |
| Command-local transition plans with submit-time preconditions and completion-time image versions, plus expanded retained closures | Caller declares desired image uses. A planner generates barriers, retains all reached objects, and tracks entry/exit subresource versions. It must define when two recordings conflict, how reset retracts a plan, how OOM preserves a plan, how uncertain submission poisons layouts, and how pass final transitions merge. | This can offer a deeper command interface and catch wrong-layout mistakes. It introduces a new scheduling/version system beside the authoritative command state and much larger subresource metadata. It would win for a renderer framework with many generated passes. M2 does not yet have that consumer. |
| Owned OffscreenTarget aggregate with atomic create/allocate/view/pass/framebuffer and a render/readback operation | Caller selects target size/format and calls clear/read. Aggregate code hides nearly all resource coordination and can own a layout state safely only if it monopolizes recording/submission. A target command list retains the whole aggregate. | It has the smallest caller interface and would win for a fixed offscreen tool. To coexist with public image/barrier/memory APIs it needs escape hatches or parallel ownership/layout routes. Monopolizing submission would replace the M1 wrapper contract and restrict M3 attachment reuse. |

Direct-edge queries scan live rows and direct edges. Busy traversal can revisit shared descendants through multiple framebuffer/view paths. The DAG bounds path depth, while the cost still scales with traversed paths. Expanded command closures or incoming counters would speed some lookups. They also duplicate reachability information that must survive creation rollback and reset. The fixed DAG and existing single active command make direct traversal a better M2 trade. No benchmark evidence is claimed.

The fixed pass layouts lose automatic UNDEFINED-to-attachment and final transfer transitions. Callers write barriers even for simple clears. In exchange, transfer and pass callers share one explicit transition route. Supporting arbitrary initial/final layouts later would be a deliberate API expansion with dependency policy, not an incidental metadata field.

Exact render-pass identity loses Vulkan's compatible-pass reuse. Fixed one-layer framebuffers and one sample lose layered rendering and MSAA. The next indexed-graphics stage uses neither. General mips/layers, 2D-array views, multiple colors, schema metadata, and full image usage metadata keep ordinary future graphics additions in the existing architecture.

Disallowing image aliasing loses temporary render-target memory reuse. Conservative copy destination intervals can reject safe padding interleaving. Allocation-wide host exclusion can block an unrelated buffer in the same allocation. These rules buy a readable safety boundary without an optimal-image memory-layout oracle, byte-set solver, or new active-range truth. They are documented limits, not hidden driver assumptions.

Finite float clear values lose NaN/Infinity payload testing and integer-color clears. The supported format list makes that boundary explicit. Wider formats need a numeric clear variant and an ABI probe rather than treating bitwise U32 words as convenient colors.

The native file grows. The design keeps direct effect-to-handler paths and one authoritative graph, but a future audited file split may improve maintainability once the emitted C include behavior is established.

## Principles that changed this design

I read the leaf skills named here in this session.

- Foundational Thinking put the graph, supported image profile, and ABI probe before new command handlers.
- Model the Domain selected a typed dependency DAG and a Recording-only Outside/Inside payload instead of a collection of independent busy/render booleans.
- Boundary Discipline keeps forgeable-handle, format, stride, scope, and clear validation at native effect entry. Internal code consumes validated metadata.
- Type System Discipline uses distinct handle types and clear variants. It keeps render-pass color/depth schema and ordered framebuffer attachments explicit while acknowledging that U32 masks still need runtime checks.
- Separate Before Serializing Shared State leaves each design artifact independent and keeps the one real registry on the existing IO writer. It rejects a second layout writer or an image-specific pending table.
- Prove It Works requires literal full readback, nonuniform addressing, native dispatch counters, and row/edge evidence. This design document itself is not runtime evidence.

## Synthesis decision

This is the explicit-layout/direct-edge candidate for the parent's arena. It recommends its own shape on the terms above. It does not claim to have compared unseen candidates or to have completed independent cross-judging. Parent synthesis may choose a different whole design and record which parts it adopts.

## Residual experiments and next step

These questions have concrete implementation-time answers. None requests permission.

- What exact flattening, packing, Maybe tags, and F32 bit conventions does Bend 2.0.37 emit for the proposed types? Resolve with the first unit's native-called ABI probe before writing field counts.
- Which selected device supports RGBA8/BGRA8 attachment and transfer configurations, and D32_SFLOAT with depth attachment plus transfer-source usage? Resolve with exact configuration queries and record returned values/results.
- Does exact D32 readback after both direct clear and render-pass clear return 0x3f000000 everywhere? Resolve through a real graphics queue with completion and host visibility, separate from injected probes.
- Can available memory types support a disjoint buffer/image shared-allocation positive case? Resolve using intersected memory_type_bits. Always run the controlled both-order overlap/page-boundary cases even when the physical positive case cannot be formed.
- Which actual selected non-graphics queues exist, and what granularity do they report? Exercise available real configurations and cover unavailable coarse/zero/depth-queue cases with dispatch substitution, clearly labeled.
- Does the emitted native translation unit preserve source-relative include resolution if a later split becomes desirable? Resolve as a separate bounded compiler experiment rather than introducing a guessed include path into M2.

Start with the source-level ABI probe and the direct-graph migration. Preserve M1 behavior before attaching new resource kinds to it.
"}

Candidate 3’s argument about fallible general-graph safety queries therefore does not apply to candidate 1’s actual proposal. The following findings affect selection or require correction before implementation.

1. **Candidate 2 has a blocking omission in view validation.** Its profile permits transfer-only images, while its specified view checks require binding and valid ranges but omit a view-eligible usage. Implemented literally, that permits an invalid `vkCreateImageView`. Within these profiles, require at least one of SAMPLED, COLOR_ATTACHMENT, or DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT, and validate inherited usage features. Candidates 1 and 3 explicitly include this rule. This is an actual Vulkan requirement. [Candidate 2 omission](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/candidate-2/design.md:271), [Khronos view requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImageViewCreateInfo.html).

2. **Candidate 2’s external dependencies need a precise transfer contract.** In `VkSubpassDependency`, ALL_COMMANDS is equivalent to ALL_GRAPHICS. Its proposed dependencies must not be interpreted as covering transfer or host stages. The candidate does require separate synchronization, so this is not proof that every proposed pass is invalid. Specify the complete dependency chain for transfer → automatic transition → attachment use, and the reverse direction. Include TRANSFER explicitly where intended. [Proposed masks](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/candidate-2/design.md:489), [Khronos dependency semantics](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/renderpass.html).

3. **Zero subpass dependencies are not a blocker for candidates 1 and 3.** Their initial, subpass, and final layouts are identical, and callers provide outside barriers. For their single-subpass profile, mandatory broad external dependencies would add policy without fixing a demonstrated gap. Keep the explicit barrier contract. [Candidate 1](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/candidate-1/design.md:454), [Khronos synchronization examples](https://docs.vulkan.org/guide/latest/synchronization_examples.html).

4. **All three address pending protection and creation rollback adequately at design level.** Candidate 1 traverses the dependency chain. Candidate 3 retains its immutable closure. Candidate 2 uses graph reachability independently of layout plans. All retain references after completion and failed reset, reserve metadata before void commands, and destroy successful native creations when publication fails. I found no remaining lifecycle blocker in those specified mechanisms.

5. **Make the framebuffer-only protection test genuinely independent.** Establish attachment layouts in an earlier submission, observe completion, and reset that recording. Then submit a command containing only framebuffer begin/end. Otherwise direct image-barrier references can mask a broken framebuffer-to-memory path. Assert exact lifetime errors through Pending, timeout, and Uncertain, followed by the correct completion/reset behavior. This strengthens [candidate 1’s existing test requirement](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/candidate-1/design.md:566).

6. **The U64 formulas are sound, but upstream arithmetic is not automatically checked.** Candidate 1’s example ends are correctly 192 and 284 bytes. Candidate 3’s single-layer example ends at 52 bytes. Preserve checked multiplication/addition and the final-row formula. The installed upstream [`W.add`](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend:37) wraps. Implement checked pure helpers explicitly, while keeping independent native boundary checks.

7. **Correct the distinction between Vulkan requirements and wrapper policies.** Four-byte buffer offsets are required for these depth/stencil copies, including D16. The copy specification also imposes a row-length byte bound. These should not be described solely as arbitrary conservatism. Conversely, allocation-wide host exclusion, rejecting image aliasing, padding-envelope overlap rejection, exact pass identity, dense clear placeholders, and finite-only color clears are wrapper policies. [Khronos copy requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html).

8. **Document depth-upload contents as a caller obligation.** Candidates 1 and 3 support buffer-to-depth-image copies without stating the baseline source-value restriction as clearly as candidate 2. Depth upload values must satisfy the applicable `[0,1]` rule. Do not add GPU-buffer inspection merely to enforce it. [Khronos depth-copy contract](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html).

9. **Keep native creation authoritative for actual image footprint.** A logical texel calculation cannot certify `maxResourceSize`. Candidate 2’s post-creation requirements comparison also should not be presented as an additional Vulkan validity requirement. Preserve actual `vkCreateImage` failures and use returned memory requirements for binding. [Khronos image-size definition](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImageFormatProperties.html).

The installed compiler reports Bend 2.0.37. Existing emitted C confirms flattened U64 fields and provides [`f32_unbox` and `f32_rewrap`](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/build/transfers-probes.c:1403). This makes speculative public `Float32Bits` fallback design unnecessary now. It does **not** establish the new nested constructor layouts. The first implementation gate must still exercise actual effect calls with distinct limbs, float lanes, clear variants, Maybe alternatives, and lists. Never substitute numeric `F32.to_u32` conversion for bit interpretation.

The coherent synthesis should adopt these parts together:

- Keep candidate 1’s direct dependency graph, explicit layouts, Recording-only scope, unified barrier migration, and transactional recording.
- Adopt candidate 3’s six formats and depth-only public descriptions. Remove combined depth/stencil formats and associated stencil options consistently across types, validation, copies, clears, and documentation.
- Adopt candidate 3’s conditional D16 endpoint readback fallback when its complete configuration is supported. Report D32 evidence separately.
- Retain candidate 1’s five implementation units, full allocation-fault coverage, and actual color/depth pass execution.

Reject candidate 2’s ledger for this milestone. It correctly separates recording proposals from completion observations, so it is not an unsafe recording-time global cache. Its epochs, read-only invalidation, cell cap, and forced re-recording are nevertheless additional conservative policies. The requested wrapper does not need them.

Do not graft candidate 3’s flattened command sets into candidate 1’s graph. Either ownership approach is coherent alone. Combining them creates another representation of reachability without a demonstrated need.

The architect red-flag screen favors that synthesis. All candidates keep a direct public-to-native path and migrate the barrier API. Candidate 1 best avoids hand-maintained closure expansion. Candidate 3’s immutable snapshots are sound, but future kinds require coordinated expansion and incoming-reference logic. Raw adapters remain importable because Bend lacks private visibility; retain one checked native operation underneath them. Vulkan setup verbosity is appropriate for the requested ash-like wrapper and is not, by itself, evidence that an OffscreenTarget renderer abstraction is needed.

The narrowed synthesis supports the next indexed graphics and voxel-mesh stages. It preserves color/depth attachments, mips, arrays, multiple colors, raw transfers, and explicit synchronization. Pipelines and indexed draws can extend the existing render scope. Meshing, material interpretation, and vertex layout remain consumer responsibilities, consistent with the [roadmap](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/docs/roadmap.md:94).

Laziness Protocol shaped the rejection of the ledger and unnecessary stencil breadth. Type System Discipline supports the tagged recording scope and clear variants.

No adversarial interrogation is needed merely because candidates 1 and 3 tie. Both ownership models are defensible. If the parent prefers candidate 2’s ledger or retains its automatic-transition policy, interrogate those specific costs and transfer dependency chains before coding. For their single-subpass profile, mandatory broad external dependencies would add policy without fixing a demonstrated gap. Keep the explicit barrier contract. [Candidate 1](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/candidate-1/design.md:454), [Khronos synchronization examples](https://docs.vulkan.org/guide/latest/synchronization_examples.html).

4. **All three address pending protection and creation rollback adequately at design level.** Candidate 1 traverses the dependency chain. Candidate 3 retains its immutable closure. Candidate 2 uses graph reachability independently of layout plans. All retain references after completion and failed reset, reserve metadata before void commands, and destroy successful native creations when publication fails. I found no remaining lifecycle blocker in those specified mechanisms.

5. **Make the framebuffer-only protection test genuinely independent.** Establish attachment layouts in an earlier submission, observe completion, and reset that recording. Then submit a command containing only framebuffer begin/end. Otherwise direct image-barrier references can mask a broken framebuffer-to-memory path. This strengthens [candidate 1’s existing test requirement](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/candidate-1/design.md:566).

6. **The U64 formulas are sound, but upstream arithmetic is not automatically checked.** Candidate 1’s example ends are correctly 192 and 284 bytes. Implement checked pure helpers explicitly, while keeping independent native boundary checks.

7. **Correct the distinction between Vulkan requirements and wrapper policies.** Four-byte buffer offsets are required for these depth/stencil copies, including D16. The copy specification also imposes a row-length byte bound. These should not be described solely as arbitrary conservatism. Conversely, allocation-wide host exclusion, rejecting image aliasing, padding-envelope overlap rejection, exact pass identity, dense clear placeholders, and finite-only color clears are wrapper policies. [Khronos copy requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html).

8. **Document depth-upload contents as a caller obligation.** Candidates 1 and 3 support buffer-to-depth-image copies without stating the baseline source-value restriction as clearly as candidate 2. Depth upload values must satisfy the applicable `[0,1]` rule. Do not add GPU-buffer inspection merely to enforce it. [Khronos depth-copy contract](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html).

The installed compiler reports Bend 2.0.37. This makes speculative public `Float32Bits` fallback design unnecessary now. It does **not** establish the new nested constructor layouts. The first implementation gate must still exercise actual effect calls with distinct limbs, float lanes, clear variants, Maybe alternatives, and lists. Never substitute numeric `F32.to_u32` conversion for bit interpretation.

- Keep candidate 1’s direct dependency graph, explicit layouts, Recording-only scope, unified barrier migration, and transactional recording.
- Adopt candidate 3’s six formats and depth-only public descriptions. Remove combined depth/stencil formats and associated stencil options consistently across types, validation, copies, clears, and documentation.
- Adopt candidate 3’s conditional D16 endpoint readback fallback when its complete configuration is supported. Report D32 evidence separately.
- Retain candidate 1’s five implementation units, full allocation-fault coverage, and actual color/depth pass execution.

Reject candidate 2’s ledger for this milestone. It correctly separates recording proposals from completion observations, so it is not an unsafe recording-time global cache. Its epochs, read-only invalidation, cell cap, and forced re-recording are nevertheless additional conservative policies. The requested wrapper does not need them.

Do not graft candidate 3’s flattened command sets into candidate 1’s graph. Either ownership approach is coherent alone. Combining them creates another representation of reachability without a demonstrated need.

The architect red-flag screen favors that synthesis. All candidates keep a direct public-to-native path and migrate the barrier API. Candidate 1 best avoids hand-maintained closure expansion. Candidate 3’s immutable snapshots are sound, but future kinds require coordinated expansion and incoming-reference logic. Raw adapters remain importable because Bend lacks private visibility; retain one checked native operation underneath them. Vulkan setup verbosity is appropriate for the requested ash-like wrapper and is not, by itself, evidence that an OffscreenTarget renderer abstraction is needed.

The narrowed synthesis supports the next indexed graphics and voxel-mesh stages. It preserves color/depth attachments, mips, arrays, multiple colors, raw transfers, and explicit synchronization. Pipelines and indexed draws can extend the existing render scope. Meshing, material interpretation, and vertex layout remain consumer responsibilities, consistent with the [roadmap](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/docs/roadmap.md:94).

Laziness Protocol shaped the rejection of the ledger and unnecessary stencil breadth. Type System Discipline supports the tagged recording scope and clear variants.

No adversarial interrogation is needed merely because candidates 1 and 3 tie. Both ownership models are defensible. If the parent prefers candidate 2’s ledger or retains its automatic-transition policy, interrogate those specific costs and transfer dependency chains before coding. All review seats use the configured same model; agreement here establishes no model diversity.

description: "Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Model the Domain

Encode the real domain in a data structure instead of scattering it across conditionals.

**Why:** Scattered booleans, repeated shape assumptions, and branching spread across files are accidental complexity. A structure that matches the domain makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches. Choosing it at write time is cheap. Recovering it later reads as a refactor and gets deferred.

**Reach for structures like these:**

- A state machine instead of scattered booleans, phases, or lifecycle checks.
- A typed object/model instead of loose parameters or repeated shape assumptions.
- A map, registry, lookup table, or discriminated union instead of branching spread across files.
- A reducer or command/event model instead of ad hoc state mutations.
- A module organized around one body of domain knowledge instead of a sequence such as load, validate, transform, and save. Execution order is not ownership.
- A small module boundary that gathers repeated behavior, ownership, or invariants.
- A queue, cache, index, graph/tree, or normalized collection where the data access pattern calls for it.
- Any other structure that fits. When none fits, work out what the code must never allow and how the data gets read, then find the structure that encodes exactly that.

Do not force an abstraction. Prefer boring code if the current shape is already clear, local, and unlikely to grow. Be skeptical of an abstraction that adds indirection without removing branches, duplicated rules, invalid states, or lifecycle risk.

The sign that you skipped this is a new feature that grows an existing if/else chain by one more branch, or a second boolean that must stay in sync with the first. Temporal decomposition is another sign. Phase-named modules repeat the same domain rules across steps.
---
name: principle-boundary-discipline
description: "Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Boundary Discipline

Place validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.

**Why:** Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.

**The pattern:**
- **At boundaries** (CLI args, config files, external APIs, network protocols): validate, return errors, handle defensively.
- **Inside the system:** typed data, error propagation, no re-validation. Trust the types.
- **Across the boundary.** Expose domain concepts, not the boundary's private representation. Keep general-purpose mechanism inside and special-purpose policy at the edge.

**Applications:**

Validation and error handling:
- Validate config at parse time (the boundary), not inside business logic
- Parse raw data into domain types at the boundary
- Do not re-export transport, storage, framework, or wire types through the public surface
- No redundant nil checks deep in call chains if the boundary already validated

Code organization:
- Business logic in pure functions with no framework dependencies
- Parse functions: pure transforms from raw bytes to typed state
- Prompt construction: structured state in, string out
- Scoring and assessment: pure transforms from state to results

**The tests:**
- "Is this data crossing a system boundary right now?" If not, validation is redundant.
- "Can this be a pure function that the shell just calls?" If yes, extract it.
---
name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
description: "Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Sequence work into verifiable units

Order work as a sequence of small units, each ending in a state you can check, and don't advance until the current one is green.

**Why:** A break caught at the unit that caused it is cheap to localize. A break caught after a batch is buried, and you have already built further on a broken base. Sequencing those same units into a delivery a reviewer can replay turns "trust me" into "watch it go red, then green."

**Execution.** In a sweep, migration, or any run of similar edits, verify each change before starting the next. Each unit is a before/after bracket: known-good state, one change, run the check, then proceed. Rebase onto clean trunk first so every check measures against the real baseline. When a lever does the edits, the per-unit check is nearly free. Run it anyway.

**Delivery.** Stack commits and PRs in the order that proves the work. The canonical shape is the failing test first, then the fix on top. Other story orders are a subtraction before the reshape, a baseline capture before the treatment, the scaffold before the feature. Each commit lands on its own and the sequence reads as an argument.

The sequencing complement to the [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md) principle skill, which keeps each check real, and the [Build the Lever](../principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md) principle skill, which makes the per-unit check cheap.
---
name: principle-prove-it-works
description: "Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'"
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Prove It Works

Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or "it compiles."

**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.

Check the real thing, not a proxy:
- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state
- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation
- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system

## Script the check when you can

The strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.

Keep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).

# P3 delegated worker

You are operating as p3-mode's full agent style. Read `skills/p3-mode/SKILL.md` in full before doing any work, including its inline Principles index. Navigate to a leaf `principle-*` skill whenever you apply that principle.

Your brief is everything you know. You do not inherit the parent's context. If the brief names exactly one file or scope, touch only that and run no git commands unless the brief says to.
---
name: principle-model-the-domain
description: "Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Model the Domain

Encode the real domain in a data structure instead of scattering it across conditionals.

**Why:** Scattered booleans, repeated shape assumptions, and branching spread across files are accidental complexity. A structure that matches the domain makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches. Choosing it at write time is cheap. Recovering it later reads as a refactor and gets deferred.

**Reach for structures like these:**

- A state machine instead of scattered booleans, phases, or lifecycle checks.
- A typed object/model instead of loose parameters or repeated shape assumptions.
- A map, registry, lookup table, or discriminated union instead of branching spread across files.
- A reducer or command/event model instead of ad hoc state mutations.
- A module organized around one body of domain knowledge instead of a sequence such as load, validate, transform, and save. Execution order is not ownership.
- A small module boundary that gathers repeated behavior, ownership, or invariants.
- A queue, cache, index, graph/tree, or normalized collection where the data access pattern calls for it.
- Any other structure that fits. When none fits, work out what the code must never allow and how the data gets read, then find the structure that encodes exactly that.

Do not force an abstraction. Prefer boring code if the current shape is already clear, local, and unlikely to grow. Be skeptical of an abstraction that adds indirection without removing branches, duplicated rules, invalid states, or lifecycle risk.

The sign that you skipped this is a new feature that grows an existing if/else chain by one more branch, or a second boolean that must stay in sync with the first. Temporal decomposition is another sign. Phase-named modules repeat the same domain rules across steps.
---
name: principle-boundary-discipline
description: "Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Boundary Discipline

Place validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.

**Why:** Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.

**The pattern:**
- **At boundaries** (CLI args, config files, external APIs, network protocols): validate, return errors, handle defensively.
- **Inside the system:** typed data, error propagation, no re-validation. Trust the types.
- **Across the boundary.** Expose domain concepts, not the boundary's private representation. Keep general-purpose mechanism inside and special-purpose policy at the edge.

**Applications:**

Validation and error handling:
- Validate config at parse time (the boundary), not inside business logic
- Parse raw data into domain types at the boundary
- Do not re-export transport, storage, framework, or wire types through the public surface
- No redundant nil checks deep in call chains if the boundary already validated

Code organization:
- Business logic in pure functions with no framework dependencies
- Parse functions: pure transforms from raw bytes to typed state
- Prompt construction: structured state in, string out
- Scoring and assessment: pure transforms from state to results

**The tests:**
- "Is this data crossing a system boundary right now?" If not, validation is redundant.
- "Can this be a pure function that the shell just calls?" If yes, extract it.
---
name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
description: "Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Sequence work into verifiable units

Order work as a sequence of small units, each ending in a state you can check, and don't advance until the current one is green.

**Why:** A break caught at the unit that caused it is cheap to localize. A break caught after a batch is buried, and you have already built further on a broken base. Sequencing those same units into a delivery a reviewer can replay turns "trust me" into "watch it go red, then green."

**Execution.** In a sweep, migration, or any run of similar edits, verify each change before starting the next. Each unit is a before/after bracket: known-good state, one change, run the check, then proceed. Rebase onto clean trunk first so every check measures against the real baseline. When a lever does the edits, the per-unit check is nearly free. Run it anyway.

**Delivery.** Stack commits and PRs in the order that proves the work. The canonical shape is the failing test first, then the fix on top. Other story orders are a subtraction before the reshape, a baseline capture before the treatment, the scaffold before the feature. Each commit lands on its own and the sequence reads as an argument.

The sequencing complement to the [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md) principle skill, which keeps each check real, and the [Build the Lever](../principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md) principle skill, which makes the per-unit check cheap.
---
name: principle-prove-it-works
description: "Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'"
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Prove It Works

Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or "it compiles."

**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.

Check the real thing, not a proxy:
- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state
- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation
- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system

## Script the check when you can

The strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.

Keep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).

+# Milestone 2 implementation contract
+
+## Decision and evidence
+
+Use candidate 1 as the base. Both parent and independent cross-judge selected it after reading every complete candidate. Parent scores were 27/24/26; judge scores were 27/23/27. Scores compare design completeness, not executed implementation. See parent-candidate-notes.md, design-judge.md and rubric.md beside this file.
+
+Keep direct native dependency edges, caller-owned execution-time layouts, Recording-only render scope, transactional preparation and the single extended barrier operation. Graft candidate 3's six-format depth-only profile, lean 2D public descriptions, framebuffer-derived pass identity and exact D16 fallback. Candidate 1 already shares the fixed pass layouts and Vulkan texel-count copy fields. Use candidate 2's careful final-byte and failure examples as verification inputs only. Reject its per-subresource layout observations, epochs and command ledger. Reject flattened command closures and combined depth/stencil breadth. No contender was dropped. There is no contested design requiring interrogate.
+
+Model the Domain chose a role-tagged dependency DAG and a tagged render scope. Boundary Discipline keeps checks on forgeable Bend values at native effects. Separate Before Serializing Shared State gives temporary design artifacts distinct owners and leaves one IO writer for registry state. Laziness Protocol removes ledger and stencil breadth. Sequence Work into Verifiable Units orders graph preservation, resources, transfers, passes and acceptance. Prove It Works requires native GPU values and controlled fault evidence independently.
+
+## Caller behavior
+
+1. Query an exact image configuration. Create a 2D optimal image, get requirements, select a memory type, allocate and bind, optionally create a view. Allocation remains explicit.
+2. Begin a command; explicitly transition UNDEFINED to transfer destination; clear using ordinary F32 RGBA; transition to transfer source; copy to a bound readback buffer; add transfer-write to host-read synchronization; end, submit and observe SUCCESS; compare raw bytes. Reset before releasing recorded references. Use the candidate-1 first usage with the narrow types below.
+3. Create a pass with ordered color attachment descriptions and optional depth description. Create a framebuffer with that pass and matching views. Transition images explicitly to attachment layouts, begin/end the framebuffer pass with ordered typed clears, transition to transfer source, copy and observe completion. The pass supplies no hidden transitions. Pipelines/draws remain milestone 3.
+
+Layouts and previous contents are caller assertions at execution. Recording, reset, submission, completion and recovery mutate no image-layout cache. Unknown execution after an unexpected submit error requires idle recovery followed by deliberate discard/overwrite or recreation before relying on data. The wrapper checks structural validity, ownership, ranges, masks and usage, and does not prove actual layout history or initialization.
+
+## Exact public shape
+
+Add Image, ImageView, RenderPass and Framebuffer Data handles with one U32 key, following existing handles. Keep all sizes, offsets and capacities as pinned W.U64. In Vulkan.bend add:
+
+```bend
+type Extent2D is Data:
+  Extent2D{width: U32, height: U32}
+type Offset2D is Data:
+  Offset2D{x: U32, y: U32}
+type RenderArea is Data:
+  RenderArea{offset: Offset2D, extent: Extent2D}
+type ImageFormatInfo is Data:
+  ImageFormatInfo{format: U32, image_type: U32, tiling: U32, usage: U32, flags: U32}
+type ImageFormatProperties is Data:
+  ImageFormatProperties{max_width: U32, max_height: U32, max_depth: U32,
+    max_mip_levels: U32, max_array_layers: U32, sample_counts: U32, max_resource_size: W.U64}
+type ImageCreateInfo is Data:
+  ImageCreateInfo{format: U32, extent: Extent2D, mip_levels: U32, array_layers: U32, usage: U32}
+type ImageSubresourceRange is Data:
+  ImageSubresourceRange{aspect_mask: U32, base_mip_level: U32, level_count: U32,
+    base_array_layer: U32, layer_count: U32}
+type ImageSubresourceLayers is Data:
+  ImageSubresourceLayers{aspect_mask: U32, mip_level: U32, base_array_layer: U32, layer_count: U32}
+type ImageViewCreateInfo is Data:
+  ImageViewCreateInfo{image: Image, view_type: U32, range: ImageSubresourceRange}
+type ImageMemoryBarrier is Data:
+  ImageMemoryBarrier{image: Image, range: ImageSubresourceRange,
+    old_layout: U32, new_layout: U32, src_access: U32, dst_access: U32}
+type BufferImageCopy is Data:
+  BufferImageCopy{buffer_offset: W.U64, buffer_row_length: U32, buffer_image_height: U32,
+    image_subresource: ImageSubresourceLayers, image_offset: Offset2D, image_extent: Extent2D}
+type ClearColor is Data:
+  ClearColor{r: F32, g: F32, b: F32, a: F32}
+type ClearValue is Data:
+  ColorClear{value: ClearColor}
+  DepthClear{depth: F32}
+  UnusedClear{}
+type AttachmentInfo is Data:
+  AttachmentInfo{format: U32, load_op: U32, store_op: U32}
+type RenderPassCreateInfo is Type:
+  RenderPassCreateInfo{colors: List<AttachmentInfo>, depth: Maybe<AttachmentInfo>}
+type FramebufferCreateInfo is Type:
+  FramebufferCreateInfo{render_pass: RenderPass, attachments: List<ImageView>, extent: Extent2D}
+```
+
+New operations follow existing IO(VkResult(...)) conventions:
+
+- Instance.get_physical_device_image_format_properties(instance,physical,info) returns ImageFormatProperties through a generated raw-limb effect plus pure adapter.
+- Device.create_image(device,info), destroy_image(device,image), get_image_memory_requirements(device,image), bind_image_memory(device,image,memory,offset), create_image_view(device,info), destroy_image_view(device,view).
+- Device.create_render_pass(device,info), destroy_render_pass(device,pass), create_framebuffer(device,info), destroy_framebuffer(device,framebuffer).
+- CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,src_stage,dst_stage,memory,buffers,images). Append the image list to the sole existing operation and migrate every caller and raw test vector in the same unit.

+

Append buffer_image_granularity:W.U64 to PhysicalDeviceLimits and its raw adapter. Cache full selected queue properties and physical limits internally. Do not add duplicate queue selection APIs or expose native pointers. Generator owns effects/constants/JS rejection. Existing owned-array policies remain unchanged.
+
+## Supported image and render profile
+
+2D optimal, depth one, exclusive sharing, flags zero, initial UNDEFINED, one sample. Positive mips/layers are configurable within exact configuration and full-mip-chain limits. Six format traits in one native table: RGBA8 and BGRA8 UNORM/SRGB, D16_UNORM and D32_SFLOAT. No stencil, compressed/multiplanar/integer color, reinterpretation, swizzle, sparse/external/linear or MSAA support. Do not expose stencil fields in the narrowed public API. Clear-depth maps to VkClearDepthStencilValue with stencil zero.
+
+Usages are a nonempty subset of transfer source/destination, sampled, color attachment and depth attachment, matching format role. Views require a bound image, same format, identity mapping, a valid positive explicit range and view-eligible usage. Accept 2D single-layer or 2D_ARRAY views. Configuration discovery can query recognized core-1.0 formats/types/tilings/usage/flags outside this creation profile. Invalid enum values reject at the boundary; valid unsupported driver configurations preserve exact FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED bits 4294967285 and never read failed outputs. Creation queries exact configuration support, checks extent/count/sample/feature constraints, then lets native creation determine actual footprint. Requirements, not logical texel bytes, determine binding size.
+
+Framebuffers are one layer; attachment views must be 2D with exactly one selected mip/layer, matching ordered format/aspect/usage and sufficient mip extent. Multiple colors up to physical limit plus optional depth, at least one attachment. Reject overlapping attachment subresources. Passes have one inline graphics subpass, sample one, specified LOAD/CLEAR/DONT_CARE and STORE/DONT_CARE operations. Initial, subpass and final layouts are identical attachment-optimal values. No explicit subpass dependencies or automatic transitions. Callers provide the outside barriers. Stencil ops are always DONT_CARE.
+
+Clear list count equals attachment count. CLEAR slots require the corresponding ColorClear or DepthClear. Others require UnusedClear. Floats must be finite; depth is within [0,1]. Color conversion follows Vulkan's normalized/sRGB semantics. Positive signed-representable render offsets/extents must fit the framebuffer. Partial-area clears require prior initialization to claim preserved outside contents.
+
+## Native organizing structure
+
+Extend the checked registry with four kinds. Replace BvUse, BvRow.bound and binding offset with one role-tagged direct BvDep list. Allowed roles are recorded operand, binding, view-image, framebuffer-pass and framebuffer-view. Binding edge alone owns allocation pointer and offset. Framebuffer metadata holds ordered pointers into its own view edges. View image and framebuffer pass identity derive from their sole role edges. Cache exact VkMemoryRequirements on buffer/image rows once after native creation, distinct from buffer logical size. New image/view/pass/framebuffer metadata is typed according to the checked kind; it can use the existing context pattern instead of a second owner.
+
+Allowed edges: command -> buffer/image/framebuffer; buffer/image -> memory; framebuffer -> pass/view; view -> image. Parents retain device/pool ownership and are never resource-use traversal edges. Direct incoming edges reject destruction. Allocation-free bounded DAG reachability from the sole Pending/Uncertain command rejects host access to every reached allocation, including aliases. Do not add flattened closures, incoming counters, busy flags, reverse maps or layout state. All current M1 commands migrate to this graph and retain their existing lifetime semantics.
+
+Persistent edges are immutable until dependent destruction. Command roots deduplicate. Stage all metadata and marshal arrays before void dispatch; failure must preserve prior roots/scope and dispatch no command. Successful VkResult-returning creation followed by failed publication destroys the native object exactly once. Bind edges are staged before bind and published only on SUCCESS. Handle IDs never repeat.
+
+Recording gains a tagged Outside/Inside payload inside its phase union. Inside carries the active framebuffer as recording context; the dependency edge owns its lifetime. Existing Pending/Uncertain fence association remains authoritative. All transfers, fill, copies, clears and pipeline barriers require Outside. Reject nested begin, unmatched end and command end Inside before dispatch. Successful reset discards open recording and roots and returns Initial; failed reset Invalid retains roots. End-pass allocates nothing. Existing submit/observe/uncertainty/loss/convenience-fence paths remain shared and authoritative.
+
+Cleanup observes idle first using existing retry/loss semantics, then pools/commands, fences, framebuffers, views, passes, images/buffers, allocations and device. Explicit destruction never silently destroys dependencies. Loss keeps exact error bits and permits ordered teardown, ordinary idle failure retains the unsafe remainder.
+
+## Binding, copies and synchronization
+
+Use a common requirements-sized binding validator for images and buffers. Preserve buffer-buffer aliasing. Reject requirement interval overlap if either peer is an image. Mixed buffer/optimal-image suballocations additionally occupy disjoint bufferImageGranularity pages, checked in both bind orders with division of [offset,end-1]. Distinct nonoverlapping images may share an allocation. Validate checked U64 bounds, alignment and type bits; no logical optimal-image address is inferred.
+
+For copy region O,B,w,h,L and normalized texel row length R/image height H, compute checked U64 row=R*B, layer=H*row and end=O+(L-1)*layer+(h-1)*row+w*B. Zero padding fields normalize to w/h; positive fields must cover w/h. Require positive extents/layers, valid mip/aspect/layers, signed-representable nonnegative offsets and bounds. B comes from the format/aspect table. Check buffer logical range, binding allocation and arithmetic overflow. Do not count trailing padding after the last copied row. Vulkan's row-byte bound and depth four-byte offset requirement apply. For the accepted four-byte color formats, texel alignment also gives four-byte offsets. Do not claim optional optimal-copy alignment limits are mandatory.
+
+Reject overlapping destination image boxes or conservative destination-buffer envelopes across regions; repeated source reads are allowed. Cap nonempty region/barrier lists at 4096. Depth uploads require caller-provided values in [0,1]; do not inspect GPU buffer contents. Copies and clears take execution-time transfer-optimal or GENERAL layouts; barriers validate old/new layout compatibility, range and stage/access masks, use IGNORED family indices, and reject overlapping image subresource ranges within one call. UNDEFINED is only an old discard layout and requires source access zero by wrapper policy. Keep CommandBuffer.end free of implicit barriers.
+
+Color copies support graphics/compute/transfer queues with actual minImageTransferGranularity checks, including whole-mip zero granularity and per-axis edge exceptions. Depth copies/clears and render operations require graphics. Color clear requires graphics or compute. Image barriers use existing baseline queue stage/access checks. No new maintenance-feature relaxations are assumed.
+
+Raw copies preserve bytes: RGBA8 R,G,B,A; BGRA8 B,G,R,A; D16 little-endian UNORM; D32 little-endian IEEE binary32. SRGB copies preserve stored encoded bytes; float clears undergo format conversion. Increasing x then y then layer, no swizzle/flip. Example defines y0 as its first/top row, independently of future viewport convention. Explicit dimensions/strides define logical data, never array capacity.
+

+

+
+For framebuffer-only pending protection, prepare attachment layouts in an earlier completed submission, then reset that recording.
