items.text:
The existing wrapper is a checked Vulkan 1.0 resource and submission layer. Its main guarantees come from the native registry, command state machine, and explicit completion observations. Milestone 2 must extend those guarantees through images, views, render passes, and framebuffers. Pinned Voltra demonstrates a useful offscreen transfer/readback sequence, but its Vulkan 1.3 rendering and weaker lifetime checks are materially different.

This explanation synthesizes both explorer artifacts and the framing contract. Targeted source inspection resolved ABI and lifecycle details. No writes, git commands, builds, tests, or nested agents were used. The reported passing baseline belongs to the [framing artifact](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/framing.md:3), not a verification run performed here.

**Observed target behavior.** Bend handles are copyable `Data` constructors containing U32 registry keys. They can be fabricated, so native effects check kind and ownership before retrieving native handles. Keys increase monotonically and never repeat. Entry, instance, and device contexts hold separately loaded dispatch tables. Devices own one selected queue; pools own commands. Registry mutation runs synchronously on Bend’s IO event loop, so waits also block other IO effects. Pure preparation can run in parallel, while dependent Vulkan operations remain sequenced. See [registry and dispatch](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/src/native.c:17) and [execution model](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/docs/design.md:8).

The command owns the sole authoritative submission association. There is no separate device pending flag or fence backpointer. At most one command per device may be Pending or Uncertain.

# Bend Vulkan dispatch and ownership

Bend 2.0.37 cannot extend its opaque host-handle types. Ordinary Data constructors are copyable and forgeable.
The wrapper keeps native handles and dispatch in C and exposes distinct checked U32 registry keys.
`Entry.with` closes the resource tree after a callback returns either success or failure.
Allocation, binding, stage/access masks, timeouts, and reset remain explicit caller choices.

## Registry and dependencies

An Entry owns the loader library and global dispatch. An Instance owns instance dispatch and interned physical-device rows.
A Device owns device dispatch, one selected queue, and its resources. Pools own command buffers.
Buffers retain their bound allocations. Commands retain generic, deduplicated references to recorded resources.
Keys are monotonic and never reused, including after failed creation. Native pointers never come from public keys.
Every effect and registry mutation runs on Bend's IO event loop. Pure preparation can run in parallel.
Dependent Vulkan effects remain sequenced because they mutate the same queue and resource tree.

Recording validates every argument and reserves all reference nodes and marshaling arrays before any void `vkCmd*` dispatch.
Fill retains its buffer. Copy retains both buffers. Buffer barriers retain each mentioned buffer.
References survive completion and failed recording/reset. Successful individual reset or pool destruction releases them.
This keeps buffer destruction independent of whether hardware has finished but completion remains unobserved.
Copy overlap checks use allocation identity plus buffer binding offsets across all source/destination regions.

"""Run controlled dispatch and allocation probes in an emitted test translation unit."""
import argparse
import os

import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def build(sanitize=False):
    source = ROOT / "build/transfers-probes.c"
    binary = source.with_suffix("")
    source.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(["bend", "tests/probe_main.bend", "-o", str(source)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    emitted = source.read_text()
    probes = (ROOT / "tests/probes.c").read_text().replace(
        "/* LIFECYCLE PROBES */", (ROOT / "tests/lifecycle_probes.c").read_text())
    probes = probes.replace("/* CAPABILITY PROBES */", (ROOT / "tests/capability_probes.c").read_text())
    macros = re.findall(r"^#define (CID_\w+) \d+$", emitted, re.M)

    def cid(match):
        name = match[1].replace(".", "_").upper()
        matches = [m for m in macros if m == "CID_" + name or m.endswith("_VULKAN_" + name)]
        if len(matches) != 1:

Milestone 2 must extend those guarantees through images, views, render passes, and framebuffers. **Observed target behavior.** Bend handles are copyable `Data` constructors containing U32 registry keys. They can be fabricated, so native effects check kind and ownership before retrieving native handles. Keys increase monotonically and never repeat. Entry, instance, and device contexts hold separately loaded dispatch tables. Devices own one selected queue; pools own commands. Registry mutation runs synchronously on Bend’s IO event loop, so waits also block other IO effects. Pure preparation can run in parallel, while dependent Vulkan operations remain sequenced. The command owns the sole authoritative submission association. There is no separate device pending flag or fence backpointer. At most one command per device may be Pending or Uncertain.

# Independent milestone 2 acceptance checks

These checks evaluate observable behavior, without choosing a candidate's internal representation. The implementation owner supplies runnable evidence; the parent reruns the committed artifact.

| Behavior | Evidence required | What a weak test would miss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supported configuration | Query format/configuration before optimal image creation and choose supported color/depth formats | Generic format flags alone omit configuration limits |
| Exact transfer clear | Clear a known RGBA value, transition explicitly, copy to staging, observe fence completion, check every pixel | Compilation or checking one pixel misses wrong extents and incomplete work |
| Addressing and orientation | Upload nonuniform literal texels using nonzero buffer offset and padded rows, update a subrectangle, read back independently | Uniform clear cannot establish row stride, channel order or orientation |
| Attachment execution | Execute color and depth clears inside a real Vulkan 1.0 render pass, read color and supported depth output | Creating a framebuffer does not prove render-pass commands or clear ABI |
| Command scope | Reject nested begin, unmatched end, command end inside and disallowed transfer/barrier commands before dispatch; then complete a valid recording | An error that corrupts the recording can hide behind a negative-only test |
| Dependency lifetime | Block destruction through recorded framebuffer/view/image/allocation references, even after completion; successful reset/pool removal releases them | Direct image-transfer tests do not prove the framebuffer dependency chain |
| Pending host exclusion | Before any completion observation, reject host access through the framebuffer-t

This is a design proposal for milestone 2. The examples and declarations are a contract sketch, not compiled artifacts. Only this candidate directory was written. Repository inspection and `bend guide` were informational. No build, test, proof run, git command, or nested agent was used.

## Usage

The caller keeps explicit allocation, synchronization, and completion choices. Native code checks each recording against a private layout plan and checks that plan again at submission. A successful recording does not change an image's observed layout.

Layout compatibility has a single native table. GENERAL accepts any supported image. TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL require the corresponding usage. COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL requires a color format and COLOR_ATTACHMENT usage. Both DEPTH_STENCIL layouts require a depth format and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT usage. SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL requires SAMPLED usage. UNDEFINED is valid only in the source positions described above. Every old/new barrier value, clear/copy layout, and attachment layout uses this same table.

At device creation, cache the actual selected `VkQueueFamilyProperties`, rather than only its flags, and the needed physical limits. The graphics restriction covers Vulkan 1.0 depth-copy restrictions and avoids inventing a transfer-only queue granularity implementation. The existing buffer API remains usable on supported transfer queues. [Khronos queue properties](https://github.khronos.org/Vulkan-Site/spec/latest/chapters/devsandqueues.html) and [copy restrictions](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html) support that choice. Later support for transfer-only image queues can replace this boundary check without changing regions, ownership, or layouts.

`buffer_offset` is relative to the buffer, not its allocation. Add the canonical binding offset only for physical allocation checks. Require four-byte offset alignment for this baseline. That covers color texel alignment and the depth-copy requirement, including D16. U64 strides can exceed U32 bytes where valid, but Vulkan's actual texel-count fields and row-byte restriction still bound the accepted values. Never truncate a quotient. Vulkan receives `bufferRowLength = row / B`, `bufferImageHeight = layer / row`, `imageOffset.z = 0`, and `imageExtent.depth = 1`. [Khronos buffer-image copy fields](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkBufferImageCopy.html).

The final span excludes trailing padding after the last written row/layer. A one-pixel region in a long row therefore does not require an unused entire row at the buffer's end. Bounds must use the checked final address, not `offset + row * height * layers`. Zero strides normalize before division, and positive extents prevent zero-divisor cases.

These are proposed caller snippets, not compiled evidence. The caller owns allocation and synchronization choices. `T.allocate` has the existing `tests/transfers.bend::allocate` behavior. It selects memory using the returned requirements' memory-type bits and requested flags. `readback` is a bound transfer-destination buffer of at least 128 bytes. `readback_memory` and `readback_binding_offset` identify its allocation and binding offset. # Laziness Protocol

Aim for the most result with the least code and complexity.

- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.
- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.
- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.
- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat "elegant" boilerplate.
- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.
- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.

**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.

# Show me your work

Keep one canonical log.

## The format

A single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.

Copy `references/decision-log-template.tsv` (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:

- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.
- **phase.** The phase or workstream.
- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.
- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.
- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.
- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.

An example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.

### Opening a PR

Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Delegated workers inherit it. Parallel workers on the same branch each get their own worktree with `t3_thread_launch` and a `workspaceStrategy`, one writer per worktree, or `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/<branch>` between them. Dirty branch with unrelated work: patch out, fresh worktree, apply. Snarled worktree: reset from main, redo minimally.

**Commits.** Commit liberally. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.

**PRs.** Run the **unslop** skill over the diff before commit. Run the **no-comments** skill before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with the **technical-writing** skill, then apply the **unslop** skill. Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.

**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `p3-stack` or `p3-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(p3-mode): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.

**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. | Recording/Outside + begin_render_pass | Validate and reserve first. Dispatch INLINE begin, then enter Recording/Inside with this framebuffer. |
| Recording/Inside + begin_render_pass | BV_LIFETIME. No dispatch or dependency changes. |
| Recording/Outside + end_render_pass | BV_LIFETIME. No dispatch. |
| Recording/Inside + end_render_pass | Dispatch end and enter Recording/Outside. Keep every recorded dependency. |
| Recording/Inside + command end | BV_LIFETIME. Caller may still end the pass and then end the command. |
| Recording/Outside + command end | SUCCESS enters Executable. Driver failure enters Invalid and keeps dependencies. No implicit synchronization. |
| Any nonactive state + successful reset | Vulkan reset, clear payload, free command dependencies, enter Initial. Recording/Inside is included. |
| Any nonactive state + failed reset | Enter Invalid, clear irrelevant recording payload, retain all dependencies. |
| Pending or Uncertain + reset/pool destroy | Reject using existing active-association logic. |
| Executable + submit | Existing SUCCESS/Pending, OOM/Executable, unexpected/Uncertain rules apply unchanged. |
| Pending + timeout/NOT_READY/ordinary observation error | Retain Pending and allocation protection. |
| Pending + fence SUCCESS or successful idle | Completed, retain dependencies, permit host access. |
| Uncertain + successful idle | Invalid, retain dependencies, permit teardown/reset. Do not claim image results or a final layout. |
| Observed device loss | Existing sticky Lost and Invalid transitions. Retain dependency lifetimes until reset or teardown. |

Successful reset of a command inside a pass discards recording; it does not synthesize `end_render_pass`. Poo

The designs offer a clear choice. Layout tracking adds consistency checks and its own state machine. Direct dependency edges protect lifetimes without making the wrapper own layout history. My current preference is direct edges with caller-owned layouts, subject to the independent judge’s review.

# Laziness Protocol

Aim for the most result with the least code and complexity.

- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.
- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.
- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.
- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat "elegant" boilerplate.
- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.
- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.

**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.

# Show me your work

Keep one canonical log.

## The format

A single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.

Copy `references/decision-log-template.tsv` (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:

- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.
- **phase.** The phase or workstream.
- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.
- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.
- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.
- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.

### Opening a PR

Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Delegated workers inherit it. Parallel workers on the same branch each get their own worktree with `t3_thread_launch` and a `workspaceStrategy`, one writer per worktree, or `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/<branch>` between them. Dirty branch with unrelated work: patch out, fresh worktree, apply. Snarled worktree: reset from main, redo minimally.

**Commits.** Commit liberally. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.

**PRs.** Run the **unslop** skill over the diff before commit. Run the **no-comments** skill before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with the **technical-writing** skill, then apply the **unslop** skill. Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.

**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `p3-stack` or `p3-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(p3-mode): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.

The context window is finite and non-renewable within a session. Every token should be worth its cost.

# Guard the Context Window

The context window is finite and non-renewable within a session. Every token should be worth its cost.

**Why:** Context overflow degrades reasoning quality, creates compression artifacts, and halts progress.

**Pattern:**
- **Isolate large payloads.** Route verbose outputs, screenshots, and large documents to `delegate_task` workers. The main context gets summaries, not raw data.
- **Keep frequently used content inline.** Templates and references used on every invocation belong in the skill file, not in separate files that cost a read each time.
- **Size phases and cap scope.** Limit files per phase, set turn budgets, account for mechanism costs.

name: technical-writing
description: "Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages."

# Technical writing

The goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.

Three rules sit above the layers:

- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.

The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.

Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.

## Vary the rhythm

The layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.

- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".

## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)

One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?

- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
- Action + work: **how-to**.
- Understanding + work: **reference**.
- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.

Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.

**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as "we", in commands: "First, do x. Now, do y."

**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: "If you want x, do y." Name the guide by the task: "How to calibrate the radar array", not "Radar array calibration".

**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.

**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.

Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.

## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)

- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete." The reader skips what does not apply.
- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.
- Don't pre-announce ("we will soon support...") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.
- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never "click here". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.
- Headings carry the point, not just the topic ("Pick the mode first", not "Modes"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase ("Create an instance"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.
- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.
- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop "etc." and say up front that a list is partial.

## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)

- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.
- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.
- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: "If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur."
- Keep "the" and "a": "Remove backup file" reads two ways. "Remove the backup file" reads one.
- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If "check" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.
- Pick one word per action and stick to it: "start", not "start" here and "initiate" there.
- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: "Install the component", not "the component must be installed".
- Avoid "-ing" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.

## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)

- Keep words like "only" and "not" next to the word they change: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth" say different things.
- Break up long noun strings: "the proto import budget check script" becomes "the script that checks the proto-import budget".
- Make every "it", "they", and "this" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use "this" or "which" to point at a whole clause.
- Don't drop verbs: "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.
- Keep the small words that show structure. "Ensure that the switch is off" keeps "that" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.
- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: "the client and the host", not "the client and host", when they are two things.
- Say which parts "and" or "or" joins when a sentence can group two ways. "Both...and", "either...or", and "if...then" are free disambiguators.

- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with "(s)".

- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.
- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.

## Worked example

Before:

> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.

After:

> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.

name: technical-writing
description: "Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages."
disable-model-invocation: true

# Technical writing

The goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.

Three rules sit above the layers:

- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.

The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.

Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.

## Vary the rhythm

The layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.

- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".

## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)

One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?

- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
- Action + work: **how-to**.
- Understanding + work: **reference**.
- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.

Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.

**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as "we", in commands: "First, do x. Now, do y."

**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: "If you want x, do y." Name the guide by the task: "How to calibrate the radar array", not "Radar array calibration".

**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.

**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.

Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.

## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)

- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete." The reader skips what does not apply.
- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.
- Don't pre-announce ("we will soon support...") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.
- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never "click here". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.
- Headings carry the point, not just the topic ("Pick the mode first", not "Modes"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase ("Create an instance"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.
- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.
- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop "etc." and say up front that a list is partial.

## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)

- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.
- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.
- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: "If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur."
- Keep "the" and "a": "Remove backup file" reads two ways. "Remove the backup file" reads one.
- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If "check" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.
- Pick one word per action and stick to it: "start", not "start" here and "initiate" there.
- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: "Install the component", not "the component must be installed".
- Avoid "-ing" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.

## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)

- Keep words like "only" and "not" next to the word they change: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth" say different things.
- Break up long noun strings: "the proto import budget check script" becomes "the script that checks the proto-import budget".
- Make every "it", "they", and "this" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use "this" or "which" to point at a whole clause.
- Don't drop verbs: "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.
- Keep the small words that show structure. "Ensure that the switch is off" keeps "that" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.
- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: "the client and the host", not "the client and host", when they are two things.
- Say which parts "and" or "or" joins when a sentence can group two ways. "Both...and", "either...or", and "if...then" are free disambiguators.
- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.
- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with "(s)".
- No slashes: write "a, b, or both" instead of "a/b" or "and/or".

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run controlled dispatch and allocation probes in an emitted test translation unit."""
import argparse
import os
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def build(sanitize=False):
    source = ROOT / "build/transfers-probes.c"
    binary = source.with_suffix("")
    source.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(["bend", "tests/probe_main.bend", "-o", str(source)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    emitted = source.read_text()
    probes = (ROOT / "tests/probes.c").read_text().replace(
        "/* LIFECYCLE PROBES */", (ROOT / "tests/lifecycle_probes.c").read_text())
    probes = probes.replace("/* CAPABILITY PROBES */", (ROOT / "tests/capability_probes.c").read_text())
    probes += "\n" + (ROOT / "tests/image_probes.c").read_text()
    probes += "\n" + (ROOT / "tests/image_transfer_probes.c").read_text()
    probes += "\n" + (ROOT / "tests/render_probes.c").read_text()
    macros = re.findall(r"^#define (CID_\w+) \d+$", emitted, re.M)

    def cid(match):
        name = match[1].replace(".", "_").upper()
        matches = [m for m in macros if m == "CID_" + name or m.endswith("_VULKAN_" + name)]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing or ambiguous emitted constructor {name}: {matches}")
        return matches[0]

    probes = re.sub(r"CID\(([^)]+)\)", cid, probes)
    split = probes.index("static unsigned bv_test_barrier_calls;")
    allocator, checks = probes[:split], probes[split:]
    anchor = "static BvRow* bv_add("
    if emitted.count(anchor) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Native reference allocator moved")
    emitted = emitted.replace(anchor, allocator + "\n" + anchor)
    begin = emitted.index("// Bend 2.0.37 effect ABI.")
    end = emitted.index("static void __attribute__((constructor)) bv_register(void)", begin)
    native = emitted[begin:end]
    # Keep the emitted-test allocator itself outside the substitution.
    native = native.replace(allocator + "\n", "")
    native = native.replace("malloc(", "bv_test_alloc(").replace("calloc(", "bv_test_calloc(").replace("realloc(", "bv_test_realloc(")
    native = re.sub(r"\bfree\(", "bv_test_free(", native)
    native = native.replace(anchor, allocator + "\n" + anchor)
    emitted = emitted[:begin] + native + emitted[end:]
    emitted = emitted.replace("static void __attribute__((constructor)) bv_register(void)", checks + "\nstatic void __attribute__((constructor)) bv_register(void)")
    emitted, registrations = re.subn(r"(io_eff\(CID_\w+, )bv_cmd_copy_buffer(\);)", r"\1bv_test_copy_buffer\2", emitted)
    if registrations != 1:
        raise ValueError("Copy probe registration moved")
    emitted, images = re.subn(r"(io_eff\(CID_\w+, )bv_destroy_image_view(\);)", r"\1test_destroy_image_view\2", emitted)
    if images != 1:
        raise ValueError("Image resource probe registration moved")
    emitted, transfers = re.subn(r"(io_eff\(CID_\w+, )bv_cmd_clear_color_image(\);)", r"\1test_clear_color_image\2", emitted)
    if transfers != 1:
        raise ValueError("Image transfer probe registration moved")
    emitted, rendering = re.subn(r"(io_eff\(CID_\w+, )bv_cmd_begin_render_pass(\);)", r"\1test_begin_render_pass\2", emitted)
    if rendering != 1:
        raise ValueError("Render pass probe registration moved")
    emitted, live = re.subn(r"(io_eff\(CID_\w+, )bv_live_objects(\);)", r"\1test_live_objects\2", emitted)
    if live != 1:
        raise ValueError("Registry cleanup probe registration moved")
    source.write_text(emitted)
    flags = ["-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer"] if sanitize else []
    subprocess.run(["clang", "-std=c11", "-O1", "-g", *flags, str(source),
                    "-lpthread", "-lm", "-ldl", "-o", str(binary)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    env = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0", UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1")
    completed = subprocess.run([str(binary)], cwd=ROOT, env=env, check=False, timeout=60,
                               text=True, capture_output=True)
    print(completed.stdout, end="", flush=True)
    if completed.stderr:
        print(completed.stderr, end="", file=sys.stderr)
    completed.check_returncode()
    for marker in ("Injected metadata/map/flush", "Injected layer/extension dispatch",
                   "Injected submit OOM/uncertainty", "Controlled image query/create/bind/view rollback",
                   "Controlled image command F32",
                   "Controlled pass/framebuffer allocation rollback",
                   "Controlled image graph idle-error retry",
                   "Real disjoint buffer/optimal-image suballocation",
                   "Controlled native probes and real GPU integration passed"):
        if marker not in completed.stdout:
            raise SystemExit(f"Missing executed probe group: {marker}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--sanitize", action="store_true")
    build(parser.parse_args().sanitize)

import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo
import ./images.bend as Images
import ./offscreen.bend as O

def color_check(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, stage: O.Staging, pair: V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory, expected: List<&2,U32>) -> V.Action(Unit):
  O.Staging{+buffer,+readback,+offset} = stage
  (+image,+memory) = pair
  +range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1}
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    O.transition(command,image,range,0,7,1,4096,0,4096)
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command,image,7,V.ClearColor{1.0,0.0,0.0,1.0},[range])
    O.transition(command,image,range,7,6,4096,4096,4096,2048)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    O.host_barrier(command)
    O.complete(device,command,fence)
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,readback,offset,64)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,O.pixels(16n,expected)),"Raw RGBA/BGRA and sRGB endpoint channel order")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    V.Device.write_memory(device,readback,offset,O.pixels(16n,[17,31,63,127]))
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,16384,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{16384,2048}],[],[])
    O.transition(command,image,range,6,7,4096,4096,2048,4096)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command,buffer,image,7,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{2048,4096}],[],[])
    V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command,buffer,W.zero(),W.of_u32(64),3452816845)
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{4096,4096}],[],[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,7,6,4096,2048}])
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    O.host_barrier(command)
    O.complete(device,command,fence)
    encoded : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,readback,offset,64)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(encoded,O.pixels(16n,[17,31,63,127])),"Every raw channel and encoded sRGB byte survives copies")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    return Unit{}

def color(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, command: V.CommandBuffer, fence: V.Fence, stage: O.Staging, format: U32, expected: List<&2,U32>) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    pair : V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory <- Images.image(instance,physical,device,V.ImageCreateInfo{format,V.Extent2D{4,4},1,1,3},0)
    color_check(device,command,fence,stage,pair,expected)

def depth16(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, stage: O.Staging, pair: V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  O.Staging{+buffer,+readback,+offset} = stage
  (+image,+memory) = pair
  +range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1}
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    O.transition(command,image,range,0,7,1,4096,0,4096)
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command,image,7,1.0,[range])
    O.transition(command,image,range,7,6,4096,4096,4096,2048)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{2,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    O.host_barrier(command)
    O.complete(device,command,fence)
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,readback,offset,32)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,O.pixels(16n,[255,255])),"D16 depth 1.0 exact ff ff bytes")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    V.Device.write_memory(device,readback,offset,O.pixels(16n,[0,0]))
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,16384,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{16384,2048}],[],[])
    O.transition(command,image,range,6,7,4096,4096,2048,4096)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command,buffer,image,7,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{2,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{2048,4096}],[],[])
    V.CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command,buffer,W.zero(),W.of_u32(32),3452816845)
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{4096,4096}],[],[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,7,6,4096,2048}])
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{2,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    O.host_barrier(command)
    O.complete(device,command,fence)
    uploaded : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,readback,offset,32)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(uploaded,O.pixels(16n,[0,0])),"Every D16 depth 0.0 upload/readback byte")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    return Unit{}

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    +stage : O.Staging <- O.staging(instance,physical,device)
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    color(instance,physical,device,command,fence,stage,37,[255,0,0,255])
    color(instance,physical,device,command,fence,stage,43,[255,0,0,255])
    color(instance,physical,device,command,fence,stage,44,[0,0,255,255])
    color(instance,physical,device,command,fence,stage,50,[0,0,255,255])
    depth : V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory <- Images.image(instance,physical,device,V.ImageCreateInfo{124,V.Extent2D{4,4},1,1,3},0)
    depth16(device,command,fence,stage,depth)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    checked : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Format readback cleanup leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,checked)
    IO.print("RGBA/BGRA UNORM/SRGB raw channels and encoded bytes 17 31 63 127 passed; D16 depth 1.0 = ff ff and depth 0.0 upload = 00 00 passed")
import Base
import ../Vulkan.bend as V
import ../src/core.bend as Core
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo
import ./offscreen.bend as O
import ./rendering.bend as R

def cycles(remaining: Nat, +index: U32, +device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, +framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, +stage: O.Staging, +baseline: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match remaining:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      O.Staging{+buffer,+memory,+offset} = stage
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
        O.transition(command,color,V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1},0,2,1,1024,0,256)
        O.transition(command,depth,V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1},0,3,1,768,0,1024)
        V.CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command,framebuffer,V.RenderArea{V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{8,4}},
          [V.ColorClear{V.ClearColor{F32.div(U32.to_f32(index),255.0),F32.div(U32.to_f32(U32.sub(255,index)),255.0),F32.div(17.0,255.0),1.0}},V.DepthClear{0.5}])
        V.CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)
        O.transition(command,color,V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1},2,6,1024,4096,256,2048)
        O.transition(command,depth,V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1},3,6,768,4096,1024,2048)
        R.read_images(command,color,depth,buffer)
        O.complete(device,command,fence)
        colors : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,offset,128)
        depths : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,W.add(offset,W.of_u32(128)),128)
        Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(colors,O.pixels(32n,[index,U32.sub(255,index),17,255])),"Changing attachment color cycle")
        Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(depths,O.pixels(32n,[0,0,0,63])),"Reused depth attachment cycle")
        V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
        V.Fence.reset(fence)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,baseline),"Image reuse grew live registry rows")
        cycles(rest,U32.inc(index),device,command,fence,framebuffer,color,depth,stage,baseline)

def destroy(+device: V.Device, framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, pass: V.RenderPass, color: R.Attachment, depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{+image,+memory,view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{+depth_image,+depth_memory,depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.Device.destroy_framebuffer(device,framebuffer)
    V.Device.destroy_image_view(device,view)
    V.Device.destroy_image_view(device,depth_view)
    V.Device.destroy_render_pass(device,pass)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,depth_image)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,depth_memory)
    return Unit{}

def churn_resources(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +color: R.Attachment, +depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{image,memory,+view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{depth_image,depth_memory,+depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[V.AttachmentInfo{37,1,0}],Some{V.AttachmentInfo{126,1,0}}})
    framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
    destroy(device,framebuffer,pass,color,depth)

def churn(remaining: Nat, +instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +baseline: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match remaining:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        color : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)
        depth : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,126,2,35)
        churn_resources(instance,physical,device,color,depth)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,baseline),"Image/view/pass/framebuffer churn leaked rows")
        churn(rest,instance,physical,device,baseline)

def reused(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +color: R.Attachment, +depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{+image,memory,+view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{+depth_image,depth_memory,+depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[V.AttachmentInfo{37,1,0}],Some{V.AttachmentInfo{126,1,0}}})
    +framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
    +stage : O.Staging <- O.staging(instance,physical,device)
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    baseline : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    cycles(32n,1,device,command,fence,framebuffer,image,depth_image,stage,baseline)
    destroy(device,framebuffer,pass,color,depth)
    churn_baseline : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    churn(32n,instance,physical,device,churn_baseline)

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    color : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)
    depth : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,126,2,35)
    reused(instance,physical,device,color,depth)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    checked : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Repeated image cleanup leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,checked)
    IO.print("32 distinct color+D32 pass/readback cycles and 32 image/view/pass/framebuffer churn cycles passed with bounded rows")

    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{2,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):

import Base
import ../Vulkan.bend as V
import ../src/core.bend as Core
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo
import ./offscreen.bend as O
import ./rendering.bend as R

def cycles(remaining: Nat, +index: U32, +device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, +framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, +stage: O.Staging, +baseline: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match remaining:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      O.Staging{+buffer,+memory,+offset} = stage
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
        O.transition(command,color,V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1},0,2,1,1024,0,256)
        O.transition(command,depth,V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1},0,3,1,768,0,1024)
        V.CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command,framebuffer,V.RenderArea{V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{8,4}},
          [V.ColorClear{V.ClearColor{F32.div(U32.to_f32(index),255.0),F32.div(U32.to_f32(U32.sub(255,index)),255.0),F32.div(17.0,255.0),1.0}},V.DepthClear{0.5}])
        V.CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)
        O.transition(command,color,V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1},2,6,1024,4096,256,2048)
        O.transition(command,depth,V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1},3,6,768,4096,1024,2048)
        R.read_images(command,color,depth,buffer)
        O.complete(device,command,fence)
        colors : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,offset,128)
        depths : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,W.add(offset,W.of_u32(128)),128)
        Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(colors,O.pixels(32n,[index,U32.sub(255,index),17,255])),"Changing attachment color cycle")
        Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(depths,O.pixels(32n,[0,0,0,63])),"Reused depth attachment cycle")
        V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
        V.Fence.reset(fence)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,baseline),"Image reuse grew live registry rows")
        cycles(rest,U32.inc(index),device,command,fence,framebuffer,color,depth,stage,baseline)

def destroy(+device: V.Device, framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, pass: V.RenderPass, color: R.Attachment, depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{+image,+memory,view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{+depth_image,+depth_memory,depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.Device.destroy_framebuffer(device,framebuffer)
    V.Device.destroy_image_view(device,view)
    V.Device.destroy_image_view(device,depth_view)
    V.Device.destroy_render_pass(device,pass)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,depth_image)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,depth_memory)
    return Unit{}

def churn_resources(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +color: R.Attachment, +depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{image,memory,+view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{depth_image,depth_memory,+depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[V.AttachmentInfo{37,1,0}],Some{V.AttachmentInfo{126,1,0}}})
    framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
    destroy(device,framebuffer,pass,color,depth)

def churn(remaining: Nat, +instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +baseline: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match remaining:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        color : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)
        depth : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,126,2,35)
        churn_resources(instance,physical,device,color,depth)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,baseline),"Image/view/pass/framebuffer churn leaked rows")
        churn(rest,instance,physical,device,baseline)

def reused(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +color: R.Attachment, +depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{+image,memory,+view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{+depth_image,depth_memory,+depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[V.AttachmentInfo{37,1,0}],Some{V.AttachmentInfo{126,1,0}}})
    +framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
    +stage : O.Staging <- O.staging(instance,physical,device)
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    baseline : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    cycles(32n,1,device,command,fence,framebuffer,image,depth_image,stage,baseline)
    destroy(device,framebuffer,pass,color,depth)
    churn_baseline : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    churn(32n,instance,physical,device,churn_baseline)

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    color : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)
    depth : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,126,2,35)
    reused(instance,physical,device,color,depth)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    checked : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Repeated image cleanup leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,checked)
    IO.print("32 distinct color+D32 pass/readback cycles and 32 image/view/pass/framebuffer churn cycles passed with bounded rows")

import Base
import ../Vulkan.bend as V
import ../src/core.bend as Core
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo
import ./offscreen.bend as O
import ./rendering.bend as R

def cycles(remaining: Nat, +index: U32, +device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, +framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, +stage: O.Staging, +baseline: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match remaining:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      O.Staging{+buffer,+memory,+offset} = stage
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
        O.transition(command,color,V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1},0,2,1,1024,0,256)
        O.transition(command,depth,V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1},0,3,1,768,0,1024)
        V.CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command,framebuffer,V.RenderArea{V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{8,4}},
          [V.ColorClear{V.ClearColor{F32.div(U32.to_f32(index),255.0),F32.div(U32.to_f32(U32.sub(255,index)),255.0),F32.div(17.0,255.0),1.0}},V.DepthClear{0.5}])
        V.CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)
        O.transition(command,color,V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1},2,6,1024,4096,256,2048)
        O.transition(command,depth,V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1},3,6,768,4096,1024,2048)
        R.read_images(command,color,depth,buffer)
        O.complete(device,command,fence)
        colors : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,offset,128)
        depths : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,W.add(offset,W.of_u32(128)),128)
        Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(colors,O.pixels(32n,[index,U32.sub(255,index),17,255])),"Changing attachment color cycle")
        Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(depths,O.pixels(32n,[0,0,0,63])),"Reused depth attachment cycle")
        V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
        V.Fence.reset(fence)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,baseline),"Image reuse grew live registry rows")
        cycles(rest,U32.inc(index),device,command,fence,framebuffer,color,depth,stage,baseline)

def destroy(+device: V.Device, framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, pass: V.RenderPass, color: R.Attachment, depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{+image,+memory,view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{+depth_image,+depth_memory,depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.Device.destroy_framebuffer(device,framebuffer)
    V.Device.destroy_image_view(device,view)
    V.Device.destroy_image_view(device,depth_view)
    V.Device.destroy_render_pass(device,pass)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,depth_image)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,depth_memory)
    return Unit{}

def churn_resources(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +color: R.Attachment, +depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{image,memory,+view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{depth_image,depth_memory,+depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[V.AttachmentInfo{37,1,0}],Some{V.AttachmentInfo{126,1,0}}})
    framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
    destroy(device,framebuffer,pass,color,depth)

def churn(remaining: Nat, +instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +baseline: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  match remaining:
    case 0n:
      V.Action.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      do V.Action<Unit>:
        color : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)
        depth : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,126,2,35)
        churn_resources(instance,physical,device,color,depth)
        live : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
        Demo.require(U32.is_eq(live,baseline),"Image/view/pass/framebuffer churn leaked rows")
        churn(rest,instance,physical,device,baseline)

def reused(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +color: R.Attachment, +depth: R.Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  R.Attachment{+image,memory,+view,visible} = color
  R.Attachment{+depth_image,depth_memory,+depth_view,depth_visible} = depth
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pass : V.RenderPass <- V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[V.AttachmentInfo{37,1,0}],Some{V.AttachmentInfo{126,1,0}}})
    +framebuffer : V.Framebuffer <- V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{pass,[view,depth_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}})
    +stage : O.Staging <- O.staging(instance,physical,device)
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    baseline : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    cycles(32n,1,device,command,fence,framebuffer,image,depth_image,stage,baseline)
    destroy(device,framebuffer,pass,color,depth)
    churn_baseline : U32 <- V.debug_live_objects()
    churn(32n,instance,physical,device,churn_baseline)

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    color : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)
    depth : R.Attachment <- R.attachment(instance,physical,device,126,2,35)
    reused(instance,physical,device,color,depth)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    checked : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Repeated image cleanup leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,checked)
    IO.print("32 distinct color+D32 pass/readback cycles and 32 image/view/pass/framebuffer churn cycles passed with bounded rows")
