import Base
import ../Vulkan.bend as V
import ../src/core.bend as Core
import ../src/constants.bend as vk
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ../examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo
import ./native.bend as T
import ./images.bend as Images

type Staging is Data:
  Staging{buffer: V.Buffer, memory: V.DeviceMemory, offset: W.U64}

def staging_bound(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +buffer: V.Buffer, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(Staging):
  V.MemoryRequirements{+size,+alignment,bits} = requirements
  do V.Action<Staging>:
    types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance,physical)
    index : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_memory_type(types,bits,2),"No host-visible staging allocation")
    +memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device,W.add(size,alignment),index)
    V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device,buffer,memory,alignment)
    return Staging{buffer,memory,alignment}

def staging(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device) -> V.Action(Staging):
  do V.Action<Staging>:
    +buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device,V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(2048),3})
    requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device,buffer)
    staging_bound(instance,physical,device,buffer,requirements)

def complete(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
    V.Device.submit(device,command,fence)
    status : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence,Core.whole_size())
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(status,0),"Offscreen fence did not complete")

def copy_bytes(bytes: List<&2,U32>) -> List<U32>:
  match bytes:
    case Nil{}:
      []
    case Con{byte,rest}:
      byte <> copy_bytes(rest)

def repeated(count: Nat, +byte: U32) -> List<U32>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      []
    case 1n+rest:
      byte <> repeated(rest,byte)

def pixels(count: Nat, +pixel: List<&2,U32>) -> List<U32>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      []
    case 1n+rest:
      List.append(&1,U32,copy_bytes(pixel),pixels(rest,pixel))

def host_barrier(command: V.CommandBuffer) -> V.Action(Unit):
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,16384,[V.MemoryBarrier{4096,8192}],[],[])

def transition(command: V.CommandBuffer, image: V.ImageHandle, range: V.ImageSubresourceRange, old: U32, new: U32, src_stage: U32, dst_stage: U32, src: U32, dst: U32) -> V.Action(Unit):
  V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,src_stage,dst_stage,[],[],[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,old,new,src,dst}])

def clear_readback(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, +target: V.ImageHandle, staging: Staging) -> V.Action(Unit):
  Staging{+buffer,+memory,+offset} = staging
  +range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,2,0,2}
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    transition(command,target,range,0,7,1,4096,0,4096)
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612739,V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command,target,7,V.ClearColor{1.0,0.0,1.0,1.0},[]))
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command,target,7,V.ClearColor{1.0,0.0,1.0,1.0},[range])
    transition(command,target,range,7,6,4096,4096,4096,2048)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,target,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,1,0,2},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{5,3}}])
    host_barrier(command)
    complete(device,command,fence)
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,offset,120)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,pixels(30n,[255,0,255,255])),"Every-pixel F32 magenta clear")
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612740,V.Device.destroy_image(device,target))
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    return Unit{}

def padded_expected() -> List<U32>:
  List.concat(&1,U32,[repeated(20n,205),
    [11,12,13,255,21,22,23,255,31,32,33,255],repeated(24n,205),
    [41,42,43,255,51,52,53,255,61,62,63,255],repeated(168n,205),
    [71,72,73,255,81,82,83,255,91,92,93,255],repeated(24n,205),
    [101,102,103,255,111,112,113,255,121,122,123,255]])

def full_expected() -> List<U32>:
  [0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,
   0,0,0,255,11,12,13,255,21,22,23,255,31,32,33,255,0,0,0,255,
   0,0,0,255,41,42,43,255,51,52,53,255,61,62,63,255,0,0,0,255,
   0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255,
   0,0,0,255,71,72,73,255,81,82,83,255,91,92,93,255,0,0,0,255,
   0,0,0,255,101,102,103,255,111,112,113,255,121,122,123,255,0,0,0,255]

def complete_expected() -> List<U32>:
  List.concat(&1,U32,[padded_expected(),repeated(228n,205),full_expected(),repeated(392n,205),pixels(120n,[0,0,0,255]),repeated(544n,205)])

def padded_roundtrip(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, +target: V.ImageHandle, source: Staging, destination: Staging) -> V.Action(Unit):
  Staging{+src,+source_memory,+source_offset} = source
  Staging{+dst,+dest_memory,+dest_offset} = destination
  +range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,2,0,2}
  +patch : V.BufferImageCopy = V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(12),7,5,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,1,0,2},V.Offset2D{1,1},V.Extent2D{3,2}}
  upload_bytes output_bytes = repeated(2048n,171) repeated(2048n,205)
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.Device.write_memory(device,source_memory,source_offset,upload_bytes)
    V.Device.write_memory(device,dest_memory,dest_offset,output_bytes)
    V.Device.write_memory(device,source_memory,W.add(source_offset,W.of_u32(12)),[11,12,13,255,21,22,23,255,31,32,33,255])
    V.Device.write_memory(device,source_memory,W.add(source_offset,W.of_u32(40)),[41,42,43,255,51,52,53,255,61,62,63,255])
    V.Device.write_memory(device,source_memory,W.add(source_offset,W.of_u32(152)),[71,72,73,255,81,82,83,255,91,92,93,255])
    V.Device.write_memory(device,source_memory,W.add(source_offset,W.of_u32(180)),[101,102,103,255,111,112,113,255,121,122,123,255])
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,16384,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{16384,6144}],[],[])
    transition(command,target,range,6,7,4096,4096,2048,4096)
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command,target,7,V.ClearColor{0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0},[range])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,4096,[V.MemoryBarrier{4096,4096}],[],[])
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612739,V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command,src,target,7,[patch,patch]))
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612739,V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command,src,target,7,[V.BufferImageCopy{Core.whole_size(),7,5,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,1,0,2},V.Offset2D{1,1},V.Extent2D{3,2}}]))
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command,src,target,7,[patch])
    transition(command,target,range,7,6,4096,4096,4096,2048)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,target,6,dst,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(20),9,6,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,1,0,2},V.Offset2D{1,1},V.Extent2D{3,2}},
      V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(512),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,1,0,2},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{5,3}},
      V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(1024),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,0,0,2},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{10,6}}])
    host_barrier(command)
    complete(device,command,fence)
    padded : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,dest_memory,dest_offset,284)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(padded,padded_expected()),"Padded nonzero-offset two-layer payload and sentinels")
    full : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,dest_memory,W.add(dest_offset,W.of_u32(512)),120)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(full,full_expected()),"Nonzero mip addressing, orientation and untouched texels")
    base : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,dest_memory,W.add(dest_offset,W.of_u32(1024)),480)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(base,pixels(120n,[0,0,0,255])),"Upload changed untouched base mip")
    all_bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,dest_memory,dest_offset,2048)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(all_bytes,complete_expected()),"Complete staging buffer payload, padding, gaps and trailing sentinels")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    return Unit{}

def transfer(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, pair: V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  (+target,+memory) = pair
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +source : Staging <- staging(instance,physical,device)
    +destination : Staging <- staging(instance,physical,device)
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    clear_readback(device,command,fence,target,destination)
    padded_roundtrip(device,command,fence,target,source,destination)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,target)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    return Unit{}

def depth_staged(+device: V.Device, +target: V.ImageHandle, stage: Staging) -> V.Action(Unit):
  Staging{+buffer,+memory,+offset} = stage
  +range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1}
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    transition(command,target,range,0,7,1,4096,0,4096)
    T.expect_error(Unit,1610612739,V.CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command,target,7,1.5,[range]))
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command,target,7,0.5,[range])
    transition(command,target,range,7,6,4096,4096,4096,2048)
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,target,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{2,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{8,4}}])
    host_barrier(command)
    complete(device,command,fence)
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,offset,128)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,pixels(32n,[0,0,0,63])),"D32 depth 0.5 exact bytes")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    return Unit{}

def depth_readback(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, pair: V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory) -> V.Action(Unit):
  (+target,+memory) = pair
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +stage : Staging <- staging(instance,physical,device)
    depth_staged(device,target,stage)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,target)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,memory)
    return Unit{}

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    pair : V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory <- Images.image(instance,physical,device,V.ImageCreateInfo{37,V.Extent2D{10,6},2,2,3},0)
    transfer(instance,physical,device,pair)
    depth : V.ImageHandle & V.DeviceMemory <- Images.image(instance,physical,device,V.ImageCreateInfo{126,V.Extent2D{8,4},1,1,35},0)
    depth_readback(instance,physical,device,depth)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    checked : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Offscreen transfer cleanup leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,checked)
    IO.print("Every-pixel clear and padded two-layer nonzero-mip offscreen transfers passed; D32 depth 0.5 = 00 00 00 3f")

type Attachment is Data:
  Attachment{image: V.ImageHandle, memory: V.DeviceMemory, view: V.ImageView, host_visible: Bool}

def preferred_memory(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, preferred: Maybe<U32>, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(V.DeviceMemory & Bool):
  match preferred:
    case Some{index}:
      V.MemoryRequirements{size,alignment,bits} = requirements
      do V.Action<V.DeviceMemory & Bool>:
        memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device,size,index)
        return (memory,True{})
    case None{}:
      do V.Action<V.DeviceMemory & Bool>:
        memory : V.DeviceMemory <- Example.allocate(instance,physical,device,requirements,0)
        return (memory,False{})

def bound_attachment(+device: V.Device, +image: V.ImageHandle, aspect: U32, pair: V.DeviceMemory & Bool) -> V.Action(Attachment):
  (+memory,visible) = pair
  do V.Action<Attachment>:
    V.Device.bind_image_memory(device,image,memory,W.zero())
    view : V.ImageView <- V.Device.create_image_view(device,V.ImageViewCreateInfo{image,1,V.ImageSubresourceRange{aspect,0,1,0,1}})
    return Attachment{image,memory,view,visible}

def attachment_requirements(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +image: V.ImageHandle, aspect: U32, +requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(Attachment):
  V.MemoryRequirements{size,alignment,bits} = requirements
  do V.Action<Attachment>:
    types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance,physical)
    pair : V.DeviceMemory & Bool <- preferred_memory(instance,physical,device,Core.find_memory_type(types,bits,2),requirements)
    bound_attachment(device,image,aspect,pair)

def partial_expected(count: Nat, +index: U32, +depth: Bool) -> List<U32>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      []
    case 1n+rest:
      +x : U32 = U32.mod(index,8)
      +y : U32 = U32.div(index,8)
      inside : Bool = Bool.and(Bool.and(U32.is_ge(x,2),U32.is_lt(x,5)),Bool.and(U32.is_ge(y,1),U32.is_lt(y,3)))
      pixel : List<&2,U32> = Bool.pick(List<&2,U32>,inside,Bool.pick(List<&2,U32>,depth,[0,0,0,63],[0,255,0,255]),Bool.pick(List<&2,U32>,depth,[0,0,128,63],[255,0,0,255]))
      List.append(&1,U32,O.copy_bytes(pixel),partial_expected(rest,U32.inc(index),depth))

def read_images(+command: V.CommandBuffer, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, +buffer: V.Buffer) -> V.Action(Unit):

    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,depth,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.of_u32(128),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{2,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{8,4}}])

def copy_pass_clear(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, stage: O.Staging) -> V.Action(Unit):

    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(depths,O.pixels(32n,[0,0,0,63])),"Vulkan 1.0 render-pass D32 depth 0.5")

def partial_expected(count: Nat, +index: U32, +depth: Bool) -> List<U32>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      []
    case 1n+rest:
      +x : U32 = U32.mod(index,8)
      +y : U32 = U32.div(index,8)
      inside : Bool = Bool.and(Bool.and(U32.is_ge(x,2),U32.is_lt(x,5)),Bool.and(U32.is_ge(y,1),U32.is_lt(y,3)))
      pixel : List<&2,U32> = Bool.pick(List<&2,U32>,inside,Bool.pick(List<&2,U32>,depth,[0,0,0,63],[0,255,0,255]),Bool.pick(List<&2,U32>,depth,[0,0,128,63],[255,0,0,255]))

def partial_clear(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, framebuffer: V.Framebuffer, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, stage: O.Staging) -> V.Action(Unit):
  O.Staging{+buffer,+memory,+offset} = stage
  +color_range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1}
  +depth_range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{2,0,1,0,1}
  expected_color expected_depth = partial_expected(32n,0,False{}) partial_expected(32n,0,True{})
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    O.transition(command,color,color_range,6,7,4096,4096,2048,4096)
    O.transition(command,depth,depth_range,6,7,4096,4096,2048,4096)
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command,color,7,V.ClearColor{1.0,0.0,0.0,1.0},[color_range])
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command,depth,7,1.0,[depth_range])
    O.transition(command,color,color_range,7,2,4096,1024,4096,256)
    O.transition(command,depth,depth_range,7,3,4096,768,4096,1024)
    V.CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command,framebuffer,V.RenderArea{V.Offset2D{2,1},V.Extent2D{3,2}},[V.ColorClear{V.ClearColor{0.0,1.0,0.0,1.0}},V.DepthClear{0.5}])
    V.CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)
    O.transition(command,color,color_range,2,6,1024,4096,256,2048)
    O.transition(command,depth,depth_range,3,6,768,4096,1024,2048)
    read_images(command,color,depth,buffer)
    O.complete(device,command,fence)
    colors : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,offset,128)
    depths : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,memory,W.add(offset,W.of_u32(128)),128)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(colors,expected_color),"Partial render area color and outside preservation")
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(depths,expected_depth),"Partial render area depth and outside preservation")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Fence.reset(fence)
    return Unit{}

def load_preserve(+device: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, +fence: V.Fence, color: V.ImageHandle, depth: V.ImageHandle, color_view: V.ImageView, +depth_view: V.ImageView) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:

def foreign_image_commands(+other: V.Device, +command: V.CommandBuffer, pool: V.CommandPool, +color: V.ImageHandle, +depth: V.ImageHandle, stage: O.Staging) -> V.Action(Unit):

def render(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +other: V.Device, +color: Attachment, +depth: Attachment) -> V.Action(Unit):
  Attachment{+color_image,+color_memory,+color_view,+visible} = color

    T.expect_error(V.Framebuffer,1610612739,V.Device.create_framebuffer(device,V.FramebufferCreateInfo{two_colors,[color_view,color_view],V.Extent2D{8,4}}))
    V.Device.destroy_render_pass(device,two_colors)
    +stage : O.Staging <- O.staging(instance,physical,device)
    foreign_image_commands(other,other_command,other_pool,color_image,depth_image,stage)
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)

    V.Device.destroy_image(device,depth_image)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,color_memory)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,depth_memory)
    return Unit{}

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    +family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    T.expect_error(V.RenderPass,1610612739,V.Device.create_render_pass(device,V.RenderPassCreateInfo{[],None{}}))

    +color : Attachment <- attachment(instance,physical,device,37,1,19)

    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()

type Attachment is Data:
  Attachment{image: V.ImageHandle, memory: V.DeviceMemory, view: V.ImageView, host_visible: Bool}

def preferred_memory(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, preferred: Maybe<U32>, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(V.DeviceMemory & Bool):
  match preferred:
    case Some{index}:
      V.MemoryRequirements{size,alignment,bits} = requirements
      do V.Action<V.DeviceMemory & Bool>:
        memory : V.DeviceMemory <- V.Device.allocate_memory(device,size,index)
        return (memory,True{})
    case None{}:
      do V.Action<V.DeviceMemory & Bool>:
        memory : V.DeviceMemory <- Example.allocate(instance,physical,device,requirements,0)
        return (memory,False{})

def bound_attachment(+device: V.Device, +image: V.ImageHandle, aspect: U32, pair: V.DeviceMemory & Bool) -> V.Action(Attachment):
  (+memory,visible) = pair
  do V.Action<Attachment>:
    V.Device.bind_image_memory(device,image,memory,W.zero())
    view : V.ImageView <- V.Device.create_image_view(device,V.ImageViewCreateInfo{image,1,V.ImageSubresourceRange{aspect,0,1,0,1}})

def attachment_requirements(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device, +image: V.ImageHandle, aspect: U32, +requirements: V.MemoryRequirements) -> V.Action(Attachment):

+## Images and views
+
+| Operation | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Device.create_image(device, info)` | An unbound `ImageHandle` |
+| `Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device, image)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
+| `Device.bind_image_memory(device, image, memory, offset)` | An explicit requirements-checked binding |
+| `Device.create_image_view(device, info)` | An `ImageView` retaining its image |
+| `Device.destroy_image_view(device, view)` | View teardown, rejecting framebuffer dependents |
+| `Device.destroy_image(device, image)` | Image teardown, rejecting views and recorded references |
+
+`ImageHandle` avoids a name collision with Bend Base's `Image` type.
+`ImageCreateInfo{format, extent, mip_levels, array_layers, usage}` creates an exclusive 2D optimal-tiled image.
+Depth is one, samples are one, flags are zero, and initial layout is UNDEFINED.
+Extent and mip/layer counts must be positive and fit the exact configuration limits and full mip chain.
+Creation checks configuration support and required format features before native creation.
+The returned memory requirements determine allocation size. Logical texel bytes do not describe an optimal image's footprint or memory layout.
+
+The creation profile accepts these formats when the driver supports the requested configuration:
+
+| Format | Value | Aspect | Raw texel bytes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` | 37 | COLOR | R, G, B, A |
+| `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB` | 43 | COLOR | Encoded R, G, B, linear A |
+| `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM` | 44 | COLOR | B, G, R, A |
+| `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_SRGB` | 50 | COLOR | Encoded B, G, R, linear A |
+| `VK_FORMAT_D16_UNORM` | 124 | DEPTH | Two little-endian UNORM bytes |
+| `VK_FORMAT_D32_SFLOAT` | 126 | DEPTH | Four little-endian IEEE binary32 bytes |
+
+Usages are a nonempty subset of TRANSFER_SRC, TRANSFER_DST, SAMPLED, COLOR_ATTACHMENT, and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT.
+Color and depth attachment usages must match the format's role. Stencil, linear tiling, MSAA, compressed formats, sparse images, and format reinterpretation are absent.
+SAMPLED usage permits resource preparation. Descriptors, samplers, and shader sampling commands are absent.
+
+`ImageFormatInfo{format, image_type, tiling, usage, flags}` queries recognized core-1.0 configurations beyond the creation profile.
+Invalid enum values return the wrapper argument error. A driver rejection preserves exact `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` bits, `4294967285`.
+Failed query outputs are never decoded.
+`ImageFormatProperties` contains `max_width`, `max_height`, `max_depth`, `max_mip_levels`, `max_array_layers`, `sample_counts`, and `max_resource_size: W.U64`.
+Generic format masks alone do not establish support for a configuration.
+
+`ImageSubresourceRange{aspect_mask, base_mip_level, level_count, base_array_layer, layer_count}` requires explicit positive counts and the format's exact aspect.
+`ImageViewCreateInfo{image, view_type, range}` requires binding and at least one view-eligible usage, SAMPLED or an attachment usage.
+Views use the image's format and identity component mapping. A 2D view selects one layer. A 2D_ARRAY view may select multiple layers.
+
+Buffer and image bindings share requirements-sized bounds, alignment, type, and owner checks.
+Buffer-buffer aliasing remains available. Binding intervals must not overlap when either resource is an image.
+Mixed buffer/optimal-image intervals must also occupy disjoint `buffer_image_granularity` pages, in either bind order.
+Distinct images may share an allocation at disjoint requirements intervals. Allocation-wide host exclusion still applies.
+
+## Image commands and readback
+
+| Operation | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, layout, value, ranges)` | Float color clear over explicit ranges |
+| `CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command, image, layout, depth, ranges)` | Depth clear over explicit ranges |
+| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command, src, dst, layout, regions)` | Raw buffer upload |
+| `CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, src, layout, dst, regions)` | Raw staging readback |
+
+Image commands require bound, same-device resources and Recording Outside scope.
+Clears and uploads require TRANSFER_DST usage and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL or GENERAL layout.
+Readback requires TRANSFER_SRC usage and TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL or GENERAL layout.
+Color clear requires a graphics or compute queue. Depth clears and depth copies require graphics.
+Color copies accept graphics, compute, or transfer queues and enforce the selected family's actual `minImageTransferGranularity`.
+Zero granularity requires a whole mip. Nonzero granularity permits the Vulkan edge exception.
+Range and copy lists are nonempty and bounded to 4096. Overlapping clear ranges are rejected.
+
+`ClearColor{r, g, b, a}` takes finite F32 values. Vulkan converts them to the destination format, including sRGB encoding of RGB.
+Copies preserve stored bytes and perform no color conversion, swizzle, vertical flip, or alpha transformation.
+Depth clears require finite values in `[0,1]`. Uploaded depth values must also be in `[0,1]`, as a caller obligation.
+The wrapper does not inspect GPU buffer contents to validate uploaded depth values.
+
+`BufferImageCopy{buffer_offset, buffer_row_length, buffer_image_height, image_subresource, image_offset, image_extent}` uses a W.U64 byte offset into the buffer.
+The offset is relative to the buffer, independently of its memory binding offset.
+`buffer_row_length` and `buffer_image_height` are texel counts. Zero means the copied width or height.
+Positive values must cover those dimensions. `ImageSubresourceLayers{aspect_mask, mip_level, base_array_layer, layer_count}` selects one mip and positive layer count.
+Offsets are nonnegative and signed-representable. Extents must be positive, signed-representable, and fit the selected mip.
+Buffer offsets are four-byte aligned, including D16. Row byte lengths cannot exceed `INT32_MAX`.
+
+For normalized row length R, image height H, bytes per texel B, width w, height h, layers L, and buffer offset O:
+
+```text
+row_stride   = R * B
+layer_stride = H * row_stride
+end          = O + (L - 1) * layer_stride + (h - 1) * row_stride + w * B
+```
+
+All arithmetic is checked U64. The final row has no required trailing padding.
+The interval must fit the buffer's logical size and its bound allocation.
+Uploads reject overlapping destination image boxes. Downloads reject overlapping destination buffer envelopes, including their internal padding.
+Repeated source reads are allowed. Logical dimensions and strides determine the result, independently of Bend array capacity.
+Texels increase in x, then y, then layer order. The example defines the first row, `y=0`, as the top.
+This convention specifies exported bytes. Viewport conventions for future draws are outside this API.
+

Sizes, offsets, and alignments are `bend-collections` `W.U64` values.
`Core.whole_size()` returns Vulkan's all-ones `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` value.
`Core.find_memory_type(types, memory_type_bits, required_flags)` returns the first eligible index or `None`.
`Core.find_queue_family(families, required_flags)` skips empty queues and returns the first matching family.

A byte list contains U32 values from 0 through 255. Host reads and writes require host-visible memory.
Each host operation maps the whole allocation temporarily and copies a checked subrange.
`read_memory` takes a U32 byte count. Host reads and both upload paths are limited to 16 MiB per call.
Memory allocation sizes and copy offsets retain all 64 bits.
Packed uploads emit each word's low-order byte first and truncate the final partial word.
The explicit U64 byte length must fit the array capacity, allocation range, and 16 MiB chunk limit.
Zero bytes at an in-bounds offset is valid. Every outcome returns the unchanged array, including the interpreted backend's native-only error.
A flush failure can leave mapped destination bytes changed.
No Bend heap pointer survives the operation.

The wrapper checks common lifetime and memory-access errors. Callers remain responsible for Vulkan validity requirements for chosen flags, extensions, and resource use.
Handle keys are checked process-local identifiers. They provide no raw Vulkan handle interoperation or access-control guarantee.

## Images and views

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_image(device, info)` | An unbound `ImageHandle` |
| `Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device, image)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.bind_image_memory(device, image, memory, offset)` | An explicit requirements-checked binding |
| `Device.create_image_view(device, info)` | An `ImageView` retaining its image |
| `Device.destroy_image_view(device, view)` | View teardown, rejecting framebuffer dependents |
| `Device.destroy_image(device, image)` | Image teardown, rejecting views and recorded references |

`ImageHandle` avoids a name collision with Bend Base's `Image` type.
`ImageCreateInfo{format, extent, mip_levels, array_layers, usage}` creates an exclusive 2D optimal-tiled image.
Depth is one, samples are one, flags are zero, and initial layout is UNDEFINED.
Extent and mip/layer counts must be positive and fit the exact configuration limits and full mip chain.
Creation checks configuration support and required format features before native creation.
The returned memory requirements determine allocation size. Logical texel bytes do not describe an optimal image's footprint or memory layout.

The creation profile accepts these formats when the driver supports the requested configuration:

| Format | Value | Aspect | Raw texel bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` | 37 | COLOR | R, G, B, A |
| `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB` | 43 | COLOR | Encoded R, G, B, linear A |
| `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM` | 44 | COLOR | B, G, R, A |
| `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_SRGB` | 50 | COLOR | Encoded B, G, R, linear A |
| `VK_FORMAT_D16_UNORM` | 124 | DEPTH | Two little-endian UNORM bytes |
| `VK_FORMAT_D32_SFLOAT` | 126 | DEPTH | Four little-endian IEEE binary32 bytes |

Usages are a nonempty subset of TRANSFER_SRC, TRANSFER_DST, SAMPLED, COLOR_ATTACHMENT, and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT.
Color and depth attachment usages must match the format's role. Stencil, linear tiling, MSAA, compressed formats, sparse images, and format reinterpretation are absent.
SAMPLED usage permits resource preparation. Descriptors, samplers, and shader sampling commands are absent.

`ImageFormatInfo{format, image_type, tiling, usage, flags}` queries recognized core-1.0 configurations beyond the creation profile.
Invalid enum values return the wrapper argument error. A driver rejection preserves exact `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` bits, `4294967285`.
Failed query outputs are never decoded.
`ImageFormatProperties` contains `max_width`, `max_height`, `max_depth`, `max_mip_levels`, `max_array_layers`, `sample_counts`, and `max_resource_size: W.U64`.
Generic format masks alone do not establish support for a configuration.

`ImageSubresourceRange{aspect_mask, base_mip_level, level_count, base_array_layer, layer_count}` requires explicit positive counts and the format's exact aspect.
`ImageViewCreateInfo{image, view_type, range}` requires binding and at least one view-eligible usage, SAMPLED or an attachment usage.
Views use the image's format and identity component mapping. A 2D view selects one layer. A 2D_ARRAY view may select multiple layers.

Buffer and image bindings share requirements-sized bounds, alignment, type, and owner checks.
Buffer-buffer aliasing remains available. Binding intervals must not overlap when either resource is an image.
Mixed buffer/optimal-image intervals must also occupy disjoint `buffer_image_granularity` pages, in either bind order.
Distinct images may share an allocation at disjoint requirements intervals. Allocation-wide host exclusion still applies.

## Image commands and readback

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, layout, value, ranges)` | Float color clear over explicit ranges |
| `CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command, image, layout, depth, ranges)` | Depth clear over explicit ranges |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command, src, dst, layout, regions)` | Raw buffer upload |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, src, layout, dst, regions)` | Raw staging readback |

Image commands require bound, same-device resources and Recording Outside scope.
Clears and uploads require TRANSFER_DST usage and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL or GENERAL layout.
Readback requires TRANSFER_SRC usage and TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL or GENERAL layout.
Color clear requires a graphics or compute queue. Depth clears and depth copies require graphics.
Color copies accept graphics, compute, or transfer queues and enforce the selected family's actual `minImageTransferGranularity`.
Zero granularity requires a whole mip. Nonzero granularity permits the Vulkan edge exception.
Range and copy lists are nonempty and bounded to 4096. Overlapping clear ranges are rejected.

`ClearColor{r, g, b, a}` takes finite F32 values. Vulkan converts them to the destination format, including sRGB encoding of RGB.
Copies preserve stored bytes and perform no color conversion, swizzle, vertical flip, or alpha transformation.
Depth clears require finite values in `[0,1]`. Uploaded depth values must also be in `[0,1]`, as a caller obligation.
The wrapper does not inspect GPU buffer contents to validate uploaded depth values.

`BufferImageCopy{buffer_offset, buffer_row_length, buffer_image_height, image_subresource, image_offset, image_extent}` uses a W.U64 byte offset into the buffer.
The offset is relative to the buffer, independently of its memory binding offset.
`buffer_row_length` and `buffer_image_height` are texel counts. Zero means the copied width or height.
Positive values must cover those dimensions. `ImageSubresourceLayers{aspect_mask, mip_level, base_array_layer, layer_count}` selects one mip and positive layer count.
Offsets are nonnegative and signed-representable. Extents must be positive, signed-representable, and fit the selected mip.
Buffer offsets are four-byte aligned, including D16. Row byte lengths cannot exceed `INT32_MAX`.

For normalized row length R, image height H, bytes per texel B, width w, height h, layers L, and buffer offset O:

```text
row_stride   = R * B
layer_stride = H * row_stride
end          = O + (L - 1) * layer_stride + (h - 1) * row_stride + w * B
```

All arithmetic is checked U64. The final row has no required trailing padding.
The interval must fit the buffer's logical size and its bound allocation.
Uploads reject overlapping destination image boxes. Downloads reject overlapping destination buffer envelopes, including their internal padding.
Repeated source reads are allowed. Logical dimensions and strides determine the result, independently of Bend array capacity.
Texels increase in x, then y, then layer order. The example defines the first row, `y=0`, as the top.
This convention specifies exported bytes. Viewport conventions for future draws are outside this API.

Layouts and initialized contents are caller assertions at execution time.
The wrapper stores no layout cache and inserts no implicit image or host barriers.
Use `ImageMemoryBarrier{image, range, old_layout, new_layout, src_access, dst_access}` in the sole `pipeline_barrier` operation.
The wrapper checks usage, aspect, range, layout enum, and queue stage/access compatibility.
Both queue-family indices are IGNORED. Overlapping image ranges within one barrier call are rejected.
UNDEFINED is an old discard layout only and requires zero source access by wrapper policy.
After unexpected submission errors, observe idle recovery and deliberately overwrite, discard, or recreate before relying on contents.

## Render passes and framebuffers

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_render_pass(device, info)` | A Vulkan 1.0 single-subpass `RenderPass` |

`RenderPassCreateInfo{colors, depth}` contains ordered `AttachmentInfo{format, load_op, store_op}` values and an optional depth attachment.
At least one attachment is required. Color count is limited by `max_color_attachments` and the wrapper's 4095-color cap.
LOAD, CLEAR, DONT_CARE and STORE, DONT_CARE operations are supported.
Attachments are single-sample. Stencil operations are DONT_CARE. The queue must support graphics.
Initial, subpass, and final layouts are all COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL or DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL for the corresponding role.
There are no explicit subpass dependencies. Supply outside barriers for transfers and attachment reads/writes, including LOAD of a prior pass's output.

`FramebufferCreateInfo{render_pass, attachments, extent}` requires same-device, ordered, format-matching 2D views.
Each view selects exactly one mip and one layer, has the required attachment usage, and covers the framebuffer extent.
Attachment subresources cannot overlap. Begin derives the exact pass identity from the framebuffer.
`RenderArea{offset, extent}` has nonnegative offsets and positive extents, all signed-representable and within the framebuffer.

The clear list has one entry per attachment, including placeholders.
CLEAR slots require `ColorClear{ClearColor{...}}` or `DepthClear{depth}` according to role.
Other slots require `UnusedClear{}`. Float constraints match image clears.
Clears cover the render area. Preserved pixels outside that area require prior initialization and correct synchronization.
Nested begin, unmatched end, and command end Inside reject before dispatch.
All fills, copies, image clears, and barriers reject Inside. Successful reset may discard an open recording.
This milestone executes begin/end and attachment clears. Pipelines, shaders, and draws are absent.

## Command submission

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |
| `Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)` | One primary command buffer |
| `CommandBuffer.begin(command)` | Begin one-time recording |
| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, src, dst, regions)` | Record nonempty byte ranges from `List<BufferCopy>` |
| `CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, src_stage, dst_stage, memory, buffers, images)` | Record explicit memory, buffer and image barriers |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | End recording |
| `Device.create_fence(device, signaled)` | A caller-owned fence |
| `Device.submit(device, command, fence)` | Submit one executable command with an unsignaled same-device fence |
| `Fence.status(fence)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_NOT_READY` |
| `Fence.wait(fence, timeout_ns)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_TIMEOUT`, with a full U64 nanosecond timeout |
| `Fence.reset(fence)` | Reset an unassociated fence |
| `Device.destroy_fence(device, fence)` | Destroy an unassociated caller-owned fence |
| `CommandBuffer.reset(command)` | Reset a nonpending command and release recorded references after success |
| `Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)` | The same submission/completion core with a persistent private fence and infinite wait |
| `Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)` | Pool teardown and invalidation of its command buffers |

`Fence.wait`, `Device.submit_and_wait`, `Device.wait_idle`, and waits during scoped cleanup or shutdown run synchronously on the IO event loop.
These waits block other IO effects until they return. A finite `Fence.wait` timeout bounds that call's blocking.

`begin` records with `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. Commands have Initial, Recording, Executable, Pending, Uncertain, Completed, and Invalid states.
Only Initial commands can begin. Successful individual reset returns a command to Initial, including during recording.
Observed completion makes a one-time command Completed. Reset and re-record before submitting it again.
A failed driver reset makes the command Invalid and retains its references.
Pools enable `RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER`. Whole-pool reset and individual command free are absent.

A fill requires bound memory, `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, four-byte alignment, and a nonempty valid range.
Copies require bound buffers, source/destination transfer usages, and positive in-bounds ranges.
They reject overlapping destinations and physical source/destination overlap across every region, including distinct buffers sharing an allocation.
Byte copies impose no four-byte alignment rule.
Recorded references are deduplicated and survive completion and recording/reset failures.
Successful command reset or pool destruction releases them. Referenced buffers, images, and framebuffers cannot be destroyed before that release.

Barrier arguments and every new reference node are validated and allocated before recording.
Buffer barriers use `VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED` for both family indices. Ownership transfers are absent.
Stage/access validation accepts supported core Vulkan 1.0 bits. Optional geometry and tessellation features remain disabled.
`ALL_COMMANDS` excludes HOST. The fill caller records its transfer-to-host barrier explicitly.
The selected queue must support transfers. There is one selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command per device.

# bend-vulkan

A native Vulkan wrapper for Bend, inspired by [ash](https://github.com/ash-rs/ash).
The implementation provides explicit instance, device, buffer, image, memory, command-buffer, fence, render-pass, and framebuffer operations.
All Vulkan byte sizes, offsets, and alignments use the actual two-limb `U64` from [bend-collections](https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend-collections).

This is a 64-bit Linux, headless Vulkan 1.0 subset. It supports capability discovery, explicit barriers, packed array uploads, GPU transfers, fence-backed command reuse, and color/depth attachment clears.
Images use a six-format, optimal-tiled 2D profile with explicit mips, layers, binding, views, and staging readback.
Graphics pipelines, shaders, draws, descriptors, surfaces, swapchains, callbacks, and general `pNext` chains are not implemented.

## Run the buffer example

Use Linux with glibc 2.34 or newer. Install Bend **2.0.37**, Clang, Python 3, Vulkan development headers, `libvulkan.so.1`, and a Vulkan driver.
A hardware driver or a software ICD such as Lavapipe can provide the device.
The examples select a graphics queue for transfer commands.

Initialize the pinned dependency:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Build and run the native example:

```sh
mkdir -p build
bend examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend -o build/buffer-roundtrip
./build/buffer-roundtrip
```

Expected output:

```text
Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified
```

The example writes four bytes to Vulkan memory and checks their readback.
It then records `vkCmdFillBuffer`, submits the command buffer, waits for completion, and checks sixteen bytes against the value `42`.
Build and run `examples/discover.bend` the same way to list layers, extensions, devices, heaps, format masks, and selected limits.
It prints U64 values as low/high limbs.

## Run the image example

Build and run the offscreen example after initializing the dependency:

```sh
bend examples/offscreen_roundtrip.bend -o build/offscreen-roundtrip
./build/offscreen-roundtrip
```

Expected output:

```text
Optimal RGBA8 image clear and every-pixel readback verified
```

The example queries the exact image configuration and clears a 4 by 4 RGBA8 image to magenta.
It transitions the image, copies all 64 bytes to a host-readable buffer, waits for fence completion, and compares every pixel.
The bytes are row-major `R,G,B,A`, with `y=0` as the first row. The example defines that row as the top.
Optimal image memory has no public linear pixel stride. Readback uses a buffer with explicit copy strides.

`bend example.bend` uses Bend's JavaScript backend. Vulkan effects report a native-build-required error in that backend.

## Use the API

Import `Vulkan.bend`, `src/core.bend`, `src/constants.bend`, and the dependency's `src/math/u64.bend` with paths relative to your program.
The executable [buffer example](examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend) shows allocation and fill submission.
The [repeated transfer check](tests/repeated.bend) shows packed upload, explicit barriers, general submission, finite completion, and reset/re-recording.
The [rendering check](tests/rendering.bend) shows Vulkan 1.0 color/depth passes, partial-area clears, and framebuffer-only lifetime protection.
The [image reuse check](tests/image_repeated.bend) runs 32 changing color/depth passes and 32 resource churn cycles.

`V.Action(A)` is `IO(V.VkResult(A))`. A `do V.Action<Unit>:` block propagates returned failures.
`V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => run(entry))` loads the Vulkan library, runs your callback, and closes its resource tree after either `Done` or `Fail`.
Use `V.or_exit(Unit, result)` at the application boundary to report the final result.
Calling `IO.die`, `IO.exit`, or `IO.try` inside a resource scope bypasses that cleanup callback.

Handle values are copyable with Bend's `+` annotations. Each handle kind has a distinct type.
Native code validates registry keys, object kinds, ownership, and liveness before it calls Vulkan.
Explicit destroy operations reject live dependents. `Entry.close` releases descendants in dependency order.
Dropping a Bend handle value does not destroy its Vulkan object.

See [the API reference](docs/api.md) for supported operations and [the design](docs/design.md) for the FFI and ownership decisions.
The [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) marks milestones 0 through 2 complete. Indexed graphics is next.

## Verify changes

Run the generator check, proof gate, native examples, and negative integration checks:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py
```

To include address and undefined-behavior sanitizers:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize
```

The native checks include 32 alternating packed uploads copied through a device-local intermediate GPU buffer to literal readback bytes.
They reuse command/pool/fence objects, check stable row counts, and reject pending reset, destruction, mapping, and further submission before observing completion.
Separate checks cover fence status/wait/idle completion, retained references, stale/wrong-owner keys, and zero remaining objects after successful and accepted-pending failure scopes.
Native and interpreted probes read the returned upload array after success and rejection.
Image checks compare every color/depth pixel, nonuniform padded two-layer copies at a nonzero mip, and untouched pixels and buffer sentinels.
They cover RGBA/BGRA UNORM/SRGB channel order, D32 depth `0.5`, and D16 depth `1.0` readback.
Pass tests establish layouts in a separate completed and reset recording before submitting only framebuffer begin/end.

`tools/check_native.py` adds controlled dispatch/allocation probes only to emitted test C.
These exercise submit OOM/uncertainty, wait/idle/reset errors, map/flush failure ownership, metadata allocation failures, enumeration retries, composite ABI, private-fence isolation, and sticky device loss.
Injected results are distinct from real GPU execution. The tests never provoke hardware loss.
The sanitizer run includes those probes and the real repeated transfer test.
The emitted-test allocator counts all wrapper metadata allocations, and teardown asserts both zero metadata allocations and zero registry rows.
Driver-global leak detection is disabled for ASan. These explicit counters cover wrapper cleanup.
The verifier records queried device/layer output in `build/discovery.txt` and validation availability in `build/validation.txt`.
When Khronos validation is installed, it also runs the real GPU checks with synchronization validation enabled.
A missing driver or device fails native verification. It is not a passing skip.
Bend's pure laws live in `LAWS.bend`; their proofs live in `PROOF.bend`.
Before committing, run `bend PROOF.bend`. For the additional proof-kernel check, run `bend PROOF.bend --verdict`.
The laws cover pure functions. They do not verify C code, Vulkan drivers, or GPU execution.

`tools/bindings.json` defines the supported effects. `tools/generate.py` generates their Bend declarations, native registrations, JavaScript errors, and selected core constants from the checked-in Khronos registry extract.
Run `python3 tools/generate.py` after changing the manifest. The generator does not implement new native commands or translate arbitrary Vulkan structs.

The milestone-2 run on NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 passed `python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize`.
Khronos validation and synchronization validation were unavailable in that run.
Optimal color image requirements exposed no compatible host-visible memory type on that device.
Real lifetime rejection and pixels use the driver and staging. Post-completion mapped access in the graph probe uses controlled dispatch and is labeled separately.
Noncoherent cache paths have controlled flush-failure coverage. Their driver coverage depends on the selected memory type.

Zero bytes at an in-bounds offset is valid. Every outcome returns the unchanged array, including the interpreted backend's native-only error.
A flush failure can leave mapped destination bytes changed.
No Bend heap pointer survives the operation.

The wrapper checks common lifetime and memory-access errors. Callers remain responsible for Vulkan validity requirements for chosen flags, extensions, and resource use.
Handle keys are checked process-local identifiers. They provide no raw Vulkan handle interoperation or access-control guarantee.

## Images and views

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_image(device, info)` | An unbound `ImageHandle` |
| `Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device, image)` | `MemoryRequirements{size, alignment, memory_type_bits}` |
| `Device.bind_image_memory(device, image, memory, offset)` | An explicit requirements-checked binding |
| `Device.create_image_view(device, info)` | An `ImageView` retaining its image |
| `Device.destroy_image_view(device, view)` | View teardown, rejecting framebuffer dependents |
| `Device.destroy_image(device, image)` | Image teardown, rejecting views and recorded references |

`ImageHandle` avoids a name collision with Bend Base's `Image` type.
`ImageCreateInfo{format, extent, mip_levels, array_layers, usage}` creates an exclusive 2D optimal-tiled image.
Depth is one, samples are one, flags are zero, and initial layout is UNDEFINED.
Extent and mip/layer counts must be positive and fit the exact configuration limits and full mip chain.
Creation checks configuration support and required format features before native creation.
The returned memory requirements determine allocation size. Logical texel bytes do not describe an optimal image's footprint or memory layout.

The creation profile accepts these formats when the driver supports the requested configuration:

| Format | Value | Aspect | Raw texel bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` | 37 | COLOR | R, G, B, A |
| `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB` | 43 | COLOR | Encoded R, G, B, linear A |
| `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM` | 44 | COLOR | B, G, R, A |
| `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_SRGB` | 50 | COLOR | Encoded B, G, R, linear A |
| `VK_FORMAT_D16_UNORM` | 124 | DEPTH | Two little-endian UNORM bytes |
| `VK_FORMAT_D32_SFLOAT` | 126 | DEPTH | Four little-endian IEEE binary32 bytes |

Usages are a nonempty subset of TRANSFER_SRC, TRANSFER_DST, SAMPLED, COLOR_ATTACHMENT, and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT.
Color and depth attachment usages must match the format's role. Stencil, linear tiling, MSAA, compressed formats, sparse images, and format reinterpretation are absent.
SAMPLED usage permits resource preparation. Descriptors, samplers, and shader sampling commands are absent.

`ImageFormatInfo{format, image_type, tiling, usage, flags}` queries recognized core-1.0 configurations beyond the creation profile.
Invalid enum values return the wrapper argument error. A driver rejection preserves exact `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` bits, `4294967285`.
Failed query outputs are never decoded.
`ImageFormatProperties` contains `max_width`, `max_height`, `max_depth`, `max_mip_levels`, `max_array_layers`, `sample_counts`, and `max_resource_size: W.U64`.
Generic format masks alone do not establish support for a configuration.

`ImageSubresourceRange{aspect_mask, base_mip_level, level_count, base_array_layer, layer_count}` requires explicit positive counts and the format's exact aspect.
`ImageViewCreateInfo{image, view_type, range}` requires binding and at least one view-eligible usage, SAMPLED or an attachment usage.
Views use the image's format and identity component mapping. A 2D view selects one layer. A 2D_ARRAY view may select multiple layers.

Buffer and image bindings share requirements-sized bounds, alignment, type, and owner checks.
Buffer-buffer aliasing remains available. Binding intervals must not overlap when either resource is an image.
Mixed buffer/optimal-image intervals must also occupy disjoint `buffer_image_granularity` pages, in either bind order.
Distinct images may share an allocation at disjoint requirements intervals. Allocation-wide host exclusion still applies.

## Image commands and readback

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command, image, layout, value, ranges)` | Float color clear over explicit ranges |
| `CommandBuffer.clear_depth_image(command, image, layout, depth, ranges)` | Depth clear over explicit ranges |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer_to_image(command, src, dst, layout, regions)` | Raw buffer upload |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command, src, layout, dst, regions)` | Raw staging readback |

Image commands require bound, same-device resources and Recording Outside scope.
Clears and uploads require TRANSFER_DST usage and TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL or GENERAL layout.
Readback requires TRANSFER_SRC usage and TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL or GENERAL layout.
Color clear requires a graphics or compute queue. Depth clears and depth copies require graphics.
Color copies accept graphics, compute, or transfer queues and enforce the selected family's actual `minImageTransferGranularity`.
Zero granularity requires a whole mip. Nonzero granularity permits the Vulkan edge exception.
Range and copy lists are nonempty and bounded to 4096. Overlapping clear ranges are rejected.

`ClearColor{r, g, b, a}` takes finite F32 values. Vulkan converts them to the destination format, including sRGB encoding of RGB.
Copies preserve stored bytes and perform no color conversion, swizzle, vertical flip, or alpha transformation.
Depth clears require finite values in `[0,1]`. Uploaded depth values must also be in `[0,1]`, as a caller obligation.
The wrapper does not inspect GPU buffer contents to validate uploaded depth values.

`BufferImageCopy{buffer_offset, buffer_row_length, buffer_image_height, image_subresource, image_offset, image_extent}` uses a W.U64 byte offset into the buffer.
The offset is relative to the buffer, independently of its memory binding offset.
`buffer_row_length` and `buffer_image_height` are texel counts. Zero means the copied width or height.
Positive values must cover those dimensions. `ImageSubresourceLayers{aspect_mask, mip_level, base_array_layer, layer_count}` selects one mip and positive layer count.
Offsets are nonnegative and signed-representable. Extents must be positive, signed-representable, and fit the selected mip.
Buffer offsets are four-byte aligned, including D16. Row byte lengths cannot exceed `INT32_MAX`.

For normalized row length R, image height H, bytes per texel B, width w, height h, layers L, and buffer offset O:

```text
row_stride   = R * B
layer_stride = H * row_stride
end          = O + (L - 1) * layer_stride + (h - 1) * row_stride + w * B
```

All arithmetic is checked U64. The final row has no required trailing padding.
The interval must fit the buffer's logical size and its bound allocation.
Uploads reject overlapping destination image boxes. Downloads reject overlapping destination buffer envelopes, including their internal padding.
Repeated source reads are allowed. Logical dimensions and strides determine the result, independently of Bend array capacity.
Texels increase in x, then y, then layer order. The example defines the first row, `y=0`, as the top.
This convention specifies exported bytes. Viewport conventions for future draws are outside this API.

Layouts and initialized contents are caller assertions at execution time.
The wrapper stores no layout cache and inserts no implicit image or host barriers.
Use `ImageMemoryBarrier{image, range, old_layout, new_layout, src_access, dst_access}` in the sole `pipeline_barrier` operation.
The wrapper checks usage, aspect, range, layout enum, and queue stage/access compatibility.
Both queue-family indices are IGNORED. Overlapping image ranges within one barrier call are rejected.
UNDEFINED is an old discard layout only and requires zero source access by wrapper policy.
After unexpected submission errors, observe idle recovery and deliberately overwrite, discard, or recreate before relying on contents.

## Render passes and framebuffers

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_render_pass(device, info)` | A Vulkan 1.0 single-subpass `RenderPass` |
| `Device.create_framebuffer(device, info)` | A one-layer `Framebuffer` retaining its pass and ordered views |
| `Device.destroy_framebuffer(device, framebuffer)` | Teardown, rejecting recorded command references |
| `Device.destroy_render_pass(device, pass)` | Teardown, rejecting framebuffers |
| `CommandBuffer.begin_render_pass(command, framebuffer, area, clears)` | Enter Recording Inside scope |
| `CommandBuffer.end_render_pass(command)` | Return to Recording Outside scope |

`RenderPassCreateInfo{colors, depth}` contains ordered `AttachmentInfo{format, load_op, store_op}` values and an optional depth attachment.
At least one attachment is required. Color count is limited by `max_color_attachments` and the wrapper's 4095-color cap.
LOAD, CLEAR, DONT_CARE and STORE, DONT_CARE operations are supported.
Attachments are single-sample. Stencil operations are DONT_CARE. The queue must support graphics.
Initial, subpass, and final layouts are all COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL or DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL for the corresponding role.
There are no explicit subpass dependencies. Supply outside barriers for transfers and attachment reads/writes, including LOAD of a prior pass's output.

`FramebufferCreateInfo{render_pass, attachments, extent}` requires same-device, ordered, format-matching 2D views.
Each view selects exactly one mip and one layer, has the required attachment usage, and covers the framebuffer extent.
Attachment subresources cannot overlap. Begin derives the exact pass identity from the framebuffer.
`RenderArea{offset, extent}` has nonnegative offsets and positive extents, all signed-representable and within the framebuffer.

The clear list has one entry per attachment, including placeholders.
CLEAR slots require `ColorClear{ClearColor{...}}` or `DepthClear{depth}` according to role.
Other slots require `UnusedClear{}`. Float constraints match image clears.
Clears cover the render area. Preserved pixels outside that area require prior initialization and correct synchronization.
Nested begin, unmatched end, and command end Inside reject before dispatch.
All fills, copies, image clears, and barriers reject Inside. Successful reset may discard an open recording.
This milestone executes begin/end and attachment clears. Pipelines, shaders, and draws are absent.

## Command submission

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Device.create_command_pool(device)` | A pool for the device's selected queue family |
| `Device.allocate_command_buffer(device, pool)` | One primary command buffer |
| `CommandBuffer.begin(command)` | Begin one-time recording |
| `CommandBuffer.fill_buffer(command, buffer, offset, size, data)` | Record a transfer fill |
| `CommandBuffer.copy_buffer(command, src, dst, regions)` | Record nonempty byte ranges from `List<BufferCopy>` |
| `CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command, src_stage, dst_stage, memory, buffers, images)` | Record explicit memory, buffer and image barriers |
| `CommandBuffer.end(command)` | End recording |
| `Device.create_fence(device, signaled)` | A caller-owned fence |
| `Device.submit(device, command, fence)` | Submit one executable command with an unsignaled same-device fence |
| `Fence.status(fence)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_NOT_READY` |
| `Fence.wait(fence, timeout_ns)` | U32 `VK_SUCCESS` or `VK_TIMEOUT`, with a full U64 nanosecond timeout |
| `Fence.reset(fence)` | Reset an unassociated fence |
| `Device.destroy_fence(device, fence)` | Destroy an unassociated caller-owned fence |
| `CommandBuffer.reset(command)` | Reset a nonpending command and release recorded references after success |
| `Device.submit_and_wait(device, command)` | The same submission/completion core with a persistent private fence and infinite wait |
| `Device.destroy_command_pool(device, pool)` | Pool teardown and invalidation of its command buffers |

`Fence.wait`, `Device.submit_and_wait`, `Device.wait_idle`, and waits during scoped cleanup or shutdown run synchronously on the IO event loop.
These waits block other IO effects until they return. A finite `Fence.wait` timeout bounds that call's blocking.

`begin` records with `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. Commands have Initial, Recording, Executable, Pending, Uncertain, Completed, and Invalid states.
Only Initial commands can begin. Successful individual reset returns a command to Initial, including during recording.
Observed completion makes a one-time command Completed. Reset and re-record before submitting it again.
A failed driver reset makes the command Invalid and retains its references.
Pools enable `RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER`. Whole-pool reset and individual command free are absent.

A fill requires bound memory, `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, four-byte alignment, and a nonempty valid range.
Copies require bound buffers, source/destination transfer usages, and positive in-bounds ranges.
They reject overlapping destinations and physical source/destination overlap across every region, including distinct buffers sharing an allocation.
Byte copies impose no four-byte alignment rule.
Recorded references are deduplicated and survive completion and recording/reset failures.
Successful command reset or pool destruction releases them. Referenced buffers, images, and framebuffers cannot be destroyed before that release.

Barrier arguments and every new reference node are validated and allocated before recording.
Buffer barriers use `VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED` for both family indices. Ownership transfers are absent.
Stage/access validation accepts supported core Vulkan 1.0 bits. Optional geometry and tessellation features remain disabled.
`ALL_COMMANDS` excludes HOST. The fill caller records its transfer-to-host barrier explicitly.
The selected queue must support transfers. There is one selected queue and at most one Pending or Uncertain command per device.
"}

A native Vulkan wrapper for Bend, inspired by [ash](https://github.com/ash-rs/ash).
The implementation provides explicit instance, device, buffer, image, memory, command-buffer, fence, render-pass, and framebuffer operations.
All Vulkan byte sizes, offsets, and alignments use the actual two-limb `U64` from [bend-collections](https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend-collections).

This is a 64-bit Linux, headless Vulkan 1.0 subset. It supports capability discovery, explicit barriers, packed array uploads, GPU transfers, fence-backed command reuse, and color/depth attachment clears.
Images use a six-format, optimal-tiled 2D profile with explicit mips, layers, binding, views, and staging readback.
Graphics pipelines, shaders, draws, descriptors, surfaces, swapchains, callbacks, and general `pNext` chains are not implemented.

## Run the buffer example

Use Linux with glibc 2.34 or newer. Install Bend **2.0.37**, Clang, Python 3, Vulkan development headers, `libvulkan.so.1`, and a Vulkan driver.
A hardware driver or a software ICD such as Lavapipe can provide the device.
The examples select a graphics queue for transfer commands.

Initialize the pinned dependency:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Build and run the native example:

```sh
mkdir -p build
bend examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend -o build/buffer-roundtrip
./build/buffer-roundtrip
```

Expected output:

```text
Host roundtrip and GPU buffer fill verified
```

The example writes four bytes to Vulkan memory and checks their readback.
It then records `vkCmdFillBuffer`, submits the command buffer, waits for completion, and checks sixteen bytes against the value `42`.
Build and run `examples/discover.bend` the same way to list layers, extensions, devices, heaps, format masks, and selected limits.
It prints U64 values as low/high limbs.

## Run the image example

Build and run the offscreen example after initializing the dependency:

```sh
bend examples/offscreen_roundtrip.bend -o build/offscreen-roundtrip
./build/offscreen-roundtrip
```

Expected output:

```text
Optimal RGBA8 image clear and every-pixel readback verified
```

The example queries the exact image configuration and clears a 4 by 4 RGBA8 image to magenta.
It transitions the image, copies all 64 bytes to a host-readable buffer, waits for fence completion, and compares every pixel.
The bytes are row-major `R,G,B,A`, with `y=0` as the first row. The example defines that row as the top.
Optimal image memory has no public linear pixel stride. Readback uses a buffer with explicit copy strides.

`bend example.bend` uses Bend's JavaScript backend. Vulkan effects report a native-build-required error in that backend.

## Use the API

Import `Vulkan.bend`, `src/core.bend`, `src/constants.bend`, and the dependency's `src/math/u64.bend` with paths relative to your program.
The executable [buffer example](examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend) shows allocation and fill submission.
The [repeated transfer check](tests/repeated.bend) shows packed upload, explicit barriers, general submission, finite completion, and reset/re-recording.
The [rendering check](tests/rendering.bend) shows Vulkan 1.0 color/depth passes, partial-area clears, and framebuffer-only lifetime protection.
The [image reuse check](tests/image_repeated.bend) runs 32 changing color/depth passes and 32 resource churn cycles.

`V.Action(A)` is `IO(V.VkResult(A))`. A `do V.Action<Unit>:` block propagates returned failures.
`V.Entry.with(Unit, entry => run(entry))` loads the Vulkan library, runs your callback, and closes its resource tree after either `Done` or `Fail`.
Use `V.or_exit(Unit, result)` at the application boundary to report the final result.
Calling `IO.die`, `IO.exit`, or `IO.try` inside a resource scope bypasses that cleanup callback.

Handle values are copyable with Bend's `+` annotations. Each handle kind has a distinct type.
Native code validates registry keys, object kinds, ownership, and liveness before it calls Vulkan.
Explicit destroy operations reject live dependents. `Entry.close` releases descendants in dependency order.
Dropping a Bend handle value does not destroy its Vulkan object.

See [the API reference](docs/api.md) for supported operations and [the design](docs/design.md) for the FFI and ownership decisions.
The [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) marks milestones 0 through 2 complete. Indexed graphics is next.

## Verify changes

Run the generator check, proof gate, native examples, and negative integration checks:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py
```

To include address and undefined-behavior sanitizers:

```sh
python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize
```

The native checks include 32 alternating packed uploads copied through a device-local intermediate GPU buffer to literal readback bytes.
They reuse command/pool/fence objects, check stable row counts, and reject pending reset, destruction, mapping, and further submission before observing completion.
Separate checks cover fence status/wait/idle completion, retained references, stale/wrong-owner keys, and zero remaining objects after successful and accepted-pending failure scopes.
Native and interpreted probes read the returned upload array after success and rejection.
Image checks compare every color/depth pixel, nonuniform padded two-layer copies at a nonzero mip, and untouched pixels and buffer sentinels.
They cover RGBA/BGRA UNORM/SRGB channel order, D32 depth `0.5`, and D16 depth `1.0` readback.
Pass tests establish layouts in a separate completed and reset recording before submitting only framebuffer begin/end.

`tools/check_native.py` adds controlled dispatch/allocation probes only to emitted test C.
These exercise submit OOM/uncertainty, wait/idle/reset errors, map/flush failure ownership, metadata allocation failures, enumeration retries, composite ABI, private-fence isolation, and sticky device loss.
Injected results are distinct from real GPU execution. The tests never provoke hardware loss.
The sanitizer run includes those probes and the real repeated transfer test.
The emitted-test allocator counts all wrapper metadata allocations, and teardown asserts both zero metadata allocations and zero registry rows.
Driver-global leak detection is disabled for ASan. These explicit counters cover wrapper cleanup.
The verifier records queried device/layer output in `build/discovery.txt` and validation availability in `build/validation.txt`.
When Khronos validation is installed, it also runs the real GPU checks with synchronization validation enabled.
A missing driver or device fails native verification. It is not a passing skip.
Bend's pure laws live in `LAWS.bend`; their proofs live in `PROOF.bend`.
Before committing, run `bend PROOF.bend`. For the additional proof-kernel check, run `bend PROOF.bend --verdict`.
The laws cover pure functions. They do not verify C code, Vulkan drivers, or GPU execution.

`tools/bindings.json` defines the supported effects. `tools/generate.py` generates their Bend declarations, native registrations, JavaScript errors, and selected core constants from the checked-in Khronos registry extract.
Run `python3 tools/generate.py` after changing the manifest. The generator does not implement new native commands or translate arbitrary Vulkan structs.

The milestone-2 run on NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 passed `python3 tools/verify.py --sanitize`.
Khronos validation and synchronization validation were unavailable in that run.
Optimal color image requirements exposed no compatible host-visible memory type on that device.
Real lifetime rejection and pixels use the driver and staging. Post-completion mapped access in the graph probe uses controlled dispatch and is labeled separately.
Noncoherent cache paths have controlled flush-failure coverage. Their driver coverage depends on the selected memory type.

import Base
import ../Vulkan.bend as V
import ../src/core.bend as Core
import ../src/constants.bend as vk
import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
import ./buffer_roundtrip.bend as Demo

def allocate(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, device: V.Device, requirements: V.MemoryRequirements, required: U32) -> V.Action(V.DeviceMemory):
  V.MemoryRequirements{size,alignment,bits} = requirements
  do V.Action<V.DeviceMemory>:
    types : List<Core.MemoryType> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_memory_properties(instance,physical)
    index : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_memory_type(types,bits,required),"No compatible memory type")
    V.Device.allocate_memory(device,size,index)

def expected(count: Nat) -> List<U32>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      []
    case 1n+rest:
      255 <> 0 <> 255 <> 255 <> expected(rest)

def clear(+instance: V.Instance, +physical: V.PhysicalDevice, +device: V.Device) -> V.Action(Unit):
  +range : V.ImageSubresourceRange = V.ImageSubresourceRange{1,0,1,0,1}
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    supported : V.ImageFormatProperties <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_image_format_properties(instance,physical,V.ImageFormatInfo{37,1,0,3,0})
    +image : V.ImageHandle <- V.Device.create_image(device,V.ImageCreateInfo{37,V.Extent2D{4,4},1,1,3})
    requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_image_memory_requirements(device,image)
    +image_memory : V.DeviceMemory <- allocate(instance,physical,device,requirements,0)
    V.Device.bind_image_memory(device,image,image_memory,W.zero())
    +buffer : V.Buffer <- V.Device.create_buffer(device,V.BufferCreateInfo{W.of_u32(64),2})
    buffer_requirements : V.MemoryRequirements <- V.Device.get_buffer_memory_requirements(device,buffer)
    +readback : V.DeviceMemory <- allocate(instance,physical,device,buffer_requirements,2)
    V.Device.bind_buffer_memory(device,buffer,readback,W.zero())
    +pool : V.CommandPool <- V.Device.create_command_pool(device)
    +command : V.CommandBuffer <- V.Device.allocate_command_buffer(device,pool)
    +fence : V.Fence <- V.Device.create_fence(device,False{})
    V.CommandBuffer.begin(command)
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT(),vk.VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT(),[],[],
      [V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED(),vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),0,vk.VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT()}])
    V.CommandBuffer.clear_color_image(command,image,vk.VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL(),V.ClearColor{1.0,0.0,1.0,1.0},[range])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,4096,[],[],[V.ImageMemoryBarrier{image,range,7,6,4096,2048}])
    V.CommandBuffer.copy_image_to_buffer(command,image,6,buffer,[V.BufferImageCopy{W.zero(),0,0,V.ImageSubresourceLayers{1,0,0,1},V.Offset2D{0,0},V.Extent2D{4,4}}])
    V.CommandBuffer.pipeline_barrier(command,4096,16384,[V.MemoryBarrier{4096,8192}],[],[])
    V.CommandBuffer.end(command)
    V.Device.submit(device,command,fence)
    status : U32 <- V.Fence.wait(fence,Core.whole_size())
    Demo.require(U32.is_eq(status,0),"Image fence did not complete")
    bytes : List<U32> <- V.Device.read_memory(device,readback,W.zero(),64)
    Demo.require(Demo.bytes_equal(bytes,expected(16n)),"Every RGBA8 pixel must be magenta")
    V.CommandBuffer.reset(command)
    V.Device.destroy_fence(device,fence)
    V.Device.destroy_command_pool(device,pool)
    V.Device.destroy_image(device,image)
    V.Device.destroy_buffer(device,buffer)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,image_memory)
    V.Device.free_memory(device,readback)
    V.Device.destroy(device)
    V.Instance.destroy(instance)
    return Unit{}

def run(+entry: V.Entry) -> V.Action(Unit):
  do V.Action<Unit>:
    +instance : V.Instance <- V.Entry.create_instance(entry,V.InstanceCreateInfo.default())
    devices : List<V.PhysicalDevice> <- V.Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance)
    +physical : V.PhysicalDevice <- Demo.first(devices)
    families : List<(U32 & U32)> <- V.Instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(instance,physical)
    family : U32 <- Demo.choose(Core.find_queue_family(families,1),"No graphics queue")
    +device : V.Device <- V.Instance.create_device(instance,physical,V.DeviceCreateInfo{family,[]})
    clear(instance,physical,device)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : V.VkResult(Unit) <- V.Entry.with(Unit,entry => run(entry))
    V.or_exit(Unit,result)
    live : V.VkResult(U32) <- V.debug_live_objects()
    count : U32 <- V.or_exit(U32,live)
    checked : V.VkResult(Unit) <- Demo.require(U32.is_eq(count,0),"Offscreen example leaked")
    V.or_exit(Unit,checked)
    IO.print("Optimal RGBA8 image clear and every-pixel readback verified")

## T3 Code orchestration

The `t3-code` MCP server provides app-owned orchestration. Treat these concepts distinctly:

- A delegated task/subagent is child work owned by the current thread. Retain each returned `taskId`, and use `task_status` or `task_cancel` to manage it. The returned `childThreadId` is backing storage for the subagent, not the target for starting another delegated review round.
- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` create ordinary top-level T3 conversations. Use them only when the user explicitly asks for separate/new/top-level threads or conversations. Never use them merely because the user said "subagent" or requested parallel delegated work.
- For every T3 delegated review round, call `delegate_task` again. Include the original brief, prior findings, responses, and unresolved objections in each new task prompt. Track each round by its own `taskId`. Use a distinct `clientRequestId` per round, stable across retries of that round. Do not use `t3_thread_send` on `childThreadId` to continue a delegated review.
- `schedule_task` creates persistent recurring work in the app scheduler. Milestone 2 is complete on `feat/offscreen-images` at `fc52f9b`. Six ordered local commits; working tree clean.

Implemented images, memory binding, views, explicit barriers, uploads/readback, color/depth clears, Vulkan 1.0 render passes/framebuffers, and dependency-safe cleanup. See the [roadmap](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/docs/roadmap.md:75) and [runnable example](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan-milestone1/examples/offscreen_roundtrip.bend).

Reviewed [Voltra’s readback implementation](https://github.com/amage-si/voltra/blob/8900b07e14b80d3528a3b38cb5b376774441d240/gpu.bend) before design.

| Design | Decision |
|---|---|
| Direct dependencies, explicit layouts | Chosen for one lifetime model |
| Layout ledger | Deferred to avoid added state |
| Flattened command references | Rejected to avoid duplicated dependencies |

Model the Domain and Boundary Discipline shaped the checked dependency graph. Laziness Protocol kept layouts caller-owned. Separate Before Serializing Shared State kept designs isolated and implementation with one owner. Sequence Work into Verifiable Units produced checked commits; Prove It Works required independent GPU execution.

The throughput checkpoint was followed: baseline and ABI checks first, independent designs in parallel, one IO registry writer, and one owner for coupled implementation.

Independent verification passed on GTX 1660: full sanitizer suite, proofs, generator freshness, six formats, exact color/depth pixels, padded mip/layer transfers, 32 reuse cycles, and 32 resource-churn cycles. [Verification log](/tmp/bend-vulkan-m2/parent-verification.log).

No open implementation decisions. No PR was created because no remote exists.

**Attention**
